sharjah/muwaileh.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are grouped by the work Muwaileh families actually buy: internal assessment supervision in Diploma subjects, and paper technique for Cambridge and Pearson candidates in Years 10 and 11. Each teaches one board and one level rather than claiming the whole range.

intro.heading: Why a good school is not the whole course
paragraphs: Muwaileh holds more international school capacity than any other district in Sharjah. Families move here deliberately for it, and the schools are generally well staffed and properly run. That is why the tutoring question in this neighbourhood is different from the one in the older coastal districts: parents here are rarely trying to compensate for poor teaching. They are discovering that good teaching covers less of the course than they assumed.

Work out the arithmetic. A Cambridge IGCSE subject gets perhaps four or five lessons a fortnight across two years. In that time a teacher has to deliver a syllabus, run practicals, set and mark assessments for a class of twenty or more, and prepare a cohort for papers written in a language of command verbs. What that timetable cannot contain is a student sitting a whole past paper under timed conditions every week for eight weeks and having each one marked individually with feedback by question type.

In the Diploma the gap is wider and more consequential, because a fifth of each subject grade comes from internally assessed work the student produces largely outside lessons. A teacher supervising thirty internal assessments can give a research question a few minutes of attention. A badly chosen research question costs marks in every criterion and cannot be rescued once the data is collected, and that is the single most common Diploma failure in this district.

There is a third, quieter gap: revision as a technique. Almost nobody is taught how to revise. Students reread notes, feel productive, and score the same mark again. Spaced retrieval, working from the mark scheme backwards, and writing answers under time pressure are learnable skills, and they belong to neither the school's timetable nor a parent's expertise.

None of this is a criticism of the schools in this district, and a page that implied otherwise would be dishonest as well as unhelpful. A teacher with a class of twenty-four and a two-year syllabus is doing the job the timetable allows. The gap is structural: it exists in Muwaileh, in Dubai, in London and in Singapore, and it is why tutoring in a well-schooled district is a supplement to good teaching rather than a substitute for bad teaching.

IB Gram addresses those three gaps with one-to-one lessons over live video. IB Gram does not visit homes in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service run only in India. For Muwaileh that matters less for traffic than for match quality: the point of a tutor here is not another lesson on the same content, it is a specialist in the exact board, level and component where the independent work is going wrong, and that specialist does not have to live down the road.

sharjah/muwaileh.programmesIntro: Three programmes dominate enquiries from Muwaileh addresses. Each entry below names the part of the course that happens outside the classroom, because that is what tutoring in this district is actually for.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three normally at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an internally assessed component contributing roughly a fifth of the grade, marked by the teacher against published criteria and externally moderated. Core components can add up to three points and can also prevent a diploma being awarded.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students in Muwaileh have good classroom provision and almost no supervised time for internal assessment drafting. The work is produced at home across months with a handful of supervisor meetings, which is why the sessions that change a Diploma grade in this district are the early ones on question design rather than the late ones on content.

programmes.name: Cambridge International IGCSE
programmes.description: Assessed by syllabus code, with Core and Extended tiers in sciences and maths that cap the attainable grade. Cambridge runs June and November series for IGCSE, O Level and International A Level. Each centre is allocated to one of six administrative timetable zones, and the school's own zone timetable is the one that applies.
programmes.countryNote: Tier is the decision Muwaileh parents hear about last and should hear about first. A Core entry caps the grade regardless of how well the candidate performs, and the entry closes months before the papers. For the March 2027 series, Cambridge sets final entries on 27 November 2026 with the exam period from 3 February to 4 March 2027.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Graded 9 to 1, available in May or June and in November, with formula provision and paper structures that differ from the Cambridge equivalent in the same subject. Some qualifications are modular, which changes when revision has to peak and when a resit is possible.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson published a November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, and released June 2026 results to centres on 19 August and to students on 20 August 2026. Provisional timetables are revised, so a Muwaileh family should work from the live PDF on qualifications.pearson.com rather than any date copied onto a tutoring page.

sharjah/muwaileh.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects requested most often from Muwaileh, described by the component where independent work decides the grade. Availability depends on board and level rather than on location, because lessons are delivered over video.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The internal exploration is marked against five criteria worth twenty marks in total, and most lost marks sit in reflection and personal engagement rather than in the mathematics itself. Higher Level Paper 3 needs extended unseen problem solving that no class drill reproduces.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Calculator-permitted throughout, which hides the real demand: interpreting a result in the context of the situation modelled. A correct number with no statement of what it means for the scenario earns little, and that habit is corrected in practice rather than in lessons.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The scientific investigation is assessed on four criteria worth twenty-four marks, and a research question that cannot generate a usable spread of data sinks all four. Energetics and organic mechanisms carry the Higher Level teaching load.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields and circular motion defeat capable students because algebra and physical reasoning must run together. Paper 1 rewards recognising which relationship applies, which is a pattern-matching skill built through volume of practice.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A long syllabus where marks are lost to imprecise language rather than ignorance. The investigation criteria reward a controlled design and an honest evaluation of limitations, both of which are planning skills rather than content knowledge.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a portfolio of three commentaries based on published news articles, each with its own word limit and each requiring diagrams drawn correctly. Candidates lose marks for articles chosen badly and for evaluation that lists rather than judges.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Extended candidates meet functions, transformations and histograms with unequal class widths; Core candidates never see them. The tier decision sets the ceiling, and once entries close in the autumn it cannot be undone.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: The alternative-to-practical paper is the biggest source of avoidable loss: candidates describe a method without naming a control variable or justifying a repeat reading. That is a question-type skill, not a topic.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis and the qualitative analysis tables carry the Extended difficulty. Learning the analysis tables as tables, rather than reasoning them out under time pressure, is worth several marks.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Mathematics 4MA1
subjects.description: Two papers with a formula sheet supplied, which changes what must be memorised and how time is allocated. Candidates trained only on Cambridge papers lose minutes adjusting to question order and method marks.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together worth up to three points, each with its own word limit and internal deadlines set by the school. Support is question framing, criteria explanation and feedback on the student's own drafts; supplied prose is a malpractice risk, not a shortcut.

sharjah/muwaileh.regionsIntro: Muwaileh sits inland on the spine of the emirate, surrounded by the districts its schools draw from. Each note describes the practical relationship with Muwaileh rather than the area on its own.

regions.name: University City
regions.note: Immediately east, where Sharjah's higher education campuses sit. Several Muwaileh schools draw staff from there, and families with an older sibling at university often want one tutor who can cover two very different levels in a week.

regions.name: Al Zahia
regions.note: North-west and newer, mostly villas and townhouses. Children from Al Zahia fill several Muwaileh classrooms, which is why the two areas share mock calendars and internal assessment deadlines almost exactly.

regions.name: Aljada
regions.note: West towards central Sharjah, a large newer community whose school-age population is growing quickly. Journeys into Muwaileh schools are short, so Aljada children are available for an earlier evening session than coastal families.

regions.name: Al Khan and Al Majaz
regions.note: Thirty minutes west on the coast. Children travelling from there to a Muwaileh school lose an hour of the day to the road and cannot take a weekday slot before 6:30pm.

regions.name: Muwaileh Commercial
regions.note: The denser apartment part of the district, closest to the schools themselves. The short walk or drive means homework starts earlier here, which makes an early evening session genuinely workable.

regions.name: Sharjah Garden City
regions.note: South-east along the Al Dhaid road, villa-based and newer. Families there use Muwaileh schools heavily and face the longest commute of any group in this cluster.

regions.name: Tilal City
regions.note: Further out towards the interior. A Muwaileh school day plus a Tilal City commute makes Saturday morning the only realistic slot for long-form work.

sections.heading: What class time covers, and what it hands back to the student
paragraphs: Start with an honest division of labour. A well-run Muwaileh school delivers content, demonstrates method, runs practicals, sets periodic assessments and gives whole-class feedback. That is a substantial amount, and it is not the whole course. The remainder is produced by the student outside the classroom, and the quality of that remainder is what separates a 5 from a 7.

The components that sit mostly outside class time are predictable. Timed practice on whole papers, with individual marking, is first. Internal assessment drafting is second, and in the Diploma it is the one with a fixed weighting attached. Independent revision across a two-year syllabus is third. Learning the vocabulary of command verbs is fourth, and it is almost never taught as a topic in its own right because it belongs to no topic.

A parent can test this quickly. Ask your child how many complete past papers they have sat under timed conditions this term, and how many of those were marked individually with feedback by question. The answer in most schools, in any country, is fewer than the parent assumed, and it is not a criticism of the teacher. A class of twenty-four papers marked individually every week is not a thing a timetable contains.

That test also tells you what to buy. If the answer is zero papers, the first purchase is not more teaching. It is a marked timed-paper cycle, because the content is probably already in place and the marks are being lost in the room. The table sets out the division component by component.

sections.heading: The tier decision that sets the ceiling before Year 11 begins
paragraphs: In Cambridge sciences and maths, candidates are entered for Core or Extended, and the tier caps the attainable grade. It is a decision made by the school, usually during Year 10, often on the basis of a single set of results, and it is the one Muwaileh parents most often learn about after it has already been taken.

The content difference is real rather than cosmetic. Extended maths candidates meet functions, transformations and histograms with unequal class widths. Extended science candidates meet additional topics and are examined on papers with a higher difficulty profile. A Core candidate who performs perfectly is still awarded within the Core grade range, which may not satisfy a sixth-form entry requirement two years later.

The timing is the part that catches families. Cambridge sets final entries months before the papers are sat: for the March 2027 series, final entries fall on 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. Once that entry is made the tier is fixed for that series. A conversation in October about moving a child up is a conversation worth having; the same conversation in January is mostly theoretical.

What tutoring can usefully do is provide evidence. A candidate sitting Extended past papers under timed conditions, marked honestly, produces a mark that a head of department can act on. That is a more persuasive case than a parent's conviction, and it is the right use of two or three early sessions in Year 10.

sections.heading: Internal assessment: where class time runs out entirely
paragraphs: This is the component that explains most of the gap between a Muwaileh student's predicted grade and their final one. It is produced outside lessons, it carries a fixed weighting, and it is marked against published criteria that most students never read properly.

The mark allocations are worth knowing as numbers rather than as a general idea. The Diploma maths exploration is assessed against five criteria totalling twenty marks: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics, with the last carrying the largest share. The scientific investigation in biology, chemistry and physics is assessed against four criteria totalling twenty-four marks: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. Economics runs a portfolio of three commentaries based on published articles. Confirm every figure against the current subject guide with your school's Diploma coordinator before planning around it.

Seeing the criteria as a mark split changes behaviour. A student who knows that reflection and personal engagement carry marks stops treating them as decoration. A student who knows that evaluation is a sixth of a science investigation writes the limitations section properly instead of in the last hour. None of this is content knowledge; it is reading the assessment instrument, and it takes one session.

The failure mode is always the same and always early. A research question is chosen in the first weeks, the student collects data for a month, and the data turns out to have no usable spread or no controllable variable. By then the deadline is close and the only option is writing up a weak investigation well. Two sessions on question design before data collection are worth ten sessions of rescue afterwards.

sections.heading: Word limits, deadlines and the documents that carry them
paragraphs: The written components of a Diploma each carry a limit, and every year candidates in every country lose marks by treating a limit as a target to exceed. Collecting the limits in one place is useful because no competing page in this market does it, and because the internal deadlines that matter most are set by the school rather than by the awarding body.

The Extended Essay is normally capped at four thousand words. The Theory of Knowledge essay and the exhibition commentary each carry their own shorter limits. Internal assessments in the sciences and mathematics carry page or word guidance rather than hard ceilings in some subjects and firm limits in others, and the economics portfolio limits each commentary individually. Every one of these should be confirmed against the current subject guide through the school, because the IB revises them and a figure copied from an old page is worse than no figure.

The deadline structure matters as much as the limit. A school sets internal dates for a first draft, a supervisor meeting, a final submission and an upload, and those dates sit months before anything external. A tutoring plan built from the awarding body's calendar will always be late; one built from the school's assessment calendar will not.

Practical consequence for a Muwaileh family: ask the school for the written internal deadline schedule at the start of the Diploma year, not in the term it bites. It is the single most useful document in the house, and tutoring sessions should be positioned relative to it rather than relative to the exam.

sections.heading: The past-paper cycle, and why volume alone does nothing
paragraphs: Every family in Muwaileh has heard that past papers are the answer, and most buy the wrong version of it. Working through papers without marking them against the scheme produces confidence and no improvement, because the student grades their own answer generously on the parts they half-knew.

A cycle that works has four steps. The paper is sat to time, unaided, in one sitting. It is marked against the official mark scheme, strictly, with the marks shown. The errors are then grouped by question type and command verb rather than by topic, which usually reveals that a student losing twelve marks across a paper lost nine of them on one kind of question. Only then is anything re-taught, and only the topics the errors actually expose.

That fourth step is the one families skip and the one that saves time. A student who loses marks on every explain question does not need the whole syllabus retaught; they need to be shown that an explain answer requires a mechanism and a consequence, and then made to write six of them. The repair is narrow and fast once the diagnosis is honest.

Volume matters after that, not before. Once the technique is in place, a weekly timed paper for eight weeks before a series is the highest-value thing a candidate can do, and it is almost impossible to arrange without someone to mark it. Doing one paper properly is worth more than doing four and checking the answers.

sections.heading: What to buy first, and what it costs around Muwaileh
paragraphs: Because the problem in this district is usually independent work rather than teaching, the spending order is different from the one families assume. The cheapest effective purchase is early and narrow; the expensive ineffective purchase is late and broad.

First on the list is internal assessment supervision in a Diploma subject, bought in the first term of the course. Three or four sessions on question design and criteria interpretation protect a fifth of the grade and cost a fraction of a year of weekly lessons. Second is a marked past-paper cycle in the weakest examined subject. Third, and only third, is weekly content teaching, which is what most families buy first.

On price, market rates read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 an hour and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with premium examiner-experienced tutors higher. In-home visiting rates run AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, and independent home tutors up to AED 500, because those figures absorb travel. Monthly online packages of around eight sessions advertise from AED 799. None of these are IB Gram prices; IB Gram quotes after a consultation.

The useful comparison for a Muwaileh family is cost per recovered mark rather than cost per hour. Four sessions on a research question in September can protect more marks than twenty sessions of content teaching in April, and that is a pricing argument as much as an academic one.

sections.heading: Home tutoring in a school-dense district, honestly compared
paragraphs: Muwaileh is unusual in the UAE in having a genuine local supply of tutors, because the schools are here and so are the teachers and the university students. A family searching for a home tutor in this district will find one, and for primary support or homework supervision that is a reasonable arrangement.

The limits show up in two places. The first is the conflict question: the closer a tutor sits to the school, the more likely it is that they are connected to it, and an arrangement in which your child's own teacher is paid privately is the one to avoid. The MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct, and in Abu Dhabi the education regulator's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Ask rather than assume.

The second is component specialism. The work this district actually needs is internal assessment supervision and marked paper cycles in specific subjects at specific levels. A local generalist can supervise homework; they cannot usually tell a Diploma candidate that their chemistry research question has no controllable variable. That is a subject-and-level match, and the pool for it is national rather than local.

IB Gram does not visit homes in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Muwaileh families are taught one-to-one over live video, with screen sharing for papers and a shared whiteboard. What video cannot do is replace laboratory bench time, and the school holds that part; a tutor teaches method, variables, uncertainty and analysis instead.

sections.heading: A diagnostic before a commitment
paragraphs: The starting sequence in this district should be unusually short, because the information needed is specific and mostly already in the house.

Send three documents: the statement of entry or subject list with board, code, tier and level; the most recent report; and the school's internal assessment and mock calendar. Those three answer almost every question a tutor needs to ask, and a family that arrives with them skips two weeks of discovery.

Then buy a diagnostic rather than a term. One session on a timed paper, marked strictly, tells you whether the problem is content, technique or planning. One session on an internal assessment research question tells you whether the component is on course or already compromised. Either costs one hour and determines what the next ten should be.

Read the first session note carefully, because it is the clearest signal you will get. A note that names a specific misconception, a question type where marks are going, or a prerequisite missing from two years back is a note written by someone who was paying attention. A note that reports good engagement and a positive attitude has told you nothing you can act on, and a second one like it is a reason to change tutor rather than to wait.

Finally, ask what happens if the specialist you need is not available at your hour. Scarce Higher Level subjects sometimes have nobody free in a Sharjah evening, and the honest answers are a waiting position or a tutor in a time zone that fits. A generalist described as a specialist is the answer to avoid, and the way a provider handles that question predicts how it will handle everything else.

process.title: Send three documents, not a description
process.description: The subject list with board, code, tier and level; the latest report; and the school's internal assessment and mock calendar. Those three remove most of the guesswork, and the third one is the document that determines when sessions should happen.

process.title: Buy one diagnostic hour
process.description: A timed paper marked strictly, or a research question interrogated properly. One hour tells you whether the problem is content, technique or planning, and those three need completely different plans and different amounts of money.

process.title: Fix the component, not the subject
process.description: If the marks are going on explain questions, the repair is a command-verb drill rather than a syllabus re-teach. Narrow repairs work faster and cost less, and the diagnostic is what identifies which narrow repair applies.

process.title: Position sessions against the school's calendar
process.description: Internal deadlines and mock windows set by the school arrive long before any external date. Sessions timed against those dates do useful work; sessions timed against the exam window arrive too late to change the drafting.

process.title: Review against the next real assessment
process.description: Judge the arrangement on the next school mock or unit test rather than on a number of weeks. If the mark has not moved, change one variable deliberately: the component being targeted, the frequency, or the tutor.

whyPoints.title: Aimed at the independent half of the course
whyPoints.description: The work this district needs is marked timed practice and internal assessment supervision, not a second delivery of content the school already teaches well. Sessions are built around the component where marks are actually being lost.

whyPoints.title: Criteria quoted as mark allocations
whyPoints.description: Internal assessment criteria appear here with their letters and marks rather than as a general idea, with an instruction to confirm the current figures through the school. Knowing that reflection carries three marks changes how a student writes it.

whyPoints.title: Tier and code confirmed before teaching
whyPoints.description: Core or Extended, Cambridge or Pearson, Higher or Standard Level: the first question on every enquiry. A tutor teaching the wrong tier or the wrong specification is teaching a course the candidate is not entered for.

whyPoints.title: Honest about delivery and limits
whyPoints.description: IB Gram does not visit homes in the UAE; in-home tutoring is an India-only service. Video lessons also cannot replace laboratory bench time, and both facts are stated before any payment rather than discovered later.

whyPoints.title: The student's work stays theirs
whyPoints.description: Tutors interrogate a research question, explain criteria and respond to drafts the student has written. No supplied text, no supplied data, no completed assessment at any price, because a malpractice finding costs more than any mark it could buy.

whyPoints.title: Figures sourced or absent
whyPoints.description: Every AED band here is a market figure with the kind of provider that publishes it and the month read. Entry dates come from Cambridge and Pearson publications. IB session dates are deliberately not restated, because they must be confirmed with the school first.

faqs.question: Our Muwaileh school is good. Why would we need a tutor at all?
faqs.answer: Because a good school and a complete course are different things. Class time delivers content, runs practicals and sets periodic assessments. What it generally cannot contain is a student sitting a whole past paper under timed conditions each week and having every one marked individually with feedback by question type, or a teacher giving thirty internal assessment research questions the hour each one deserves. Those two pieces of work carry a large share of the available marks, and they sit outside the timetable in almost every school anywhere.

faqs.question: How many past papers has my child actually sat under timed conditions?
faqs.answer: Ask them, because the answer is usually lower than parents assume and it is the most useful diagnostic question available. A paper read through at home is not a paper sat; a paper sat but self-marked is not a paper marked. If the honest answer this term is none, the first purchase is not more teaching but a marked timed cycle, because the content is probably in place and the marks are being lost in the room rather than in the knowledge.

faqs.question: What are the Diploma maths exploration criteria worth in marks?
faqs.answer: The exploration is assessed against five criteria totalling twenty marks: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection, and use of mathematics, with use of mathematics carrying the largest single share. Knowing the split matters because candidates treat reflection and personal engagement as decoration when together they carry a meaningful number of marks. Confirm the current allocations against the subject guide through your school's Diploma coordinator before planning around them, since the IB revises its guides.

faqs.question: How is a Diploma science investigation marked?
faqs.answer: Against four criteria totalling twenty-four marks: research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The pattern of lost marks is consistent. Research design fails when there is no controllable independent variable. Data analysis fails when raw data is presented without processing or uncertainty. Conclusions fail when they are not supported by the data collected, and evaluations fail when limitations are listed generically rather than tied to the method used. Confirm the current criteria with your school before relying on these figures.

faqs.question: When should a Muwaileh Diploma student start work on their internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Earlier than almost anyone does. The decisive moment is choosing the research question, which happens in the first weeks of the course, and a question that cannot generate a usable spread of data cannot be rescued once the data is collected. Two or three sessions on question design before any data gathering protect a fifth of the subject grade. Families who contact a tutor at the drafting stage are usually paying more for a worse outcome than families who called in September.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the line between legitimate IA support and malpractice?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the boundary is clear. A tutor can teach the content, interrogate the research question, explain what each criterion asks for, read a draft the student has written and say where it falls short, and teach referencing and data presentation. A tutor must not supply text, data, analysis or conclusions that end up in the submission. The test is whether the school would be comfortable seeing the tutor's contribution on the page. Anyone selling a finished assessment is selling a malpractice finding.

faqs.question: My child was entered for Core rather than Extended. Can that be changed?
faqs.answer: Only before the entry deadline, which falls months ahead of the papers. For the Cambridge March 2027 series, final entries are due on 27 November 2026 against an exam period of 3 February to 4 March 2027. After that the tier is fixed for that series, and the grade ceiling with it. If you want the question reopened, the useful move is evidence: have the candidate sit Extended past papers under timed conditions, marked honestly, and take that mark to the head of department.

faqs.question: What is the word limit on the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: It is normally capped at four thousand words, and the practical risk is not the ceiling but the internal deadlines around it. Schools set their own dates for a first draft, supervisor meetings, final submission and upload, and those arrive long before anything external. Ask the school for its written internal deadline schedule at the start of the Diploma year. Confirm the current word limit through the coordinator as well, because the IB revises its guidance and a figure copied from an old page is worse than none.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send tutors to homes in Muwaileh?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service run only in India. Muwaileh families are taught one-to-one over live video, with screen sharing for past papers and a shared whiteboard. In a district with this many schools there is a real local supply of visiting tutors, and for homework supervision that is a sensible option. For internal assessment supervision in a specific Diploma subject the match needs to be national rather than local.

faqs.question: Should we avoid a tutor who teaches at our own school?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct, and in Abu Dhabi the education regulator's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Beyond the rules, it is a conflict: the person who sets and marks the assessment should not also be paid to prepare your child for it. An independent tutor gives you a second reading of where the marks are going, which is most of the value you are buying.

faqs.question: What does tutoring cost in this part of Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 an hour and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with premium examiner-experienced tutors higher again. In-home visits run AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, and independent home tutors up to AED 500, because travel is absorbed in the rate. Monthly online packages of about eight sessions advertise from AED 799. IB Gram quotes after a consultation rather than publishing a flat rate.

faqs.question: Is it better to spend money in September or in April?
faqs.answer: September, almost always, and by a wide margin in the Diploma. Three sessions in the first term on an internal assessment research question protect a fifth of a subject grade that cannot be recovered later. Three sessions in April can only polish what already exists. In an examined IGCSE year, autumn money buys tier evidence and content repair while spring money buys technique, which is still worthwhile but narrower. The expensive mistake is buying broadly and late.

faqs.question: How do practical skills get taught if lessons are on video?
faqs.answer: Method, variables, uncertainty, graph work and analysis all teach well on screen, and that is where most practical marks are actually awarded. Cambridge alternative-to-practical papers test naming a control variable, justifying a repeat reading and identifying a systematic error, none of which need apparatus. What video cannot replace is bench time, which belongs to the school laboratory. A tutor claiming otherwise is overselling; the honest division is that the school provides the hands and the tutor the reasoning.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we tutor at once in an exam year?
faqs.answer: One or two, done properly. Exam technique improves through repetition within a single subject, so four subjects at one session each produces shallow work in all of them and consumes four evenings. The pattern that moves a grade is one subject, twice a week, almost entirely on marked papers, with the school handling the rest. Add a second subject only once the first has stabilised against a real school assessment, and expect to drop something else from the week to make room.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is free for a scarce Higher Level subject?
faqs.answer: You should be told plainly rather than offered someone adjacent. Some Higher Level subjects have no UAE-based specialist free in the Sharjah evening window, and the honest options are a waiting position until a slot opens or a tutor in another time zone whose working day covers your evening. Ask who the tutor is, what they have taught and at what level, and ask before paying. A provider that answers vaguely has told you how it will behave for the rest of the year.

sharjah/muwaileh.closingHeading: Buy the half of the course that nobody else covers
sharjah/muwaileh.closingBody: Muwaileh families are generally not short of teaching. They are short of marked timed practice and of serious attention on the internally assessed work that carries a fifth of each Diploma subject grade. Send the subject list with board, code and tier, the latest report, and the school's internal deadline calendar, and the first hour can go on a diagnostic rather than a sales conversation. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, criteria figures here should be confirmed through your school, and the student writes every word of their own assessed work.

A Cambridge 0620 chemistry specialist and a Pearson 4CH1 chemistry specialist prepare candidates for different papers, and matching the wrong one to a student is the most common and most avoidable error in this market.

intro.heading: The decision most households here are actually weighing
paragraphs: Sharjah Garden City is a villa community south-east of the inland school belt, along the Al Dhaid corridor, with a large population of families from India and Pakistan and a smaller number from the Levant and Egypt. The housing is spacious, the commute is long, and the academic conversation in these households is unusually specific: a high proportion are either in an Indian-curriculum school considering a move to an international one, or have recently made that move and are discovering what it involved.

That makes this a decision page rather than a grade page. The question is not only whether to switch, but what a switch actually commits a child to. Parents are generally well informed about CBSE and considerably less so about the differences between the two international boards their child might end up sitting, which is understandable, because almost nobody in this market explains them.

Here is the part that surprises people. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both offer an International GCSE in mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology and English, and in each case the two are different qualifications with different codes, different paper structures, different formula provision and different approaches to practical assessment. Cambridge mathematics is 0580; the Pearson equivalent is 4MA1. A tutor teaching one while the child sits the other is teaching a real course to the wrong candidate.

The second thing families here discover late is that the school chooses the board, not the parent, and that the choice is rarely explained at admission. A household can move for a British curriculum, find the school enters candidates with Pearson, and spend a year using Cambridge past papers bought on a neighbour's recommendation. The statement of entry is the document that settles it, and asking for it in Year 10 rather than Year 11 is the single cheapest piece of planning available.

The distance matters in one further way. Living out along the corridor means a parent is not at the school gate hearing that entries close in November or that the mock week has shifted. Information has to be requested in writing rather than picked up, and households here who do well are the ones who ask for the statement of entry, the mock calendar and the zone timetable as documents rather than waiting for a message home.

IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video, matched by board and code rather than by area. IB Gram does not visit homes in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service run only in India. For a community this far from the school belt that is also an availability point: the local supply of board-specific specialists is thin, and a video slot does not depend on who is prepared to drive out along the Al Dhaid road at seven in the evening.

sharjah/sharjah-garden-city.programmesIntro: Four routes are live in this community, and the useful information about each is what it demands that the previous one did not. That difference is the work a switch creates.

programmes.name: Indian curriculum, Classes 9 and 10
programmes.description: A centrally examined curriculum with a predictable paper structure, strong emphasis on procedural accuracy and complete solutions, and a reporting culture built on percentages. Candidates arrive at an international board drilled, fast and accurate, which is a genuine advantage that is often undersold.
programmes.countryNote: The reason so many Sharjah Garden City families consider a switch is university destination rather than dissatisfaction. It is worth being clear with yourself about which it is, because if the schooling is working and only the destination is in question, there are routes other than changing system, and a switch made in Class 10 is the most expensive version of this decision.

programmes.name: Cambridge International IGCSE
programmes.description: Assessed by syllabus code, with Core and Extended tiers in maths and sciences that cap the attainable grade, and in sciences an alternative-to-practical paper that examines experimental reasoning on paper. Cambridge runs June and November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the school for its zone timetable in writing, especially from a community this far out.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Graded 9 to 1, with specification codes beginning 4, commonly two written papers per subject and a formula sheet supplied in several of them. Available in May or June and again in November, and some qualifications are modular, which changes when revision has to peak.
programmes.countryNote: The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Provisional timetables are revised, so build a plan from the live PDF on qualifications.pearson.com rather than from a date copied elsewhere.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The post-16 route many families here are ultimately aiming at, with six subjects, internally assessed components, Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. It assumes independent research and sustained written work, neither of which an examination-led system trains.
programmes.countryNote: If the Diploma is the destination, the IGCSE years are preparation for it rather than an end in themselves. That changes the subject and tier decisions: keeping Extended tier sciences and a strong maths route open matters more than maximising the number of grades, and a household weighing a switch should decide this before Year 10 rather than during it.

sharjah/sharjah-garden-city.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are listed with their codes on both boards where relevant, because the code is what a tutor must teach to. Availability follows board and level rather than neighbourhood, since lessons are delivered over video.

subjects.name: Mathematics, Cambridge 0580 and Pearson 4MA1
subjects.levels: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher
subjects.description: Both assess the same broad content and differ in paper count, question order, formula provision and the proportion of marks carried by method. A candidate trained on the wrong board loses time rather than knowledge, which is worse because it is invisible until the mock.

subjects.name: Physics, Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1
subjects.description: Cambridge sets an alternative-to-practical paper that examines experimental method on paper; Pearson supplies a formula sheet that changes what must be memorised. Both punish method answers that omit a control variable or a repeat reading.

subjects.name: Chemistry, Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1
subjects.description: Mole calculations and electrolysis dominate lost marks on either board. Cambridge's qualitative analysis tables have to be learned as tables, and candidates who reason them out under time pressure give away marks they already held.

subjects.name: Biology, Cambridge 0610 and Pearson 4BI1
subjects.description: Long syllabuses where precision rather than coverage decides the grade. Examiners want the structure named, the mechanism linked and the direction stated, which is a writing discipline a procedural background rarely builds.

subjects.name: English Language, Cambridge 0500 and Pearson 4EA1
subjects.description: Summary and directed-writing tasks have a learnable form, and the two boards set them differently. This is the subject where a confident speaker from an Indian-curriculum school most often underperforms in a first international year.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language, Cambridge 0510 and 0511
subjects.description: Reading for detail rewards precision over fluency, and the listening components need practice under exam conditions. A good choice where academic register rather than comprehension is the real gap.

subjects.name: Economics, Cambridge 0455 and Pearson 4EC1
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides more marks than essay prose. Axes mislabelled, no new equilibrium marked, and evaluation that lists both sides without judging are the three recurring faults on either board.

subjects.name: Business Studies, Cambridge 0450 and Pearson 4BS1
subjects.description: Marks come from applying a concept to the case material and reaching a defended conclusion. Candidates who define terms accurately and never apply them plateau in the middle of the range.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics, Cambridge 0606
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by candidates heading for a demanding post-16 maths route. Useful preparation for Diploma Analysis and Approaches, and a reasonable way to keep that door open from a CBSE background.

subjects.name: Computer Science, Cambridge 0478
subjects.description: Algorithm design and pseudocode conventions carry more marks than programming fluency. Students who code well still lose marks on tracing tables and on documenting a design decision.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the licensed curriculum in UAE private schools, and frequently the lowest grade on an otherwise strong report. Script fluency and verb patterns respond to short frequent sessions rather than to intensive blocks.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Pearson, side by side, by code
paragraphs: The single most useful table in this market does not exist anywhere in it, which is strange, because the information is public and the consequences of not having it are expensive. Two awarding bodies offer an International GCSE in the same subjects. Their qualifications share most of the content and differ in how it is examined.

Start with identification. Cambridge syllabus codes are four digits: mathematics 0580, physics 0625, chemistry 0620, biology 0610, first language English 0500, economics 0455, business studies 0450, computer science 0478, additional mathematics 0606. Pearson Edexcel specification codes begin with a 4: mathematics A is 4MA1, physics 4PH1, chemistry 4CH1, biology 4BI1, English language A 4EA1, economics 4EC1, business 4BS1.

Then the differences that change how a candidate should prepare. Cambridge tiers sciences and mathematics into Core and Extended, which caps the attainable grade at Core; Pearson mathematics is tiered Foundation and Higher. Several Pearson specifications supply a formula sheet, which shifts revision away from memorising relationships and towards selecting the right one. Cambridge sciences set an alternative-to-practical paper examining experimental reasoning on paper. Paper counts and question orders differ, which affects pacing more than difficulty.

None of this makes either board better. It makes them different, and it means a tutor, a past paper and a revision guide all have to match the board the child is entered for. The table sets the pairs out; check every code against the statement of entry, because schools occasionally enter different subjects with different boards.

sections.heading: Grades, tiers and what a 9 to 1 scale does not tell you
paragraphs: Families moving from a percentage-based system have to learn a new reporting language, and the thing that causes the most confusion is that a grade carries information about the tier as well as about the performance.

A Cambridge candidate entered for Core cannot be awarded above the Core grade range however well they perform. A candidate entered for Extended can reach the full range. The same logic applies to Pearson Foundation and Higher tier mathematics. So two children with the same grade may have performed very differently, and a strong Core grade can still fail a sixth-form entry requirement that specifies a grade only available at Extended.

The second point of confusion is the coexistence of scales. Cambridge reports on 9 to 1 or on A* to G depending on the syllabus and the region, and Pearson International GCSE reports on 9 to 1. Converting between them in your head is a bad idea; read the grade as it is issued and read the sixth-form requirement as it is written.

The practical consequence is to ask two questions before accepting a tier. Which grade range does this tier make available, and what grade does the post-16 course we are aiming at require. If those two answers are incompatible, the conversation to have is with the head of department, and the useful evidence is a marked higher-tier past paper rather than a parental opinion.

One caution about comparing with an Indian-curriculum report. A percentage and a 9 to 1 grade are not translatable into each other, and attempts to do it produce false comfort or needless alarm. A child who scored in the eighties under one system has told you nothing about which grade they would reach under another, because the papers reward different behaviour. The only honest comparison is a marked past paper from the board they will actually sit.

sections.heading: What a board switch leaves the student to work out alone
paragraphs: A school teaches the content of the specification it has chosen, and it generally teaches it well. What it rarely teaches explicitly is the board-specific apparatus around that content, and that apparatus is where a transferring candidate loses marks for a term or more.

Four things in particular are left to the student. The paper structure, meaning how many papers there are, what each covers and how long each is. The formula position, meaning what is supplied and what has to be memorised, which differs between the boards and changes revision priorities. The question order and the mark distribution, which determine pacing. And the mark scheme conventions for that board, which determine what wording earns a mark.

None of those is difficult. All of them are invisible unless somebody names them, and a candidate who has been practising on the other board's past papers, as many do on a relative's recommendation, will have learned the wrong set. This is the specific independent-work gap in this community, and it is cheap to close once identified.

The table below is the checklist worth going through once, in the first term of Year 10, with the actual specification open. An hour spent on it saves a term of misdirected practice, and it is work a capable student can largely do themselves if somebody tells them what to look for.

Two sources are worth using directly rather than through an intermediary. The awarding body's own site carries the specification and the past papers for the code the child sits, and the school's examinations officer holds the entry details and the timetable. Everything else circulating in a community like this one, including advice from a relative whose child sat a different board three years ago, should be checked against those two before it changes anything.

sections.heading: What transfers from an Indian-curriculum background, and what does not
paragraphs: There is a condescending version of this conversation in which a CBSE background is treated as a deficit. It is not, and families in this community should push back on anyone who implies it. What a candidate brings from that system is real and valuable, and what they lack is specific and learnable.

What transfers well is procedural fluency, speed, accuracy and work ethic. A CBSE-trained candidate frequently out-calculates classmates and copes with a heavy content load without complaint. In mathematics in particular, the transfer at the level of method is nearly complete, which is why maths is usually the first subject to look fine after a switch.

What does not transfer is the explanatory apparatus. Command verbs, the expectation that a six-mark answer contains a mechanism and a consequence, the habit of evaluating rather than describing, and the write-up conventions of practical work. Those are not intelligence or effort; they are a vocabulary nobody has taught, and ten to sixteen weeks of targeted work generally closes the gap.

The sequencing advice follows from that. Do not start a transfer block with content revision, because the content is largely present. Start with a marked past paper from the correct board, group the lost marks by question type, and work on the two question types that account for most of them. Families who do this in the first term of Year 10 rarely need help in Year 11.

It helps to say this to the student explicitly. A capable child who has been near the top of a class and is suddenly scoring in the middle tends to conclude that they have become worse at the subject, when what has happened is that they are being marked on a form of answer nobody has taught them. That conclusion, left alone for a few weeks, costs more than the marks did, and it is entirely avoidable with one honest conversation.

sections.heading: If the school does not offer the subject: the private candidate route
paragraphs: A recurring problem in this community is a child who needs a subject their school does not teach, usually additional mathematics, computer science or a particular science, often because the intended post-16 route requires it. The private candidate route exists and it is more constrained than families expect.

The mechanics are these. Entries are made by a centre, not by an individual, so a private candidate needs a centre willing to enter them. That centre sets its own deadlines inside the board's deadlines, charges its own fees, and may decline subjects it cannot administer. Components involving coursework or practical assessment are the most likely to be unavailable to private candidates, so the subject you want is sometimes offered only in a restricted form.

The deadlines are the part that catches people. The board's own cut-offs sit months before the papers: Cambridge sets final entries for the March 2027 series on 27 November 2026, with the exam period running from 3 February to 4 March 2027, and the centre's internal deadline will be earlier still. A plan formed in January for a February sitting is not a plan.

What a family should do is contact candidate centres early, ask which subjects and which components they will enter a private candidate for, ask for their internal deadline and their fee, and get all of it in writing. Entry fees are set by the centre rather than published centrally, so no figure should be quoted to you by a tutoring provider, including this one.

sections.heading: What the switch costs, in money and in time
paragraphs: A board or system change has two costs and families usually budget only for the first. The fee difference between schools is visible and easy to compare. The academic cost is a term or two of adjustment, and it is paid in the child's time and sometimes in a tutoring bill.

On tutoring, market rates read in October 2026 put qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300 an hour and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with premium examiner-experienced tutors higher. In-home visiting rates run AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, and independent home tutors up to AED 500, since travel is absorbed. Monthly online packages of around eight sessions advertise from AED 799. None are IB Gram prices; IB Gram quotes after a consultation.

The planning number is the block, not the hour. A transfer catch-up in one subject is typically ten to sixteen sessions. Fixing a wrong-board practice habit is often four to six. A board-and-route consultation is one. Costing those out makes the decision concrete, and it compares favourably with a year of general weekly tutoring bought because nobody diagnosed anything.

Worth adding for context: the Dubai regulator confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in that emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package. Sharjah fees are approved by the Sharjah Private Education Authority on its own basis, so a Dubai announcement is not a Sharjah one, and the school is where to ask.

sections.heading: Home tutoring a long way from the school belt
paragraphs: This community has space and villas, which makes an in-home tutor an attractive idea, and distance, which makes it a difficult one. Both things are true and a family deserves to hear both.

The practical position is that local supply here is thin, so a visiting tutor is usually travelling from Muwaileh, the older centre or across the Dubai boundary. That journey is priced into the rate whether the invoice says so or not, it limits how many evening appointments the tutor can hold, and it means the slot on offer is often earlier than a household returning from a long commute can actually use.

The board-specific requirement sharpens the problem. The pool of tutors within driving distance who teach the exact specification a child sits, with that board's past papers and mark schemes, is small. Families end up choosing a tutor for availability and discovering in the spring that the practice material was the wrong board, which is the specific failure this page exists to prevent.

IB Gram does not visit homes in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Households here are taught one-to-one over live video, matched by board and code. The limits are honest ones: a quiet room and a camera are needed, maths work needs the student's working in shot, which a phone above a notebook solves, and laboratory bench time belongs to the school rather than to any tutor.

sections.heading: Deciding, then starting
paragraphs: Two decisions and one purchase, in that order, is the sequence that works for a household in this community. Reversing it is how families end up a year in with a tutor teaching the wrong specification.

The first decision is whether to switch system at all, and the honest test is to separate dissatisfaction from destination. If the schooling is working and only the university route is in question, there may be routes that do not require changing system, and a switch in Class 10 is the most expensive version of this decision available. If the switch is right, make it at the end of Class 8 or Class 9 rather than later.

The second decision is not yours: the school picks the board. What is yours is finding out which one, in writing, in Year 10. Ask the admissions office or the examinations officer for the board and code per subject, the tier where one applies, and the centre's zone timetable. Those answers make every subsequent choice straightforward.

Then buy one diagnostic hour: a past paper from the correct board, sat to time, marked strictly, with the lost marks grouped by question type. That hour tells you whether you need a ten-session transfer block, a four-session board-correction block, or nothing at all. It is a far better first purchase than a standing weekly slot bought on a neighbour's recommendation, and in this community it frequently reveals that the subject the family was worried about is not where the marks were going.

process.title: Separate dissatisfaction from destination
process.description: Decide whether you are switching because the schooling is not working or because of where it leads. Those have different answers, and a system change made in Class 10 is the most expensive version of this decision available.

process.title: Get the board and code in writing
process.description: Ask the school for the board, specification code and tier for every subject, plus the centre's zone timetable. The school chooses the board and rarely explains it, and everything a tutor does depends on that answer.

process.title: Buy one diagnostic hour
process.description: A past paper from the correct board, sat to time and marked strictly, with lost marks grouped by question type. That hour decides whether the work ahead is ten sessions, four, or none, which no conversation can establish.

process.title: Close the board-specific gaps first
process.description: Paper structure, formula provision, mark distribution and mark scheme conventions, before any content revision. These are invisible until named and cheap to fix once they are, and they are where a transferring candidate leaks marks.

process.title: Check the entry route early if a subject is missing
process.description: If a required subject is not taught, contact candidate centres two terms ahead and get their subject list, internal deadline and fee in writing. Cambridge set 27 November 2026 as final entries for a March 2027 series.

whyPoints.title: Matched by code, not by subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are different qualifications, and a tutor is assigned to the specification the candidate actually sits. In a market where wrong-board practice is routine, this is the most consequential matching decision there is.

whyPoints.title: The board differences published, not glossed
whyPoints.description: Paper counts, formula provision, tiering and practical assessment all differ between the two boards, and this page sets out which is which. No competing page in this market does, and the omission costs families a term of misdirected revision.

whyPoints.title: An Indian-curriculum background treated as an asset
whyPoints.description: Procedural fluency, speed and accuracy transfer almost completely; command verbs and mechanism-based explanation do not. The work is naming the second group and closing it, usually in ten to sixteen sessions, not retreading content already known.

whyPoints.title: Entry routes explained with real deadlines
whyPoints.description: Private candidate entry runs through a centre with its own deadlines inside the board's, and coursework components are often unavailable. Those constraints are published here rather than discovered in January.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated plainly
whyPoints.description: IB Gram does not visit homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is an India-only service. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, and no regulator or examination board has approved, accredited or licensed IB Gram.

whyPoints.title: No entry fees invented
whyPoints.description: Examination entry fees are set by the centre rather than published centrally, so no figure appears here. Every AED band on this page is a market tutoring rate with the kind of provider that published it and the month it was read.

faqs.question: How do I find out which board my child's school will enter them for?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer or the admissions office directly, in writing, and ask subject by subject, because schools sometimes use different boards for different subjects. The statement of entry is the document that settles it. Do not infer the board from the textbook, since schools often teach from one publisher and enter candidates with another awarding body. Get this in Year 10 rather than Year 11, because it determines which past papers, mark schemes and tutor are the right ones.

faqs.question: If both boards call it an International GCSE, what is actually different?
faqs.answer: No. They cover similar content and differ in how it is examined. Cambridge mathematics is 0580 and the Pearson equivalent is 4MA1; Cambridge physics is 0625 against Pearson 4PH1. The differences that matter are paper counts, question order, what formulae are supplied, tiering structure and whether practical skills are examined through a dedicated paper. Neither board is better. Both punish a candidate who has practised on the other one's papers, because pacing and mark scheme wording differ.

faqs.question: My child has been revising with the wrong board's past papers. How bad is that?
faqs.answer: Recoverable, and worth fixing immediately. The content overlap is large, so the knowledge is not wasted, but pacing, formula expectations and mark scheme wording are board-specific and those are exactly the things that decide marks under time pressure. Typically four to six sessions on the correct board's papers closes the gap, which is a small cost compared with discovering the problem in a mock. Switch the practice material on the day you confirm the board.

faqs.question: What does Core and Extended actually mean for the grade?
faqs.answer: Core caps the attainable grade range, however well the candidate performs, while Extended makes the full range available. Pearson mathematics works the same way with Foundation and Higher tiers. So a strong Core grade can still fail a sixth-form requirement that specifies a grade only available at Extended. Before accepting a tier, ask which grade range it makes available and what the post-16 course requires, and raise any mismatch in the autumn because the tier is fixed at the entry deadline.

faqs.question: When should a family move a child from an Indian-curriculum school to an international one?
faqs.answer: The end of Class 8, or Class 9 at a push. That gives two years to learn the command verb vocabulary, the mechanism-based explanation that mark schemes reward, and the practical write-up conventions, none of which a procedural system builds. A switch into Year 11 is survivable but the honest plan becomes triage across two or three subjects rather than a full catch-up. Also separate the reasons first: if only the university destination is in question, there may be routes that do not require changing system.

faqs.question: What does a CBSE background actually give a child in an IGCSE class?
faqs.answer: More than this market usually admits. Procedural fluency, calculation speed, accuracy and tolerance for a heavy content load all transfer, and in mathematics the transfer at the level of method is close to complete, which is why maths is usually the first subject to look fine. What does not transfer is the explanatory apparatus: answering the verb, giving a mechanism and a consequence, evaluating rather than describing. That is a vocabulary gap rather than an ability gap, and it closes in ten to sixteen weeks.

faqs.question: My child needs a subject the school does not teach. Can they sit it privately?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, through an approved examination centre willing to enter private candidates. Entries are made by a centre rather than by an individual, so you need one that will take your child, in the subject you want, including any practical or coursework component, which is where the route most often fails. The centre sets its own internal deadline inside the board's deadline and its own fee. Start two terms ahead and get the subject list, the deadline and the fee in writing.

faqs.question: How much does an examination entry cost as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: That depends on the centre, and no tutoring provider should quote you a figure. Entry fees are set by the centre rather than published centrally, and they vary with the subject, the number of components and the administrative work involved. Ask two or three candidate centres for their fee schedule in writing and compare. Ask also what the fee includes, whether practical components are available, and what their internal deadline is, because the centre's cut-off always precedes the board's.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor out to Sharjah Garden City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not make home visits anywhere in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service run only in India. Households here are taught one-to-one over live video, matched by board and specification code. This far from the school belt the local pool of board-specific specialists is thin, and a visiting tutor is usually travelling from the inland belt or the older centre, pricing that journey into the rate and offering only the hours the journey allows.

faqs.question: Which board is better for getting into a good university?
faqs.answer: Neither, and anyone telling you otherwise is selling something. Both Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE are widely recognised school qualifications, and admissions decisions at post-16 and university level rest on grades, post-16 qualifications and subject choices rather than on which awarding body issued a Year 11 certificate. The decision that genuinely affects a route is the tier and the subject set, because those determine which post-16 courses remain available.

faqs.question: What should we establish about the specification in the first term of Year 10?
faqs.answer: Six things: the board and code per subject, the tier where one applies, how many papers there are and what each covers, which formulae are supplied, how marks are distributed across question types, and whether practical skills are examined on paper. All six are public and all six change how revision should be organised. An hour spent on that checklist with the actual specification open saves a term of misdirected practice, and a capable student can do most of it themselves.

faqs.question: Do we need to worry about the Cambridge zone timetable?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth a written request. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the examinations officer which zone your centre is in and obtain that timetable in writing. From a community this far out, information has to be requested rather than absorbed at the school gate.

faqs.question: What is the fastest way to raise marks after a mid-year transfer?
faqs.answer: A marked past paper from the correct board, with lost marks grouped by question type rather than by topic. That almost always shows two recurring behaviours carrying most of the loss: method not shown on calculations, or describing where an explanation was asked for. Each is a one-session repair followed by practice. Content revision feels more thorough and usually moves fewer marks, because a transferring candidate's content knowledge is generally better than their mark scheme literacy.

faqs.question: Will tutoring fees or school fees change next year?
faqs.answer: School fees in Sharjah are approved by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, whose remit covers tuition fees as well as curricula and assessment, so your school is the place to ask. A fee announcement in another emirate is not a Sharjah announcement: the Dubai regulator confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase for private schools in that emirate for 2026-27, which does not apply here. On tutoring, market rates read in October 2026 are set out in the table above with their sources.

faqs.question: How long should a transfer catch-up block run before we review it?
faqs.answer: Ten to sixteen sessions for a CBSE to IGCSE adjustment in one subject, four to six for a wrong-board correction, and two or three for practical write-up conventions. Each should end with a named test rather than a date: explain questions earning full marks on a marked paper, or two timed papers in the correct format at target standard. A block with no end condition becomes an indefinite weekly arrangement that nobody reviews, which is the most common way families overspend.

sharjah/sharjah-garden-city.closingHeading: Confirm the code, then diagnose once
sharjah/sharjah-garden-city.closingBody: The most expensive mistake available to a household in Sharjah Garden City is a year of tutoring aimed at the wrong specification. Ask the school in writing for the board, code and tier per subject, then buy one diagnostic hour: a past paper from the correct board, sat to time, marked strictly, with lost marks grouped by question type. That hour tells you whether the work ahead is sixteen sessions, four, or none. Lessons run one-to-one over live video and the student writes every word of their own assessed work.

sharjah/tilal-city.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are the ones Tilal City families use most: board-specific IGCSE specialists for Years 10 and 11, and Diploma subject tutors who work by marking and diagnosis rather than by re-delivering content the school has already taught.

intro.heading: When the commute is the constraint
paragraphs: Tilal City is a newer development out towards the interior of the emirate, away from the coastal districts and some distance from the inland school belt around Muwaileh and University City. Families move here for space and for value, and they accept a longer journey in exchange. That journey is the single most important fact about tutoring here, because it eats the part of the day in which independent work would otherwise happen.

Count it honestly. A school day that ends at 2:40pm, plus a journey that can run thirty-five to fifty minutes at that hour, plus a meal, leaves a student starting work somewhere after 5pm with a full set of homework and whatever revision they intended. On a Tuesday in March that is not enough time, and the thing that gets dropped is always the same: the self-directed work that nobody checks.

Which matters because the self-directed work is where a large share of the marks live. School covers content, runs practicals and sets periodic assessments. What it generally cannot contain is a student sitting whole past papers to time every week and having each one marked individually, or learning the vocabulary of command verbs, or being taught how to revise rather than being told to.

So the useful intervention in Tilal City is not more hours of teaching. It is making the hours the student does have produce something. That means a study method chosen on evidence rather than on how productive it feels, a plan the student can run without supervision, and a weekly check by someone who marks honestly. The tutor's job here is closer to a coach with a mark scheme than to a second teacher.

There is one more consequence of distance that families only notice late. Living far from the school also means living far from the informal conversation at the gate, the one where a parent hears that entries close in November or that the mock week has moved. Out here, information has to be requested in writing rather than absorbed, and the households that do well are the ones who ask the school for the zone timetable, the mock calendar and the internal deadlines rather than waiting to be told.

IB Gram delivers that one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not visit homes in the UAE, and in-home tutoring is a service run only in India. In a community this far out that is not a philosophical position but an availability one: the pool of tutors willing to drive to Tilal City for a 6pm appointment is small, the subset who teach a specific Higher Level subject is smaller still, and a video slot at 7pm is simply more reliable than a car on the Al Dhaid road.

sharjah/tilal-city.programmesIntro: Three programmes account for nearly all enquiries from this community. Each entry names the independent workload it assumes, since that is the part the commute squeezes.

programmes.name: Cambridge International IGCSE
programmes.description: Assessed by syllabus code across two years, with Core and Extended tiers in maths and sciences that cap the attainable grade. Cambridge runs June and November series for IGCSE, O Level and International A Level, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October.

A family this far from the school should have that zone timetable in writing rather than relying on a note home.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Graded 9 to 1, offered in May or June and in November, with formula provision and paper structures that differ from the Cambridge equivalent. Some qualifications are modular, which changes when revision has to peak and whether a resit is possible within the same course.
