umm-al-quwain/al-riqqa.programmesIntro: How much a programme assumes a student will manage alone differs sharply between the three routes below, and so does the kind of independent work that matters.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Terminal examinations at the end of Year 11 across eight to ten subjects. The independent demand here is almost entirely volume and self-marking: practice accumulated over months and checked honestly against published schemes. Cambridge separates Core and Extended tiers in several subjects, so practice must match the tier the school entered.
programmes.countryNote: Confirming the board, the code, the tier and the series by email matters more for a commuting family, because nobody is at the school gate to ask informally. Get it in writing in Year 10 and keep it, since every past paper the student touches for two years depends on that answer being right.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. The independent demand is coursework as well as revision, and it runs continuously rather than peaking before exams. Internal assessments are produced outside lesson time and submitted to internal deadlines set months before the written papers.
programmes.countryNote: A Diploma student commuting out of Umm Al Quwain has the hardest version of this, because coursework deadlines fall in the same evenings as homework and the travel has already taken part of the week. Front-loading coursework in Year 12 is the only version of the plan that works, and it has to be set up deliberately in September.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Three or four externally examined subjects with no central core. The independent expectation shifts towards reading beyond the lesson and sustained past-paper work, and the modular structure differs between boards, which affects when a result can be banked and therefore when a subject stops consuming revision time.
programmes.countryNote: With fewer subjects and no coursework core, A Levels are the more forgiving route for a commuting student, but they assume more unprompted reading. A student used to being told exactly what to study will find the first set of internal exams unpleasant unless that habit is built deliberately in the first term.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each and reported as criterion levels from 0 to 8. The independent demand is modest but the habits formed here are the ones the Diploma will rely on, particularly keeping a process journal and reading criterion feedback rather than the summary grade.
programmes.countryNote: Ask the school for the criterion-level breakdown rather than the summary grade. For a commuting household it is the cheapest and most informative diagnostic available, it arrives by email, and it is the earliest warning of the independent-work habits that will cost marks in the Diploma.

umm-al-quwain/al-riqqa.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are listed by what independent work actually moves them, because that is where the assumed hours either pay off or do not.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE 0580 and 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The purest volume subject. Thirty mixed multi-stage questions a week, self-marked against the scheme, moves a grade in a term. Reading worked examples for the same number of hours does not, and the difference between the two is invisible to anyone watching the student at a desk.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebra, functions, calculus and proof with a non-calculator paper and the Higher Level problem-solving paper. Independent work has to include attempting questions that defeat the student, because the Higher Level paper rewards sustaining an argument rather than recognising a type.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Multi-step questions are the grade boundary. Independent practice should be deliberately mixed rather than organised by topic, because selecting between energy, momentum and force approaches is the skill, and a topic-labelled exercise removes the selection step entirely.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Practical-reasoning questions about apparatus, anomalous readings and improvements are examined on the written paper and almost never revised deliberately, because they do not look like content. They are among the most recoverable marks available to an independent student.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: Command-term discipline is the whole of the independent gain. A student who sorts past questions by command term and writes one-line answer plans learns more in an hour than one who rereads a chapter, and the effect carries across every paper in the subject.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Independent work means timed writing that someone marks, which is precisely the part a student cannot supply alone. Where no marking is available, comparing their own answer against a published model line by line is the usable substitute.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Planning rather than writing is the efficient independent task. Five essay plans in an hour teaches more about argument structure than one finished essay, and the individual oral rewards rehearsal, which is one of the few genuinely solo activities on the course.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0450 and 0455
subjects.description: Case-study application is learned by doing many short case questions rather than by learning more theory. The evaluation marks at the end of long questions are the most commonly abandoned on the paper and the most improvable without a teacher present.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0460 and 0470
subjects.description: Case-study deployment and source handling. Independent work should be practising the deployment rather than accumulating more case material, because students almost always know more than they can use under time pressure.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Tracing algorithms by hand under time pressure is the examined skill most neglected by independent study, because writing code on a machine feels more productive and tests something different from what the paper asks for.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Retention-led, so independent work has to be frequent and short rather than long and weekly. Fifteen minutes daily on script reading and vocabulary beats a two-hour Saturday session, and the difference shows within a month.

subjects.name: Coursework and internal assessment
subjects.description: The work most exposed by a lack of supervision, because deadlines are internal and nobody chases until late. Independent progress depends on reading the criteria against the student's own draft, which is a teachable step and almost never taught.

regions.note: The old peninsula quarter. Furthest from the Ajman and Sharjah schools and therefore the shortest usable evening in the emirate, which is why long independent work there belongs on a weekend.

sections.heading: Auditing the week: taught hours against assumed hours
paragraphs: The useful first exercise is an hours audit rather than a subject review. Write down, for one real week, how many hours the student spends in taught lessons, how many on set homework, and how many on work that nobody set but everybody assumes: revision, past papers, coursework, reading. The third column is usually the largest for a Year 11 or Year 13 student and the only one with no supervision attached.

From Al Riqqa that third column is genuinely available, which is the local advantage. The Ajman run is short, students are home early by this emirate's standards, and the afternoon is not consumed by travel the way it is on the peninsula. Having the hours and not converting them is a more frustrating problem than not having them, and it is also a more fixable one.

What the audit usually reveals is that the assumed hours are being spent on the lowest-return activities. Rereading notes, copying out summaries, reorganising files, watching explanation videos. All of those feel like study, produce a visible artefact, and return very little per hour compared with timed retrieval, mixed-topic practice and self-marked past-paper work. The student is not idle; they are busy at the wrong things.

There is a second reason the audit is worth doing in writing rather than in your head. Independent hours are the part of the week nobody reports on, so a household's sense of them comes from impressions: the student was at the desk, the door was shut, the light was on. An hours table makes the distinction between presence and activity visible, and it usually settles an argument that was otherwise going to be had repeatedly for two years.
The table below is a template for that audit. Fill in the real numbers for one week rather than an estimate for a typical week, because estimates average away the two evenings that actually vanished.

sections.heading: Homework that is set against work that is assumed
paragraphs: Parents often judge whether a student is working by whether homework is finished, and that is a reasonable proxy for a Year 8 student and a poor one for a Year 11. Set homework is a fraction of the expected independent load by the final two years, and a student can complete all of it conscientiously while doing almost none of the work that actually determines the grade.

The distinction is worth making explicit in the household. Set homework is a floor, not a target. It is designed to consolidate the lesson, it is collected, and the student gets feedback on it. The assumed work is a different category: nobody set it, nobody collects it, and its absence shows up only in an examination months later. Treating the first as sufficient is the most common honest mistake families make.

There is a related trap in the way schools communicate. A teacher reporting that a student always finishes their homework is reporting on the floor, accurately and positively, and a parent hears a general statement about diligence. Both are behaving reasonably. The question that produces useful information is different: how much past-paper work has this student done, and have I seen any of it marked?

For a commuting household the follow-up matters more than elsewhere, because informal contact is limited. Written questions by email produce written answers, and a short specific question about independent work volume is more likely to get a useful reply than a general question about progress. The answer also tells you whether the school is tracking it at all, which is itself worth knowing.
bullets: Set homework is a floor by the final two years, not a target

sections.heading: Self-marking: the skill that stands in for a teacher at home
paragraphs: Of all the assumed skills, self-marking has the best return and is the least taught. A student who can take their own attempt at a long question and compare it honestly against a published mark scheme has effectively acquired a teacher for every hour of independent work they do. A student who cannot has to wait for someone else to tell them what went wrong, which in a commuting household may be a week later or never.

Doing it properly is a procedure rather than an attitude. Attempt the question under timed conditions and stop when the time stops. Mark in a different colour, awarding marks only for what is actually written rather than for what was intended. Note the mark lost and why, in a word or two, beside each loss. Then group the losses: content, method presentation, command-term response, or pacing. The grouping is the useful output and it takes two minutes.

The reason it fails without teaching is that students mark generously and do not know it. A step they were holding in their head reads as present; a conclusion they implied reads as stated. Watching a specialist mark the same script strictly, and then marking the next one themselves with the specialist questioning each awarded mark, corrects that in a handful of sessions. After that the student keeps the skill for the rest of their education.

Two cautions. Mark schemes and past papers belong to the exam boards, so they should be accessed through the school or the board's official site rather than from any provider distributing copies, and the version must match the syllabus code and series. And honesty is the whole mechanism: a self-marked score that flatters is worse than no score, because it removes the signal that something needs fixing.

sections.heading: Past papers: how many, which, and in what order
paragraphs: Past-paper practice is the highest-return independent activity in the final two years and it is almost always started too late and organised badly. Students typically begin complete papers a few weeks before the exams, having spent the preceding year on topic exercises, and discover pacing problems at the point where there is no time left to fix them.

A better sequence starts earlier and changes shape. Through the first year of a course, questions by topic, immediately after that topic is taught, are the right unit: they convert fresh teaching into exam-format practice while the content is still live. From the start of the final year, mixed-topic sets matter more, because selecting the right method is the examined skill and a topic-labelled question removes the selection. Complete papers under timed conditions belong monthly from the start of the final year and weekly in the last term.

Which papers also matters. They must match the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the current syllabus version, because a paper from an earlier specification can test content no longer on the course and omit content that is. A student practising the wrong board's papers loses marks on format rather than knowledge, which is the most avoidable loss available and is entirely a consequence of nobody having checked the code.

Marking is the constraint. A student can self-mark structured and calculation questions reliably once taught, but extended written answers need someone else, which is the sensible division of labour: volume done independently, extended writing marked by a specialist, and the session spent on what the marking revealed rather than on working through questions together.

sections.heading: The Cambridge and Pearson calendars side by side
paragraphs: A commuting family needs the series calendar in writing because they cannot pick it up informally, and the two boards work differently enough that assuming one applies to the other causes real problems. Both publish their dates; neither publishes them in a form a parent finds easily, which is why they are set out together here.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Its March series is the clearest illustration of how early the real deadlines sit: for March 2027, the exam period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries were due 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including for future November sittings, and provisional means revisable.

No International Baccalaureate session or results date appears on this page. The research behind it could not confirm any IB date from the IB's own site, which blocks automated access, so publishing one would be guessing. Confirm IB dates with your school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org directly, and treat any page quoting them without a source with caution.

sections.heading: Mocks: the most wasted data in a school year
paragraphs: A mock examination generates the single richest dataset a student will see before the real papers, and in most households it produces one number and a conversation about effort. The script, with its annotations and its pattern of losses, contains almost everything needed to plan the remaining months, and it usually goes into a bag.

Extracting the data takes about half an hour and starts with the same grouping used in self-marking. Sort every lost mark into content, method presentation, command-term response or pacing. Then look at the distribution across the paper: a script that falls away in the final section is reporting a pacing problem regardless of what the total says, and a script with losses evenly spread in the form of half-earned questions is reporting a technique habit rather than a knowledge gap.

The second thing a mock reveals is question selection, where the paper allows choice. Students pick the question whose topic looks familiar rather than the one whose command structure they can answer, and that single habit can cost a grade. It is visible on a mock script and invisible everywhere else, and it is correctable in one session once named.

The third is the gap between predicted and actual, which schools use for forecast grades. Cambridge requires forecast grades at a published point in the cycle, 27 February 2027 for the March 2027 series, and those forecasts rest on the evidence the school holds. A mock analysed and acted on changes the evidence base; a mock filed does not. That is a practical reason to treat the script as a working document rather than a verdict.
bullets: Group every lost mark into content, method, command term or pacing

sections.heading: When the school cannot offer a subject: the self-study route
paragraphs: In a small emirate with a narrow local option block, some Al Riqqa students want a subject their school does not timetable. That is a self-study route with an external entry at the end of it, and it is a real option rather than a loophole, but it has to be arranged in the right order or it fails on administration rather than on academics.

The sequence is: establish whether the school will support an entry at all, find an exam centre approved by the board that will accept the candidate, confirm which components that centre can administer, and check the entry deadline against the series calendar. Practical and speaking components are the usual constraint, because not every centre offers every component for an external candidate, and that is the question to ask first rather than last.

The academic demand is higher than families expect. Self-studying a full IGCSE subject alongside a normal timetable means covering content with no lessons, acquiring the exam technique with no class practice, and keeping to a schedule with no teacher chasing. It works for a motivated student with one additional subject and a clear reason. It does not work as a way of adding a third science to an already full year.

Where a tutor is genuinely necessary rather than merely helpful, this is it: there is no teacher, so the content has to come from somewhere, and the specification coverage has to be systematic rather than topic-by-interest. The right structure is a mapped schedule against the syllabus, weekly checkpoints, and past-paper practice from the start rather than at the end.

sections.heading: The parent's job here is project management, not teaching
paragraphs: Parents in commuting households often feel they should be able to help with the work and cannot, because the syllabus has moved since they sat it and the assessment conventions are unfamiliar. That is fine. The useful parental role in the independent half of a course is not subject teaching and it is more valuable than subject teaching would be.

Four things make the difference and none of them requires knowing the subject. Asking to see marked work regularly, which creates a mild and healthy accountability. Asking for the grouping rather than the score, which trains the student to produce it. Protecting one evening a week as slack, so a plan survives the first disruption. And keeping the calendar: internal deadlines, entry deadlines, series dates and results dates in one place everyone can see.

The fifth is harder and matters most: resisting the instinct to equate time at the desk with work. A student who spends three hours copying out notes is visibly busy and learning very little; a student who spends forty minutes on timed retrieval and then stops has done more. Rewarding visible effort over effective method is a natural parental error and it reinforces exactly the habits that cost marks.

For a commuting family there is a sixth: being the one who writes the emails. Informal teacher contact is limited, so specific written questions about past-paper volume, criterion breakdowns, internal deadlines and syllabus codes are the information channel. Those questions are reasonable, they get written answers, and the answers are worth keeping.

sections.heading: Starting from Al Riqqa
paragraphs: The first message should contain three things: the board and syllabus code with the tier where one applies, one recent marked paper rather than a report grade, and the honest arrival time at home after the Ajman or Sharjah run. From this district that arrival time is usually earlier than elsewhere in the emirate, which means a full session on a weekday is realistic and the plan can be more ambitious than on the peninsula.

The first lesson is free and it is spent on the marked paper. The output is a grouping: how much of the loss is content, how much is method presentation, how much is command-term response, and how much is pacing. Those four need completely different responses, and most families have never seen the distinction made. Sometimes the answer is that the student needs the self-marking protocol and four sessions, not a year of weekly teaching.

Where the honest answer is that the independent hours are the problem rather than the teaching, the plan says so and is built to hand over. A self-marking block ends when the student can run it alone. A past-paper programme sets volume as independent work and uses sessions for the marking they cannot do themselves. Both are designed to shrink rather than to grow, which is the opposite of how this market usually works.

On availability, narrow Higher Level specialists may not be free at the slot you want, and in that case you should get a timeline and alternatives rather than a substitute who nearly fits. If a match is wrong after two or three sessions, the tutor is changed. And if the diagnosis turns out to have been wrong, because a second marked piece shows no movement, it is the diagnosis that gets changed rather than the hours that get doubled.

process.title: Audit one real week
process.description: Count taught hours, set homework and assumed work for one actual week rather than a typical one. The third column is usually the largest and the only unsupervised one, and seeing the number is what makes the rest of the conversation concrete.

process.title: Send a marked paper and the codes
process.description: One recent script with the marker's annotations, plus the board, syllabus code and tier in writing from the exams officer. Every past paper the student touches for the next two years depends on those codes being right.

process.title: Take the free trial for a grouping
process.description: The first session is free and produces a grouping of the losses into content, method presentation, command-term response and pacing. Those four need different responses, and most families have never seen them separated.

process.title: Set volume as independent work
process.description: Practice volume is done between sessions, not inside them. Sessions are used for the marking a student cannot do alone, chiefly extended written answers, and for analysing what the marking revealed.

process.title: Plan the handover
process.description: A self-marking block ends when the student can run the protocol without supervision, and the end point is in the plan from the first session. Support that does not plan its own exit has built a dependency instead of a skill.

whyPoints.title: Aimed at the assumed hours
whyPoints.description: School teaches the syllabus and assumes self-marking, past-paper volume, mock analysis and revision sequencing. Those are the hours that decide the grade and the ones nobody is scheduled to teach, which is where sessions here are pointed.

whyPoints.title: Self-marking taught to be handed over
whyPoints.description: A student who can mark their own script honestly against the published scheme has acquired a teacher for every independent hour. Blocks are designed to end when that transfer is complete rather than to continue indefinitely.

whyPoints.title: Volume outside, analysis inside
whyPoints.description: Practice is set as independent work and sessions are spent on marking the student cannot do alone and on what it revealed. That buys fewer paid hours for more progress than working through questions together does.

whyPoints.title: Series dates from the boards themselves
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page come from each board's own published pages and are cited as such. No International Baccalaureate date appears, because none could be confirmed from an official source; confirm those with your coordinator.

whyPoints.title: Copyright respected
whyPoints.description: Past papers, mark schemes and syllabuses belong to the boards. They are referenced and linked rather than distributed, and practice must match the correct code, tier and current syllabus version to be worth doing at all.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery suits document work
whyPoints.description: Lessons are taught live online, one to one. Self-marking, mock analysis and coursework feedback are all document-based, and both people seeing the same annotated script at once is more precise than the same conversation across a table.

faqs.question: Our child finishes all their homework. Why is the grade not moving?
faqs.answer: Because by the final two years set homework is a floor rather than a target. The work that determines the grade is largely assumed: revision method, past-paper volume, self-marking, mock analysis and, for a Diploma student, coursework produced to internal deadlines. None of it is set, none of it is collected, and its absence shows up only in an examination months later. A teacher reporting that homework is always finished is reporting accurately on the floor. Ask instead how much past-paper work has been done and whether any of it has been marked.

faqs.question: How do we teach a student to mark their own work honestly?
faqs.answer: By turning it into a procedure rather than an attitude. Attempt the question under timed conditions and stop when the time stops. Mark in a different colour, awarding marks only for what is written rather than what was intended. Annotate each loss with a two-word reason. Then group the losses into content, method presentation, command-term response and pacing. Students mark generously without knowing it, so the fix is watching a specialist mark the same script strictly and then being questioned on each mark they award themselves.

faqs.question: When should past-paper practice actually start?
faqs.answer: In the first year of the course, as topic questions immediately after each topic is taught, which converts fresh teaching into exam format while the content is live. From the start of the final year, mixed-topic sets matter more because choosing the method is the examined skill and a topic label removes the choice. Complete timed papers belong monthly from the start of the final year and weekly in the final term. Starting complete papers a few weeks before the exams finds pacing problems too late to fix.

faqs.question: Does it matter which past papers we use?
faqs.answer: A great deal. They must match the board, the syllabus code, the tier where one applies and the current syllabus version, because papers from an earlier specification can test content no longer on the course and omit content that is. A student practising the wrong board's papers loses marks on question format rather than on knowledge, which is the most avoidable loss available. Ask the exams officer for the codes and tiers in writing, and access papers through the school or the board's own official site rather than from a third party.

faqs.question: What should we do with a returned mock script?
faqs.answer: Spend half an hour on it before it goes in a bag. Sort every lost mark into content, method presentation, command-term response or pacing. Look at the distribution across the paper, because a script that falls away in the final section is reporting a pacing problem whatever the total says. Check question selection where the paper offers choice, since students pick familiar topics rather than answerable command structures. Mocks also feed the evidence behind school forecast grades, which Cambridge required by 27 February 2027 for the March 2027 series.

faqs.question: How far ahead do Cambridge entry deadlines sit?
faqs.answer: Months. For the March 2027 series, Cambridge's own key dates show final entries due on 27 November 2026 for an exam period running 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February 2027, results on Cambridge Direct on 13 May and certificates in late June. Cambridge runs June and November series as well, plus Checkpoint tests in March, May and October for lower years. The practical point is that tier and subject decisions must be settled long before anyone feels exam pressure.

faqs.question: Why would our exam timetable differ from a cousin's in another country?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam because the wrong version was used. The same paper can therefore be sat at a different local time in two countries. Always work from the version your child's own exams officer issues, never from a timetable found online or shared by a relative abroad.

faqs.question: When do Pearson Edexcel results come out for each series?
faqs.answer: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. The January date is the one to check before entering a November retake, because it decides whether a result exists in time for an application deadline. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, and provisional means revisable, so plan from the version the school issues.

faqs.question: Why does this page not give any IB exam dates?
faqs.answer: Because none could be confirmed from an official source. The research behind this page could not verify an International Baccalaureate session or results date from the IB's own site, which blocks automated access, so publishing one would be guessing with a family's planning. Cambridge and Pearson dates are published by those boards and appear here with that attribution. For IB dates, ask your school's Diploma coordinator or check ibo.org directly, and treat any page quoting them with no source attached with caution.

faqs.question: Can a student take an IGCSE subject their school does not teach?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, through self-study and an external entry, and the order of operations decides whether it works. Ask whether the school will support an off-timetable entry at all. Find an approved exam centre that accepts external candidates. Confirm which components that centre can administer, because practical and speaking components are the usual constraint. Then check the entry deadline against the series calendar. The academic demand is also higher than families expect, so it suits one extra subject for a motivated student rather than a third science in a full year.

faqs.question: How much independent study should a Year 11 student be doing?
faqs.answer: The honest answer is that the number matters less than the method, and most households get the number roughly right and the method wrong. Three hours of copying out notes is visibly busy and returns very little; forty minutes of timed retrieval with self-marking returns considerably more. Rather than setting an hours target, audit one real week, see what the assumed hours are being spent on, and change the activity. Rewarding time at the desk over effective method reinforces exactly the habits that cost marks in the exam.

faqs.question: What can a parent usefully do if they do not know the subject?
faqs.answer: Four things, none of which needs subject knowledge. Ask to see marked work regularly, which creates mild and healthy accountability. Ask for the grouping of losses rather than the score, which trains the student to produce it. Protect one evening a week as slack, so the plan survives the first disruption. And keep every internal deadline, entry deadline, series date and results date in one visible place. For a commuting household, add a fifth: be the one who writes the specific written questions to the school.

faqs.question: Does living in Al Riqqa give us more study time than elsewhere in the emirate?
faqs.answer: Yes, measurably. This district sits closest to the Ajman border, so the cross-emirate run is the shortest in Umm Al Quwain and students are typically home earlier than peninsula families. That makes a full-length weekday session realistic and a more ambitious independent schedule workable. The advantage is only worth having if the hours get used well, which is the whole subject of this page; having the time and not converting it is more frustrating than not having it, and considerably more fixable.

faqs.question: Should sessions be used to work through questions together?
faqs.answer: Mostly no, and this is the main inefficiency in how tutoring is usually bought. Volume can be done independently once a student can self-mark, so paying for someone to sit through it is poor value. The division that works is volume outside the session and, inside it, the marking a student cannot do alone, chiefly extended written answers, plus analysis of what that marking revealed. That buys fewer paid hours for more progress, and it leaves the student able to work without the tutor.

faqs.question: What if the second marked paper shows no improvement at all?
faqs.answer: Then the diagnosis was wrong and it is the diagnosis that should change rather than the hours that get doubled. Grouping the losses exists precisely so that question can be answered with evidence instead of impressions. Sometimes the first grouping identified a real weakness that was not the binding one; sometimes the pairing is not working and a different specialist is the answer. Either way the decision belongs at the end of the block, not deferred to results day when nothing can be done about it.

umm-al-quwain/al-riqqa.closingHeading: Send a marked paper and the real arrival time, and we will start there
umm-al-quwain/al-riqqa.closingBody: From Al Riqqa the hours exist; the question is what they are being spent on. Send the board, the syllabus code, the tier where one applies, one recent marked paper rather than a report grade, and the honest time your child gets home after the Ajman or Sharjah run. The first lesson is free, taught online one to one over live video, and it produces a grouping of the losses into content, method presentation, command-term response and pacing. Those four need different responses, and knowing which one you have is worth more than another term of general support.

umm-al-quwain/al-salamah.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE and the IB Diploma and Middle Years Programme. Each works with one student at a time, and the number of sessions is proposed from a diagnosis rather than from a package tier.

intro.heading: Nobody in this market will tell you what tutoring costs, so here it is
paragraphs: Al Salamah is the broad residential district that holds much of Umm Al Quwain's modern housing, inland from the old harbour town. Households here are doing the same arithmetic as everyone else in the emirate: school outside the emirate, a long daily run, and a tutoring decision taken under a budget that already has school fees in it. What makes that decision harder than it should be is that the market refuses to publish numbers.

The research behind this page examined the pages currently ranking for tutoring queries across the UAE. Three of the six leading pages publish no price at all; one of them has a frequently asked question that asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer it. The two that do publish quote in United States dollars, a currency no family in Umm Al Quwain transacts in. The practical effect is that a parent cannot tell whether a quoted figure is high, low or absurd until they have made six phone calls.

So this page publishes the ranges. They are market rates read in October 2026 from provider pages and published rate trackers, and they are presented as the market rather than as our prices, because a figure that is not attributed to somebody is worth nothing. Where a number could not be verified it is left out: there is a fine schedule circulating for unlicensed tutoring, for example, that no official source publishes, so it does not appear here.

The second half of the problem is that the hourly rate is the wrong thing to optimise. Two subjects supported weekly for two years costs several times what one subject supported properly for a term does, and the second is more often what was actually needed. A diagnosis that says four sessions and a review is a cheaper product than an open-ended booking at a lower rate, and it is the one that moves a grade.

There is a third factor specific to this emirate. Umm Al Quwain has limited international school provision, so students travel to Ajman, Sharjah or Ras Al Khaimah, and the evening left at the end of that journey is short. A cheap session at a time the student cannot use is not cheap. Any honest cost conversation here includes session length and timing, not only the per-hour figure.

One more framing point before the numbers. A tutoring bill is not a fee for attendance; it is a payment for a change in a mark. That makes it the only line in an education budget with a measurable outcome attached, and the only one a family can honestly audit. Marked work at the start, marked work at the end, and a decision in between is what turns a recurring cost into a finished piece of work.

What follows is the full picture: the market ranges by provider model, the variables that move a quote up or down, where tutoring sits against school fees and exam entry costs, how group formats change the per-student number, the extras to ask about before paying anything, and what a legitimate invoice and permit position look like.

umm-al-quwain/al-salamah.programmesIntro: Cost differs by programme more than most families expect, because the work differs. A terminal-exam course and a coursework-heavy one need different numbers of hours in different parts of the year.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE
programmes.description: Eight to ten externally examined subjects at the end of Year 11, with Cambridge using four-digit codes and Core and Extended tiering in several subjects, and Pearson Edexcel using its own series. Support is typically concentrated in Year 11 and in two or three subjects rather than spread across the whole timetable, which is where families overspend.
programmes.countryNote: Market rates quoted for IGCSE sit at the lower end of the published bands, with one UAE provider advertising IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200 as of October 2026. For an Al Salamah family the more useful question is how many subjects genuinely need support, because three subjects at a modest rate costs more than one subject at a higher one.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across Higher and Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessments are produced outside lesson time, so demand for support clusters around coursework deadlines rather than around exams, which changes when money is spent as well as how much.
programmes.countryNote: Published rate trackers put specialist exam-year support at roughly AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more a month for weekly sessions, read October 2026. A Diploma family in this emirate should budget for coursework blocks in Year 12 as well as revision in Year 13, because the pattern of leaving it all to the final year costs more and achieves less.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria each and reported as criterion levels. Support here is usually cheapest and most effective because it is about habits rather than content: how method and reflection are written, which is what the criteria reward and what later Diploma internal assessments will demand.
programmes.countryNote: This is the stage where a small amount of spending has the longest payback, and it is the stage families skip. A short block in the Middle Years on criterion-based writing costs a fraction of an emergency Diploma coursework intervention three years later and removes much of the need for it.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: Three or four externally examined subjects with no central core and a modular structure that differs between boards. Spending here is concentrated in revision and exam technique rather than coursework, and the modular pattern means a banked result can remove a subject from the budget part-way through.
programmes.countryNote: For a household on a fixed-term posting the modular structure has a financial advantage worth knowing: results banked earlier reduce the exposure if the family relocates mid-course. That is a planning point rather than an academic one, but in this emirate fixed-term postings are common enough to matter.

umm-al-quwain/al-salamah.subjectsIntro: Subjects differ in how many hours they need to move a grade, which is the real driver of cost. Each note says what the hours are actually buying.

subjects.name: Mathematics (IGCSE 0580 and 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The best value subject to support, because fluency responds to volume and volume can be set as homework. A tutor who assigns thirty mixed multi-stage questions a week and marks a sample is buying more improvement per dirham than one who works through examples in the session.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Among the most expensive subjects to support properly, because Higher Level problem solving needs long sessions and a genuine specialist. Published premium rates for named specialists reach AED 500 to 650 and above, though a qualified subject tutor in the 150 to 300 band covers most students' needs.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0625 and 4PH1
subjects.description: Needs fewer hours than families expect once the real problem is identified, because the usual weakness is choosing between energy, momentum and force approaches rather than missing content. That is a technique fix of a handful of sessions, not a term of teaching.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0620 and 4CH1
subjects.description: Two separate cost centres: the written papers and the internal assessment. The internal assessment block is finite and tied to a deadline, which makes it the easier of the two to budget, and it is often where the recoverable marks are concentrated.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0610 and 4BI1
subjects.description: Cheap to improve and routinely over-supported. Most of the available gain is in matching answers to command terms and in data-based questions on unfamiliar experiments, both of which are short pieces of work rather than ongoing weekly commitments.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Benefits from frequency rather than duration, so two short slots a week usually cost the same as one hour and achieve more. The marks are in register and task fulfilment, which respond to marked timed writing rather than to discussion.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: The clearest case for splitting an hour, because vocabulary retention drives the grade and retention follows frequency. A long weekly session is poor value here compared with two short ones, whatever the rate.

subjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0450 and 0455
subjects.description: Evaluation marks at the end of long questions are the most commonly abandoned on the paper and the cheapest to recover, because they are a structural habit. Content support in these subjects is usually the more expensive and less productive option.

subjects.name: Coursework and internal assessment support
subjects.description: Finite, deadline-bound and therefore budgetable: a defined block ending at submission rather than an open commitment. A tutor teaches the criteria and responds to the student's own draft; nothing is produced for the student at any price.

subjects.name: Exam technique and paper management
subjects.description: The highest return per dirham of any support available and almost never sold as a product. Pacing, question selection and marks-per-minute discipline are visible on a mock script and fixable in a few sessions, with gains across every subject at once.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.levels: IB HL and SL, IGCSE 0460 and 0470
subjects.description: Essay and source planning rather than more content is the efficient spend. Planning five essays in an hour teaches more about argument than writing one does, which also means fewer paid hours are needed to change the grade.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Variable in cost because prior programming exposure varies enormously between schools. A diagnostic session first is worth more here than in any other subject, because the gap could be two sessions or two terms and nobody can tell from a report.

modes.title: One to one, by the session
modes.description: The most expensive per hour and the only format that can work on one student's specific weakness in one paper of one syllabus. Worth paying for where the problem has been diagnosed and is individual. Market rates for a qualified online subject tutor sat at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour in October 2026, with premium named specialists published considerably higher.

It fails quietly when the students are not aligned, and the saving then buys a session that helps neither of them.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges, by provider model
paragraphs: The table below is the thing the leading pages in this market do not publish. It is built from rates read in October 2026 on UAE provider pages and from a published Dubai tutoring cost tracker, and it is organised by provider model rather than by brand, because the model is what determines the price. All of it is market context; none of it is an IB Gram price list, and a current quote should be asked for directly.

The bands overlap for a reason. A university student with a private tuition work permit and a strong grade in the subject genuinely can teach a Year 10 student well, and the low band reflects that. A specialist who teaches one Higher Level course full time across multiple exam series is doing a different job, and the upper bands reflect that too. The error families make is assuming the bands correspond to quality in a linear way; they correspond to scarcity and to the specificity of the match.

The in-home band is inflated by travel and should be read that way. A tutor pricing a visit into Umm Al Quwain is covering a round trip from Sharjah or Ajman around a one-hour lesson, and the rate reflects that whether or not it is itemised. Families who want to understand what they are paying for should ask what the rate would be for the same tutor teaching the same hour remotely.

Monthly package figures advertised in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four in-home double sessions. A rate tracker's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

sections.heading: What actually moves a quote up or down
paragraphs: Parents often assume the rate is set by the provider's brand, and it is mostly set by eight variables that have nothing to do with branding. Knowing them means a quote can be interrogated rather than accepted, and in several cases a family can change the number by changing the request rather than the supplier.

Scarcity is the biggest driver. A Higher Level Diploma specialist in a narrow subject commands more than an IGCSE mathematics tutor because the pool is smaller, and the same subject at a popular late-evening slot commands more than at a quiet one. In this emirate that matters directly: the hours a commuting household needs are late, which is the most contested part of the day nationally.

The second is proximity to the exam. Demand rises through the spring term, so a family that arranges support in October is buying in a looser market than one arranging it in March. Session length and frequency also move the number, usually sub-linearly, which means a ninety-minute session rarely costs double a forty-five minute one even though some providers price it that way.

The variables worth negotiating are not the obvious ones. Asking for a cheaper tutor usually buys a worse match. Asking for a shorter session at a quieter hour, a finite block instead of an open commitment, or a pair arrangement with another student on the same syllabus and tier can lower the total meaningfully without lowering the quality of the match.

sections.heading: Tutoring against the rest of the education bill
paragraphs: A tutoring rate read on its own is meaningless. Read next to the other numbers a family in this emirate pays, it is clearly a small share of total education spend and a large share of the discretionary part, which is exactly why it deserves scrutiny rather than either dismissal or panic.

School fees dominate everywhere. For context from the country's largest private market, Dubai's regulator confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a total of AED 2.5 billion. Fees for Al Salamah families are set by the regulator of whichever emirate the school sits in: the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge both approve tuition fees in their emirates.

The second large line for a household in this emirate is transport, and it is the one most often excluded from the comparison. A cross-emirate bus place or a daily private-car run to Sharjah is a real annual cost, and it also consumes the evening that tutoring has to fit into, which is a second cost paid in a different currency. Any honest budget conversation here puts those two lines next to each other.

Exam entry fees are the third. They are set by the centre rather than by any national schedule, vary by board and subject, and are usually bundled into school fees for internal candidates but charged separately for private candidates. No reliable single figure exists to publish, so the right action is to ask the exams officer or the centre directly rather than to rely on any number found online, including on competing pages that publish one.

sections.heading: When a pair or a small group is genuinely cheaper
paragraphs: Group formats are the obvious way to lower the per-student cost and they work under conditions narrow enough that they are worth stating before anyone tries. The saving is real when the conditions hold and entirely illusory when they do not, because a session pitched between two misaligned students teaches neither of them.

The conditions are three. The same syllabus, including the same board and the same code. The same tier or level, because a Core-tier and an Extended-tier student are sitting different papers. And a genuinely similar current position, which means similar recent marked work rather than similar school year. Two Year 11 students both entered for Cambridge 0580 Extended with comparable mock profiles can work together productively; two siblings two years apart cannot.

Where the conditions hold, the pedagogy is better than families expect. Explaining a method to a peer is one of the strongest tests of recall available, and a student who has to articulate why a step works finds out quickly whether they know it. A pair also sustains pace in a way a one-to-one session sometimes does not, because neither student wants to be the one holding it up.

Where they do not hold, the better economy is sequencing. Support one child or one subject properly for a block, finish it, then move to the next. That forces an uncomfortable decision about priority and is almost always clarifying, and it costs less over a year than two thin arrangements running in parallel.

sections.heading: Extras, conditions and the questions to ask before paying
paragraphs: The headline rate is the beginning of the cost, and the differences between providers show up in the conditions rather than the number. These are the questions worth asking before any money moves, and a provider who answers them crisply is describing a process rather than improvising.

Ask whether the price is per hour or per lesson, because a fifty-minute lesson billed as an hour is a ten per cent difference nobody mentions. Ask what happens to a cancelled session and how much notice is required, which matters enormously in a household whose evening depends on a cross-emirate journey. Ask whether session notes, marked work and worked solutions are included or extra. Ask what a replacement costs if the match is wrong.

Ask about anything described as free. A trial lesson, an assessment or a first month described as free should come with its conditions stated on the same screen: how long, who is eligible, whether a card is required, and what happens at the end of it. A condition that only appears later is the single most common complaint in this market and it is entirely avoidable.

On tax, ask the one question that can be answered: does the quoted dirham figure include VAT, and does the provider hold a tax registration number. The VAT treatment of private tuition in the UAE depends on Federal Tax Authority rules and is not something this page states as fact; confirm it with the authority or a tax adviser rather than with a tutoring provider's marketing page.

sections.heading: Paying for a diagnosis before paying for hours
paragraphs: The largest avoidable cost in this market is not the rate; it is buying the wrong product. A family sees a disappointing grade, books general weekly support in that subject, and pays for a term of competent teaching that addresses something other than the actual problem. The grade moves little, everyone concludes tutoring does not work, and the money is gone.

A diagnosis first changes the purchase. One marked paper, read properly, distinguishes a content gap from a technique habit, and those two need completely different and differently priced interventions. A content gap across several topics is a weekly commitment through a term. A technique habit, such as missing interpretation sentences or answering description where explanation was asked, is four to six sessions and then done.

Most families who ask for a year need a block. That is an uncomfortable thing for a provider to say and it is the honest answer in the majority of cases, which is why the trial lesson here ends with a written number rather than a recommendation to continue indefinitely. If the number is four, it says four, and the block ends with a second marked piece so the result is visible as a mark.

The corollary is that a provider who proposes a long commitment before seeing any marked work is guessing, however reasonable the rate. The question to put to any provider is simple: what will you look at before telling me how many sessions we need? A good answer names a document. A poor one names a package.

sections.heading: What a free trial should and should not be
paragraphs: A free first lesson is standard across this market and the quality of it varies more than the rates do. At its best it is a diagnostic session that produces a document. At its worst it is a sales meeting with a whiteboard, where a tutor is pleasant, the student is reassured, and nothing specific is identified, after which a package is proposed.

The test is what the family holds at the end. A useful trial produces a written note naming the specific gap, the criterion or command term behind it where relevant, what was attempted in the session and how the student responded, and a recommended number of sessions with a reason. That document is useful even if the family never books anything, which is the point: it is a service rather than a pitch.

There are things a trial should not do. It should not spend its time establishing rapport at the expense of looking at work; rapport develops over sessions and diagnosis does not. It should not conclude that everything is fine, because then there was nothing to diagnose and the family should be told to save their money. And it should not be free in a way that has conditions nobody mentioned, such as a card requirement or an automatic enrolment.

Bring the marked work. A trial lesson given a recent marked script and a one-line note from the parent about the pattern they noticed is worth roughly three times one given nothing, and the parent's observation is often the right one. Nobody sees a child's work more often than the person who signs the homework diary.

sections.heading: Permits, invoices and what a legitimate arrangement looks like
paragraphs: Price and legitimacy are connected, because the cheapest end of this market is also where the permit question is most often skipped. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, so cost is not a reason for anyone to be without one.

The eligible categories are wide and include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. MoHRE's own service listing is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fee stated and a two working day completion time, applied for through the smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no amounts are published, so quoted figures should be treated with suspicion.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a separate case and needs its own educational services permit from the relevant authority, with an initial approval stage and annual renewal. An individual's permit does not cover a centre, and a centre's permit does not make its tutors individually licensed. Asking which document a provider holds is a fair question and the answer tells you what kind of organisation you are dealing with.

Nothing here is a regulator endorsement. No education authority in the UAE accredits tutoring providers, so phrases implying regulator approval should be read as a warning rather than a credential. What exists is a permit, and a legitimate tutor or provider can show it alongside a clear invoice that states what was delivered, over what period, and whether the amount includes VAT.

sections.heading: Fitting the budget to the slot Al Salamah actually has
paragraphs: A cost plan in this emirate that ignores the timetable will not survive contact with it. Most secondary-age students from Al Salamah travel out of the emirate for school, so the evening is short, and a session bought at a time the student cannot reliably use is money spent on absences. The sensible order is to fix the slot, then choose the format, then look at the rate.

The arithmetic starts from the real arrival time, including bus stops, which is usually later than a parent's estimate. From there, a short weekday session with a single objective is the format that holds, with long work moved to a weekend morning when the student is rested and the commute is not in the way. That combination also tends to cost less than two long weekday sessions, because it buys fewer total hours and uses them better.

Cancellation policy matters more here than elsewhere for the same reason. A household whose evening depends on a cross-emirate journey will lose sessions occasionally, and the difference between a provider who reschedules and one who charges is a real annual number. Ask about it before the first payment rather than after the first missed lesson.

The last point is about stopping. A plan reviewed every half term against marked work and ended when it has done its work costs a fraction of one that runs by default until results day. In a household where both money and evenings are scarce, a session that is no longer needed is costing twice.

faqs.question: What does an IB or IGCSE tutor cost per hour for an Al Salamah family?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 run roughly from AED 33 to AED 150 an hour for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180 to AED 500 for in-home visits once travel is built in, AED 200 to AED 450 and above for IB and IGCSE specialists, and AED 500 to AED 650 and above for premium named or examiner-marketed tutors. One UAE provider advertises IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Those are market figures rather than our prices; ask us directly for a current quote.

faqs.question: Why do most tutoring websites refuse to publish a price?
faqs.answer: Because quoting a number invites comparison and because the real figure depends on scarcity, level, slot and format. The research behind this page found three of the six leading pages in this market publish no price at all, with one posing the question in its own frequently asked questions and then declining to answer it, and the two that do publish quoting in United States dollars. The practical cost to a parent is six phone calls before they can tell whether a quote is reasonable, which is why the ranges appear here instead.

faqs.question: Is the hourly rate the number we should be comparing?
faqs.answer: No. Duration controls the total far more than the rate does: two subjects supported weekly for two years costs several times what one subject supported properly for a term does, and the second is more often what was needed. A higher rate with a diagnosis and a four-session block is usually cheaper in total than a lower rate with an open commitment nobody reviews. Compare the proposed number of sessions and the basis for it, then compare rates within that.

faqs.question: What makes one tutor cost twice as much as another?
faqs.answer: Mostly scarcity and specificity rather than general quality. A Higher Level specialist in a narrow Diploma subject commands more because very few people teach it; a popular late-evening slot commands more than a quiet afternoon one; demand rises through the spring term as exams approach. In-home rates carry a round trip inside them. Premium positioning adds a further layer, and where a tutor is described as an examiner it is reasonable to ask what evidence supports the claim before paying for it.

faqs.question: Can we lower the cost without accepting a worse tutor?
faqs.answer: Yes, by changing the request rather than the supplier. Ask for a shorter weekday session with one objective plus a single weekend block instead of two long weekday hours. Offer a quieter slot where you can. Agree a finite block with a session count and an end date rather than an open commitment. If another student is on the same board, the same code, the same tier and at a genuinely similar point, a pair arrangement lowers the per-student cost without diluting the match.

faqs.question: How much do school fees and transport change the picture?
faqs.answer: They dominate it. Fees are the largest line and are approved by the regulator of the emirate the school sits in, so a Sharjah school's fees are approved by the Sharjah Private Education Authority and a Ras Al Khaimah school's by the Department of Knowledge. For context from the largest market, Dubai's regulator confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no fee increase for 2026-27. For this emirate, cross-emirate transport is the second standing line and it also consumes the evening tutoring has to fit into, which is a second cost in a different currency.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to enter one IGCSE exam?
faqs.answer: There is no national schedule to quote, which is why no honest figure appears here. Entry fees are set by the exam centre, vary by board and subject, and are usually bundled into school fees for internal candidates while being charged separately for private candidates. Ask your child's exams officer or the centre directly for the current figure for the specific subjects and series. Any page publishing a single number for this is either quoting one centre without saying so or has invented it.

faqs.question: When does a pair or group session actually save money?
faqs.answer: When three conditions hold: the same syllabus including board and code, the same tier or level, and a genuinely similar current position based on recent marked work rather than school year. Two Year 11 students both entered for Cambridge 0580 Extended with comparable mocks can work well together, and explaining to a peer is a strong test of recall. Siblings two years apart on different courses cannot share usefully, and the apparent saving buys a session that helps neither of them.

faqs.question: What should we ask about before paying anything?
faqs.answer: Five things. Whether the price is per hour or per lesson, and how long a lesson actually is. The cancellation notice required and what happens to a missed session, which matters a great deal when your evening depends on a cross-emirate journey. Whether session notes, marked work and worked solutions are included. What a replacement tutor costs if the match is wrong. And whether the quoted dirham figure includes VAT and whether the provider holds a tax registration number.

faqs.question: Does tuition in the UAE have VAT on it?
faqs.answer: That depends on Federal Tax Authority rules and is not something a tutoring page should state as fact, so this page does not. What you can and should ask any provider is narrower and answerable: does the quoted dirham figure include VAT, and does the provider hold a tax registration number. If the tax treatment itself matters to your household, confirm it with the Federal Tax Authority or a tax adviser rather than with a provider's marketing material.

faqs.question: Is anything described as a free trial genuinely free?
faqs.answer: It should be, and the conditions should appear on the same screen as the word. Ask how long the trial is, who is eligible, whether a card is required, and what happens at the end of it. A condition that only surfaces afterwards is the most common complaint in this market and entirely avoidable. A good trial is also a service rather than a pitch: it should end with a written note naming the specific gap and a recommended session count, useful to you even if you never book.

faqs.question: Why insist on seeing marked work before quoting a number of sessions?
faqs.answer: Because a marked paper distinguishes the two problems that look identical from outside and cost very different amounts. If losses cluster in one or two topics it is a content gap, which is a weekly commitment through a term. If losses are spread thinly as half-earned questions across the whole paper, it is a technique habit, which is four to six sessions and then finished. A provider proposing a long commitment before seeing any work is guessing, however reasonable their rate.

faqs.question: Do cheaper tutors still need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the permit is free, so cost is not a reason for anyone to lack one. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include school and government teachers, public and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to wait until the term before the exams?
faqs.answer: Almost never. Demand and therefore rates rise through the spring term, availability of specialists in narrow subjects narrows, and the late-evening slots this emirate needs are the first to go. More importantly, the work that moves a grade most, namely technique repair and coursework support, takes weeks to produce a result and cannot be compressed into the final fortnight. Arranging in October buys a looser market, a better match and more time, usually for fewer total hours.

faqs.question: At what point should an Al Salamah family stop buying sessions?
faqs.answer: Set the review date in advance and use marked work rather than impressions. A block should end with a second marked piece so the result is a mark, and a weekly arrangement should be reviewed every half term against the grade the student started at. If the mark has moved and the gap has closed, stop. If it has not moved, the diagnosis was wrong and the response is to change it rather than add hours. Support that runs by default until results day is the most expensive product available.

umm-al-quwain/best-ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: The profiles below name the subject, the level and the components each tutor works on, plus the boards whose papers they have marked. Those are the attributes a parent can test. A free trial session comes before any figure is discussed, and the honest measure of the match is the marked piece of work it produces rather than how the conversation felt.

intro.heading: Translate the word into things you can check
paragraphs: No regulator, board or authority in this country publishes a ranked list of private tutors. There is no register of quality, no inspection band for individuals, and nothing a parent can look up to settle the question. Every site telling you it has the finest IB tutors is making an unverifiable assertion, and several of the pages competing for this exact search back it with statistics that have no sample size, star ratings they awarded themselves, and in two documented cases figures that contradict each other on the same page.

That does not make the question meaningless. It means the word has to be converted into testable attributes before it is useful. Does this tutor work on the component my child is losing marks on, at the right level. Has the person actually applied a markscheme to papers from the right board. Are they legally permitted to take payment for lessons in this country. Will the first session produce something in writing that I keep. Does the provider state what happens when no specialist is available, or do they discover that in week three and improvise.

Delivery first, as on every page in this set. IB Gram provides tuition to Umm Al Quwain as one-to-one lessons over live video. There are no home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service. For the question of quality this is the central fact rather than a disclaimer, because in the least populous emirate in the country the pool of people who can teach Chemistry HL and happen to live within driving distance is close to empty. A family insisting on somebody at the table is, in practice, choosing a generalist. A family willing to use a screen is choosing from everyone.

The second thing this page does is put rates and capability side by side. A Diploma hour in this market can be bought for AED 45 or for AED 650, and both figures are published by real providers. The spread is not arbitrary, but neither is it a quality scale you can read off a price list. Somewhere in the middle, the correlation between price and capability breaks down entirely, and knowing where that happens is worth more than any shortlist.

Third, it names the claims that should end a conversation. Regulator accreditation nobody holds. A school presented as a client. An offer to supply a finished internal assessment, which is a malpractice exposure for your child rather than a service. A phone number in another country as the only route to a human. Prices in dollars or pounds on a page written for UAE parents. Each of those appears somewhere in the pages ranking for these searches today.

Finally it gives you the test that actually settles the matter, which is not a reputation but a six-week comparison of two dated marked pieces of work on the same question types. That is cheap, it is unambiguous, and no amount of marketing survives it.
