sections.heading: Permits, VAT and what a free trial has to mean
paragraphs: Three consumer questions sit underneath every tutoring quote in this country, and all three have clear answers.

On permits: private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount appears here. A permit is free, which means a tutor who cites permit costs as a reason for a higher rate is telling you something useful.

There is also a professional-conduct point that affects who you can legitimately hire. Press reporting on Abu Dhabi indicates that ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Hiring your child's own classroom teacher privately is therefore not the shortcut it appears to be, and this should be checked against the current policy document rather than treated as settled wording.

On VAT: the UAE tax treatment of tuition fees is not something this page states as fact, because doing so would need a Federal Tax Authority citation. What a family should do instead is ask any provider a direct question: is the figure you have quoted inclusive of VAT, and do you hold a tax registration number. A provider who cannot answer that plainly has told you what you need to know.

On free trials: a trial is only free if the condition is on the same screen as the word. Length, eligibility and whether card details are required, stated up front. Our trial is a working session that produces a piece of marked work or a scoped plan, with no card required to book it, and the figure for ongoing sessions is given afterwards rather than before, because before the session nobody knows honestly what the plan should be.

sections.heading: When to spend, and when to stop
paragraphs: The last section of a cost page should say when to close the wallet, because every provider has an incentive not to.

Spend early. Phases one to four carry the value, and they are the phases families underfund because the pressure is not visible yet. A diagnostic block in the first term of DP1 and a scoped core block in DP2 together cost less than six weeks of three-subject panic in the spring, and they move more.

Stop when the evidence stops moving. Six weeks of flat results on the specific question types a plan named is not a reason to buy more hours; it is a reason to change the diagnosis or the tutor. Stop also when a student has become able to mark their own work against a markscheme and plan their own revision. That is the point of the exercise, and continuing past it converts a tutor into a comfort purchase.

Do not spend against a narrow slot you cannot fill. If the only time your family can manage is the single most contested hour of the week, and the specialist you need is not free in it, the cheapest honest answer is to move the time rather than to accept whoever is available. Coverage is not unlimited, and a narrow Higher Level combination in one fixed slot sometimes has no match that week. You will be told that, with a different time, an adjacent specialist or a date, rather than being sold a generalist described as a specialist.

Finally, spend on the thing you can audit. An hour that returns a marked script with the markscheme reference attached is worth more at any rate than two hours of unrecorded company, and the question that separates the two is the same one every time: what will this session produce in writing, and do we keep it.

process.title: Say which phase you are in
process.description: DP1 diagnostic, DP1 habit building, internal assessment block, core supervision or final stretch. The phase decides the format, the scope and the realistic cost more than the subject does, and naming it in the enquiry removes a whole round of questions before anyone is matched.

process.title: Send the coordinator's deadline sheet
process.description: The dates that drive Diploma spending are set by the school, not the board. With the internal deadlines in front of us the support can be bought once and in time, rather than twice and in a hurry. For families schooled in another emirate this single document saves more money than any rate negotiation.

process.title: Take the trial before discussing a figure
process.description: A working session over live video that produces a marked piece of work or a scoped plan. No card details to book it. Our own rate is quoted afterwards, because the honest number depends on the component, the level and how many weeks are left, and quoting it beforehand would be a guess dressed as a price.

process.title: Scope the block, and name the finish line
process.description: For internal assessment and core work, agree a defined number of sessions against one submission date. For weekly subject support, agree the target question types and the review date. A block with a finish line is the part of a Diploma budget that does not quietly expand across two years.

process.title: Review at six weeks and decide
process.description: Three honest outcomes: continue because the targeted marks moved, change the tutor or the targets because they did not, or stop because the student now works independently. The review is a decision point with evidence on the table, which is what stops a tutoring arrangement becoming a standing order.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries its source
whyPoints.description: The dirham bands on this page are published market rates with the publisher named, not an invented price list and not a competitor's number repeated as ours. Where our own cost is concerned the answer is the trial session and the consultation, because the real number depends on the component and the weeks remaining.

whyPoints.title: No travel inside the hour
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video. In-home rates in the published data sit above online rates because somebody pays for the drive, and to this emirate that drive is long. Removing the format removes the line item rather than discounting it, and widens the specialist pool at the same time.

whyPoints.title: Priced by phase, not by a flat rate
whyPoints.description: A diagnostic block in DP1, a scoped internal assessment block, a core supervision block and a tightly limited final stretch. Families who buy in that order spend less and move more than families who buy an even weekly commitment for two years and then run short in April.

whyPoints.title: Core supervision treated as the best value, not the afterthought
whyPoints.description: Up to three Diploma points sit in the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combination, and most families fund it last. Scoped supervision against the criteria, with the student writing every sentence, is the cheapest point movement on the whole programme.

whyPoints.title: Authorship boundaries stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: The student writes every sentence of assessed work, drafts are dated, and no replacement text is ever supplied. One provider in this market sells finished internal assessments outright. Naming that boundary in writing is both the rule and a genuine difference in this particular search result.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are disclosed up front
whyPoints.description: When no specialist is free for a narrow Higher Level combination in a single fixed evening slot, you are told, with an alternative time, an adjacent specialist or a date. Paying a specialist rate for a generalist is the most expensive mistake available in this market.

faqs.question: What does a full two-year IB Diploma tutoring plan cost from Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: There is no single figure, and any provider offering one before seeing the student is guessing. What can be given is the shape. Published market bands put an IB specialist at roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour and above, with monthly patterns in this market around AED 799 for eight online sessions. A sensible two-year plan is not weekly support for twenty-four months; it is a diagnostic block in DP1, one or two subjects weekly while habits form, a scoped internal assessment block per subject, a core supervision block, and a limited final stretch. Budget by phase and the total is far smaller.

faqs.question: Is it cheaper to buy Diploma support in DP1 or wait until DP2?
faqs.answer: DP1, decisively. The hourly rate is the same but the value is not. In DP1 there is time for a habit to form, so a procedural fix such as writing method steps or planning extended responses pays off across eighteen months of assessment. In the spring of DP2 the constraint has shifted from understanding to available time, and the same hour buys triage rather than teaching. Families who spread spending evenly across two years consistently find themselves funding the least efficient phase most heavily, and cutting something that was working in order to afford it.

faqs.question: How many of the 45 points can money realistically move?
faqs.answer: Honestly, nobody can put a number on it, and anyone who does is making a claim they cannot support. What can be said is which components respond. Technique components move fastest: timed paper method, command-term discipline, calculator and graph work, structured evaluation. Internal assessments respond to supervision, never to purchase. Up to three points sit in the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combination and respond well to criterion-referenced questioning. Unstudied syllabus content in a subject with no work happening between sessions barely responds at all, because the missing resource is study time rather than teaching.

faqs.question: What does internal assessment supervision add to the bill?
faqs.answer: It is best bought as a scoped block rather than as open weekly support: a defined number of sessions against one submission date, per subject. Scoped that way it is a modest, predictable line and one of the better-value items on a Diploma budget, because internal assessment marks are a fixed share of the grade and are settled inside the school year. Left until the coordinator's deadline is three weeks away, the same work costs more and achieves less, because the sessions become rescue rather than development. Get the deadline sheet in September and book the block against it.

faqs.question: Why is a Diploma hour priced above an IGCSE hour?
faqs.answer: Partly content and partly supply. Diploma Higher Level courses go deeper and carry components such as an extra paper of extended problem-solving, so the tutor pool capable of teaching them is smaller. Unitors, for example, publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200, which reflects that difference in the market rather than a view about difficulty. Supply pressure is sharpest in a few subjects: Computer Science HL and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL sit near the top of the band across the UAE because few specialists are available, not because the hour contains more teaching.

faqs.question: Does an IB Diploma tutor here come to the house, and what would that add?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. There are no home visits in the UAE; it is a service offered only in India, and tuition to every emirate is delivered one-to-one over live video. On the market generally, published data puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 500 an hour against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and the difference is the drive. To Falaj Al Mualla or Al Riqqa that approach is long, so the premium is larger here than in Dubai. Choosing live video removes the component rather than negotiating it down.

faqs.question: What does the evening slot scarcity in this emirate do to the rate?
faqs.answer: It does not raise the published rate so much as reduce the choice available at it. Almost every Diploma candidate living here is schooled in Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah and gets home late, so demand concentrates into roughly ninety minutes of weekday evening. That band is contested, and the specialists with options are often booked in it. Families flexible enough to take a weekend morning for the long session, or a 17:30 start where the commute allows, get better availability for the same money. It is the cheapest change most households here could make.

faqs.question: Are Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay worth paying a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Per point available, they are the best value on the programme and the item most families fund last. The two together contribute up to three points to the Diploma total, which is frequently the gap between an offer and a near miss. Support is supervision rather than teaching: questioning the claim, naming the criterion, identifying what the descriptor asks for that is missing, and sending the student back to write it themselves. Scoped as a block across DP2 it is a small line. What it must never be is anyone other than the candidate producing the words on the page.

faqs.question: What are the costs nobody quotes until results day?
faqs.answer: Board fees for enquiries upon results, remarks and retake entries, none of which appear in a tutoring quote. A retake also means a second preparation period with its own cost. Private-candidate entries, where a student sits a subject the school does not offer, carry entry fees and have to be arranged through a centre that accepts private candidates, which from here usually means Sharjah or Ajman. Add exam-day travel to a centre in another emirate across several weeks, a calculator model change if the school requires one, and university admissions test and application fees landing in the same months.

faqs.question: How does a year of weekly Diploma support compare with school fees?
faqs.answer: For most families at an international school, a year of weekly support on one subject is a modest fraction of the annual fee bill, and a scoped core block is smaller still. The scale context is worth having: Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no fee increase for Dubai private schools in 2026-27. Where the comparison breaks down is three subjects weekly through the whole of DP2, which is a different order of commitment and usually a symptom of earlier underspending.

faqs.question: Should we buy a block of sessions or pay week by week?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the sessions are for. Internal assessment and core work should be bought as a block, because the work has a submission date and a finish line, and a block with a scope does not quietly expand. Weekly subject support is better paid as you go, because the aim is to become unnecessary and a prepaid term removes the incentive to notice when that has happened. If you do buy a block in this emirate, ask what happens to unused sessions when the school moves its mock window, since the school calendar belongs to another emirate entirely.

faqs.question: Does a higher hourly rate buy a better Diploma grade?
faqs.answer: Not reliably, and nobody can promise a grade at any price. What a higher rate usually buys is narrower specialism: somebody who works on that exact component at that exact level, rather than a generalist covering four subjects. For Higher Level work and for internal assessment supervision that specialism matters, and the cheapest tiers, from around AED 45 to 65, generally buy homework company instead. The useful test is not the rate but the output: what will the first session produce in writing, which markscheme was applied, and do we keep the script.

faqs.question: Is VAT included in the figures quoted on tutoring sites?
faqs.answer: Often unstated, and this page will not assert the UAE tax treatment of tuition fees as fact, because doing so would require a Federal Tax Authority citation. The practical move is to ask the provider two direct questions before paying: is this figure inclusive of VAT, and do you hold a tax registration number. The market bands quoted on this page are published rates from the sources named and should be treated as indicative rather than as final invoices. A provider who cannot answer either question plainly has given you useful information about their operation.

faqs.question: What has to be true before a trial session counts as free?
faqs.answer: The conditions have to appear next to the word. How long the session is, who is eligible, whether card details are required to book, and what happens if you do not continue. A trial advertised as free with a card requirement buried a page away is not free in the sense a parent reads it. Ours is a working session over live video, booked without card details, which produces a marked piece of work or a scoped plan. The figure for ongoing sessions is given after it rather than before, because beforehand nobody honestly knows what the plan should be.

faqs.question: How many subjects should we fund at once in the Diploma?
faqs.answer: One or two, almost always. Three weekly subjects is a budget shape that signals the diagnosis was never done: in most cases one subject is genuinely weak, one is a technique problem that is cheap to fix, and the others are suffering from time pressure created by the first two. Funding all of them at specialist rates spreads the money thin and leaves nothing for the internal assessment and core blocks, which carry better value. Fix the technique problem first, since it is fast and visible, then reassess what is actually left.

faqs.question: At what point in DP2 does extra spending stop helping?
faqs.answer: Once the constraint becomes available time rather than understanding, which for most candidates is somewhere after the mock examinations. From that point an additional hour competes with revision the student needs to do alone, and adding a third or fourth subject to the plan reliably makes the whole thing worse. The final stretch is best kept to two subjects, tightly scoped to timed-paper technique on the question types a marked script has identified. Spending heavily here to compensate for a thin DP1 is the most expensive pattern in the programme and the least effective.

umm-al-quwain/ib-diploma-tutor.closingHeading: Budget the Diploma once, in September
umm-al-quwain/ib-diploma-tutor.closingBody: The families in this emirate who spend least across two years are not the ones who negotiated hardest on an hourly rate. They are the ones who sat down in the first term of DP1 with the coordinator's deadline sheet, decided which phases they were funding, protected the core block, and kept the final stretch to two subjects. Book a free trial session, send the last marked piece of work and the school's internal deadlines, and you will get a plan with phases and a finish line rather than an open weekly commitment. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, timed around the school run.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma and Middle Years Programme subjects one-to-one over live video. Each works from the student's own scripts and drafts, so what comes back to a parent is marked evidence rather than a description of how the session went.

intro.heading: The question behind the search for a home tutor
paragraphs: A parent in Umm Al Quwain typing "IB home tutor" is usually not shopping for a format. They are trying to solve a trust problem. Somebody will spend an hour a week with their child, be paid for it, and the only evidence of what happened will be the child's own account and a grade that arrives three months later. The appeal of a tutor sitting at the dining table is that you can hear it working.

That instinct is reasonable, and this page takes it seriously rather than arguing with it. The answer is not that online is more pleasant. The answer is that the thing a parent actually wants - visible, dated, checkable evidence that the hour is moving marks - is a documentation question, not a geography question. A tutor in your living room who sets nothing and marks nothing gives you less to inspect than a tutor on a screen who returns a marked script every fortnight.

So the structure of this page is an evidence file. It sets out what should exist after week one, week two and week four; how a paper is marked the way an examiner marks it, including the method marks and the error-carried-forward rule most parents have never had explained; how an Internal Assessment draft is read against its published criteria and their mark allocations; and what grade movement realistically looks like on a 1 to 7 scale over a term rather than over a fortnight.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE - that service exists only in India - and there is no UAE office or centre. Sessions here are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. In this emirate the format also happens to be the practical one, because the Diploma students who live here mostly attend school in Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah and arrive home with a short evening left.

Where an in-home arrangement genuinely suits a family, this page gives the market rates in dirhams so a quote can be judged, and says which situations it suits best. What it does not do is pretend to sell one. The rest is about what to demand from any tutoring arrangement, in writing, before the end of the first month: a named weakness, a method, and work coming back marked.

One caution before the detail. No tutor can promise a grade, and anybody producing a predicted score before they have read a piece of your child's work is performing confidence rather than assessment. A Diploma grade is a band of marks reached over two years, and the largest variable in it is what the student does in the hours nobody is watching. The reason to insist on an evidence file is precisely that it measures the thing a promise cannot: whether those hours are changing.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Each IB programme produces a different paper trail, and knowing which one your child is inside tells you what evidence to expect from a tutor. The notes below are written from that angle rather than as a curriculum summary.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Each subject is assessed against four criteria, A to D, marked out of 8, and converted to a 1-7 grade through published boundaries. Because most MYP subjects have no external paper, almost all the evidence is school-generated: task sheets with criterion strands highlighted, and teacher comments tied to descriptors rather than to percentages.
programmes.countryNote: For an Umm Al Quwain family this is the easiest programme to audit, because the task sheets come home. A tutor working with an MYP student should be able to point at a specific criterion strand and show which band the work sits in, which is a far more useful conversation than one about effort.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects graded 1-7 plus the core. Evidence splits in two: internally assessed work marked at school against published criteria and moderated by the IB, and externally examined papers marked by examiners working from a mark scheme. The two produce different documents and fail for different reasons, so a tutor should be generating both kinds of evidence.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma students here are usually enrolled in another emirate, so the school's internal deadline list is the document that governs everything. Ask a prospective tutor to work from it, and ask to see how the plan maps onto it; a plan that ignores the school's own draft dates will produce evidence at the wrong time.

programmes.name: Mandatory UAE subjects and school reporting
programmes.description: Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies run alongside the licensed international curriculum under the Ministry's general regulations, and they appear on the same report card as the IB subjects, often on a different scale. Parents reading a report are therefore reading two assessment systems at once, which is a common source of confusion.
programmes.countryNote: Private schools in Umm Al Quwain are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, so reporting formats vary by school rather than following an emirate template. For these subjects, additional or different content requires prior Ministry permission, so any tutoring works from the school's own scheme.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: What a marked script tells you differs by subject. The entries below describe what to look for in each one when a tutor returns work, because that is how a parent judges whether the marking is real.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: A properly marked script shows method marks awarded separately from answer marks, so a student who sets up correctly and slips at the final line still scores. If every question is simply right or wrong with a tick or a cross, the marking is not following the scheme and tells you nothing diagnostic.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Look for comments on reasoning around calculator results. The commonest loss in this course is a correct figure produced by technology with no mathematical justification written beside it, and a marker who does not flag that is missing the main thing the examiner will penalise.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Data questions are the tell. A real marking should name missing uncertainties, inconsistent significant figures, and conclusions stated without reference to the data. Those are the same errors the scientific investigation loses marks for, so one piece of marking should be visibly useful in two places.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The useful marking here identifies terminology precision and command-term mismatch, not content coverage. A student who wrote an accurate general account of a process and scored half marks needs the specific missing term circled, which is what a returned script should show.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Working in symbols before numbers is the habit that earns method marks, and a returned script should show whether the student has it. Unit and magnitude errors under time pressure are the other recurring loss, and they only become visible when a paper has been sat to time rather than worked through at leisure.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Marking should be annotated at sentence level: where a point was stated without evidence, where the analysis slipped into summary, where a paragraph stopped short of linking back to the question. A global comment at the end of an essay is not evidence of anything a student can act on.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Management
subjects.description: The diagnostic marks here are about use rather than recall. A good marker will show where a diagram or framework was produced but never used in the argument, and where a judgement was expected and a description was given instead. That is the difference between a middle grade and an upper one.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Marking should cover the statistics section of the experimental report line by line, because that is where students lose most, and should distinguish between listing limitations and weighing them. Both are checkable by a parent reading the annotations, with no psychology background required.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Evidence here is draft history: successive versions with the research question sharpened, and comments tied to the assessment criteria. The student writes every word, so what a parent should see is a trail of their child's own drafts improving against descriptors, dated.

subjects.name: Arabic and Islamic Education
subjects.levels: First language and additional language streams
subjects.description: Mandatory alongside the IB under the Ministry's general regulations, and reported separately. Support works from the school's own scheme of work, since the use of different or additional content for these subjects without prior Ministry permission is not allowed, so expect evidence that maps onto the school's material.

umm-al-quwain/ib-home-tutor.regionsIntro: The evidence file depends on something mundane: whether the student has a place to sit, a device and twenty uninterrupted minutes. These notes are about that, area by area, because it is the most common reason an otherwise good arrangement produces nothing.

regions.note: Mostly family villas and apartments where the usual study spot is a shared living room. A headset and a door that closes change the quality of a session more than any change of tutor, and we raise it on day one rather than after a month of distracted hours.

regions.name: Al Riqqa
regions.note: Closer to the Sharjah road, so students are often home earlier and can work before fatigue sets in. The practical gain is that written work set between sessions actually gets done, which is what makes the fortnightly marked script possible.

regions.note: Newer apartments with ordinary household broadband, which is sufficient for one-to-one video and screen sharing. The limiting factor is usually a quiet corner and a second device for viewing a paper while talking, not connection speed.

sections.heading: What "home tutor" buys, and what it does not
paragraphs: The honest version of this comparison starts with what in-home tuition genuinely does better. A tutor in the room is harder for a teenager to ignore. Materials are physically shared, a younger child can be supervised, and some students simply settle better with an adult beside them. For a Middle Years Programme student who will not engage with a screen, that can be the deciding factor, and a family in that position should take it.

What it does not buy is evidence. The documentation a parent wants - dated marked scripts, criterion-by-criterion draft notes, an error log - is produced by a tutor's working method, not by their location. A visiting tutor who talks through homework for an hour and leaves has given you a pleasant hour and nothing to inspect. This is the substitution most families make without noticing: presence feels like proof.

It also does not buy choice. Umm Al Quwain is the least populous emirate and its Diploma students mostly attend school elsewhere, so the pool of adults living nearby who have taught Higher Level Chemistry or Analysis and Approaches to examination standard is very small. Filtering by driving distance first usually means accepting a generalist, and a generalist cannot mark against a scheme they have never used.

IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service, and there is no UAE centre. What this page offers instead is the thing the search is really after, written down: specialists matched by subject and level, and an evidence trail a parent can audit each fortnight. sections.heading: The evidence file: what should exist after four weeks
paragraphs: A month is long enough to judge the paperwork even if it is too early to judge the grade. By the end of week four a family should be holding a small, dated set of documents, and if they are not, that is the conversation to have rather than waiting for a report card to tell you.

Week one should produce a diagnostic: a short set of questions across the syllabus areas, one piece of the student's writing marked against the criteria or scheme, and a written statement of where the marks are going. Not a grade prediction - a list of specific losses. Week two should produce the first set task coming back marked, with the lost marks named. Week three should produce a second, and the beginnings of a pattern. Week four should produce the first honest statement of which losses are reducing and which are not.

The value of writing this down is that it converts a trust problem into an inspection problem. A parent who does not teach the subject can still check that the dates are real, that the annotations refer to specific questions, that the same error is not being named for the fourth week running without a change of approach, and that the student recognises what is in the file.

It also sets up the six-week review honestly. At six weeks there is enough evidence to say whether anything is moving. If the file shows the same three error types recurring at the same rate, the arrangement is not working, and the right response is a different tutor or a different plan decided then - not a wait-and-see that consumes a term.

sections.heading: How a paper is marked the way an examiner marks it
paragraphs: Most parents have never had examination marking explained, which makes it hard to tell real marking from decoration. The core idea is that marks are allocated to parts of an answer, not to its correctness overall. A six-mark question is six separate decisions, and a student can earn four of them while reaching a wrong final answer.

Method marks are the clearest example. In mathematics and the sciences, marks are available for setting up correctly, for substituting correctly, and for the answer, so a student who rearranges an equation properly and then mis-keys a number on the calculator loses one mark rather than all of them. The related rule is error carried forward: where an earlier mistake feeds a later part, the later part can still earn full credit if the method is correct from that point. A marker who crosses out everything downstream of the first error is not following the scheme.

Accuracy conventions carry their own marks. Significant figures and units are credited or penalised explicitly in the sciences, and premature rounding inside a multi-step calculation produces an answer that is penalised even though every step was sound. In written subjects the equivalent is the mark scheme's level descriptors, where the band is set by the quality of argument rather than by counting correct points.

This is why a returned script is the most informative document a tutor produces. A parent can look at it and see whether method marks were awarded separately, whether the annotations refer to specific scheme points, and whether the comments tell the student what to do differently. Those three checks need no subject knowledge, and they separate marking from ticking.

sections.heading: Reading an Internal Assessment draft against its criteria
paragraphs: Internal Assessment criteria are published, lettered and weighted, which means a draft can be audited rather than guessed at. This is the single most useful thing a tutor does with a Diploma student, and it is entirely legitimate because the student has written the draft and will do all the revising.

The mathematics exploration is marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with use of mathematics carrying the largest allocation and the rest sitting at three or four marks each. The pattern this reveals matters: a beautifully presented exploration using mathematics below the level of the course cannot reach the top bands, while a plainer piece at the right level can. Students almost always misjudge that trade.

The sciences scientific investigation is marked out of 24 across criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, in equal allocations. Equal weighting is the useful insight: evaluation is worth as much as design, and it is the section students write last and shortest. Economics uses a portfolio of commentaries on published articles with strict word limits; History uses an investigation with its own source-evaluation section; Psychology an experimental report whose statistics section is the main loss. Confirm all of these against your child's current subject guide, since the IB revises them on a cycle.

The method is mechanical. Take one criterion, read the top-band descriptor aloud, and ask the student to point at the part of their draft that does what the descriptor says. Where they cannot, that is the work. Where they can, move on. A tutor talks the student through it; the student makes every change.

sections.heading: What grade movement actually looks like
paragraphs: This is where most tutoring marketing becomes dishonest, so here is the plain version. Diploma subjects report on a 1 to 7 scale, and a grade is a band containing a range of marks. A student can gain real marks and stay on the same number, or sit near a boundary and move a grade on a small improvement. Nobody can promise a grade, and anyone offering a predicted score before they have seen the student's work is guessing in front of you.

What moves first is not the grade. It is the shape of written answers: command terms read correctly, conclusions actually reached, working shown, data referenced. That is visible in a marked script within two or three weeks and is why the fortnightly script matters more than a monthly grade. The second thing to move is usually accuracy under timed conditions, which needs papers sat to time rather than worked through comfortably.

Internal Assessment marks behave differently again. Because the criteria are published and the work is produced over weeks, a draft audited properly against descriptors can gain marks that are then banked, independent of examination performance. For a student who is a borderline grade, this is frequently where the movement that matters comes from, which is an argument for starting the Internal Assessment conversation early rather than at the deadline.

A realistic timescale, stated honestly: answer quality within two to three weeks, measurable change in timed-paper accuracy across a term, and Internal Assessment marks secured on the school's own deadline schedule. Mock grades are a noisy signal, because mock papers and boundaries vary by school, so read them as a direction rather than a measurement.

sections.heading: When the evidence says it is not working
paragraphs: Tutoring arrangements fail quietly, and they fail in recognisable ways. The first pattern is a file with no student work in it: sessions happen, nothing is set, nothing comes back marked. The second is a file in which the same three error types are named every fortnight at the same rate, which means the diagnosis is right and the method is not changing. The third is a student who cannot say what they are working on, which usually means the hour is being driven by whatever homework is due.

None of these requires confrontation. They require a conversation at six weeks with the file open: what has been set, what came back, what is reducing. A tutor doing the job well will have the same picture and often the same concern. A tutor who treats the question as a complaint has answered it.

The remedies differ. Where nothing is being set, the fix is usually structural: a shorter session with a task attached rather than a longer discussion. Where the same errors persist, the fix is a change of method - timed conditions instead of untimed, or one topic rebuilt from the beginning instead of papers practised across all of them. Where the hour has become homework help, the fix is to separate the two explicitly, because homework help is a legitimate service but it is not what a Diploma student losing marks on command terms needs.

And sometimes the answer is a different tutor. Subject knowledge, marking discipline and the ability to hold a sixteen-year-old's attention over video are three separate skills. A change request is a normal part of the arrangement here, and a month into a two-year programme is a much better time to make it than after the first mock series.

paragraphs: Families comparing options deserve numbers rather than a brochure. These are market rates compiled from providers' own published figures and from Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost table. They are not IB Gram's price list, and they are published here because three of the six pages ranking for UAE tutoring queries publish no price at all while the two that do quote US dollars.

An in-home one-to-one visit, travel included, runs roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate showing AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500. Monthly in-home packages advertised in the market sit around AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. A named IB or A-Level specialist runs AED 200 to 450 and upwards, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium examiner-marketed tutors reach AED 500 to 650 or more, with BartyED publishing AED 650.

The northern emirates distort the in-home band in a way Dubai-written pages do not mention. Umm Al Quwain sits roughly an hour from the Sharjah tutoring market in ordinary traffic, so a visiting tutor is absorbing a two-hour round trip for a one-hour booking. That is paid for either in the rate, in a two-hour minimum, or in reliability - and the cancellation always arrives in the busiest term.

Judge any quote against two questions rather than against the number alone. What comes back marked, and how often? And is the person quoting it a specialist in the course your child actually sits? A lower rate for an hour that produces no evidence is more expensive than a higher rate that produces a marked script every fortnight.

sections.heading: Reading the school report alongside the tutoring file
paragraphs: Two documents describe your child's progress and they do not agree, which confuses parents more than anything else in the Diploma. The school report carries teacher assessment, often a predicted grade, and sometimes mock results. The tutoring file carries marked scripts and draft history. Each is measuring something different, and the useful reading comes from putting them side by side rather than choosing one.

A predicted grade is a professional judgement made by the school for university applications, based on the evidence the teacher holds at that moment. It is not a forecast of the final result and it is not a ceiling. Where a predicted grade is lower than a parent expected, the productive question to the school is which evidence it rests on, because that evidence is precisely what tutoring work can add to.

Mock grades are noisier than they look. Mock papers, timing and boundaries vary between schools, and a school may set boundaries deliberately high to concentrate attention. A mock grade is therefore a direction rather than a measurement, and it is most useful when read with the actual script beside it: which questions were lost, and whether they were lost to knowledge, to timing or to command-term misreading.

Because most students here attend school in another emirate, one practical step is worth taking. Ask the school for its internal deadline list for the year - draft dates, mock windows, Internal Assessment submission points - and give it to the tutor in full. Private schools in Umm Al Quwain fall under the federal Ministry of Education while those in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah fall under their own emirate authorities, so formats vary, and a plan written from the actual list produces evidence at the moments the school is going to look.

faqs.question: Can we get an IB home tutor who comes to our house in Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. Home visits are a service offered only in India, and there is no UAE office or centre; tutoring for families here is one-to-one over live video. Independent tutors in the northern emirates do offer visits, and this page publishes the market rates so a quote can be judged. Before booking one, ask the same question you would ask us: what will be set between sessions, what comes back marked, and how often. Presence in the room is not the same thing as evidence of progress.

faqs.question: What proof should I have that the tutoring is actually working?
faqs.answer: By the end of week four you should hold a dated file: a diagnostic from the first session naming specific mark losses, a written plan split between Internal Assessment and examination work, at least two set tasks returned with the lost marks named, and the start of an error log. By week six there should be a statement of which error types are reducing and which are not. If the file is empty and the only evidence is a verbal report, that is the problem to raise, and it is the same problem whether the tutor sits in your living room or on a screen.

faqs.question: How can I tell real marking from a tutor just ticking answers?
faqs.answer: Three checks, none of which need subject knowledge. First, are method marks shown separately from the answer, so a student who set up correctly and slipped at the end still scores? Second, do the annotations name specific scheme points, or are they general comments at the end? Third, has the error carried forward rule been applied, meaning later parts still earn credit after an early slip? A script where everything downstream of one mistake is crossed out is not following the scheme and tells your child nothing they can act on.

faqs.question: How many marks is the IB mathematics exploration worth and how is it split?
faqs.answer: It is marked out of 20 across five criteria: presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics, with use of mathematics carrying the largest single allocation and the others at three or four marks each. That split explains the commonest mistake, which is a beautifully presented exploration using mathematics below the level of the course. A plainer piece pitched at the right level scores higher. Check the exact allocations against your child's current subject guide, because the IB revises subject requirements on a rolling cycle.

faqs.question: How is the sciences scientific investigation marked?
faqs.answer: Out of 24 marks across criteria covering research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation, in equal allocations. The equal weighting is the useful part: evaluation is worth exactly as much as research design, and it is almost always the section students write last and shortest. A tutor can read a draft against each descriptor and say where it falls short of a band, while the student does every piece of the writing and revising. Confirm the current criteria with the subject guide your child's school is working from.

faqs.question: How quickly should we expect to see a grade go up?
faqs.answer: Not quickly, and any tutor promising otherwise is guessing. A Diploma grade is a band of marks, so real gains can leave the number unchanged for a while. What moves first is the shape of written answers - command terms read correctly, working shown, conclusions reached - and that is visible in a marked script within two or three weeks. Timed-paper accuracy takes a term of repeated practice. Internal Assessment marks are the exception: audited properly against the criteria, they are secured once submitted.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a predicted grade and a mock grade?
faqs.answer: A predicted grade is a professional judgement made by the school for university applications, based on the evidence the teacher holds at that point. It is not a forecast and not a ceiling. A mock grade comes from a paper the school set and marked, often against deliberately demanding boundaries, so it varies between schools and reads best as a direction rather than a measurement. Both are most useful read with the actual script beside them, because the script shows whether marks were lost to knowledge, timing or command-term misreading.

faqs.question: Our tutor is pleasant but nothing seems to change. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Open the file at six weeks and look for one of three patterns. No student work in it means nothing is being set, and the fix is usually a shorter session with a task attached. The same three error types named every fortnight at the same rate means the diagnosis is right and the method is not changing, so switch to timed conditions or rebuild one topic from the start. A student who cannot say what they are working on usually means the hour has become homework help. If none of that shifts it, change tutor; a month in is a much better time than after the mocks.

faqs.question: Can a tutor read my child's Internal Assessment draft without breaking IB rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear line. A tutor can explain what each criterion rewards, read the top-band descriptor with the student, discuss the research question until it is answerable, teach the method, and say where a draft falls short of a band. The student writes every assessed word and makes every change. What nobody may do is supply paragraphs, rewrite a draft into final form, or provide text submitted under the student's name. One provider in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright, and the malpractice consequence of that falls on the student.

faqs.question: What does an in-home IB tutor cost in the northern emirates?
faqs.answer: Market rates for an in-home one-to-one visit including travel run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, with Bestimate showing AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors asking AED 200 to 500; monthly packages of four two-hour sessions are advertised around AED 1,599 to 1,799. Add the geography: Umm Al Quwain sits about an hour from the Sharjah tutoring market, so a visiting tutor absorbs a two-hour round trip for a one-hour booking, usually paid for in the rate, a two-hour minimum, or reliability. These are market figures, not IB Gram's.

faqs.question: Does my child need a quiet room, or is a laptop enough?
faqs.answer: A door that closes and a headset change the quality of a session more than almost anything else, and in shared family spaces they matter more than connection speed. Ordinary household broadband across this emirate handles one-to-one video with screen sharing. Two practical extras help: a second device so a paper can be read while talking, and a printer, because a paper sat on printed sheets to time and photographed back produces much more honest evidence than one worked through on screen.

faqs.question: Should two children in the same house share a session?
faqs.answer: Usually not, even when they take the same subject. The marked evidence is the point of the arrangement, and work produced in a shared hour cannot be cleanly attributed to one student, which makes an error log almost useless. Separate evenings also stop the stronger child setting the pace. Where cost is the reason, a better compromise is one child at a time with alternating weeks of marked work, so each has a genuine file rather than two half-files that show nothing in particular.

faqs.question: Which schools do Umm Al Quwain IB students usually attend?
faqs.answer: Most travel out of the emirate, to Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah, because Diploma provision inside Umm Al Quwain is limited. That places them under a different authority: the Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah and the Department of Knowledge does so in Ras Al Khaimah, and both also approve fees, curricula and assessment methods, while private schools in Umm Al Quwain itself are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. The practical consequence for tutoring is that the school's own internal deadline list, not a generic IB calendar, governs the plan.

faqs.question: Is the tutor legally allowed to take payment for private lessons here?
faqs.answer: They need a private tutor work permit from the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any amount quoted online is unverified. Since the permit costs nothing, a tutor who has not obtained one has simply not done it.

faqs.question: What happens in the free trial session?
faqs.answer: It is a working session with the tutor who would teach, not a sales call, and it produces a document you keep either way. The tutor sets a short diagnostic across the syllabus areas, marks a piece of the student's own writing against the criteria or scheme, and writes up the specific marks being lost along with what the first four weeks would target. You should be able to read it without a teaching background, and it should contain no predicted grade, because nobody can honestly offer one on an hour's evidence.

intro.heading: Evidence first: what a tutor should be able to put in front of you by week four
paragraphs: Start with the honest part. IB Gram delivers tuition to Umm Al Quwain as one-to-one lessons over live video. There are no home visits in the UAE; that is an India-only service, and it is stated the same way on every country page on this site. The phrase in the URL is the phrase parents type, and it describes a real need, so this page answers the home-tutoring question properly before explaining why a screen beats a car journey in this particular emirate.

Umm Al Quwain makes the case easier than most. It is the least populous emirate, and the pool of subject specialists living inside it for Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 or Diploma Chemistry HL is close to empty. A family searching for an IB IGCSE home tutor in Umm Al Quwain is realistically choosing between a generalist who can drive over and a specialist who can log in. The second option also removes the travel surcharge that sits inside every in-home quote in the northern emirates.

What replaces the reassurance of somebody sitting at the dining table is paperwork. Not a glossy monthly report with a smiley face on it, but artefacts: the script your child wrote, the markscheme the tutor applied, the mark written in the margin, the second attempt at the same question type three weeks later. A progress report is an opinion. A marked paper with a total on it is a measurement, and measurements are the only thing that tells you whether to keep paying.

Most households here are running two boards at once. An older child sits Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE papers while a younger one is halfway through MYP criteria, or a Year 11 student is finishing IGCSEs while a sibling has just started the Diploma. The two systems produce completely different evidence. IGCSE evidence is raw marks out of a paper total. Diploma and MYP evidence is criterion letters with achievement levels. Conflating them is the single most common reason a parent cannot tell whether tuition is working.

There is a timing problem on top of that. Almost every internationally schooled child living here travels out of the emirate for school, so the day ends late and the evening available for work is short. A tuition plan that assumes a 17:00 start is a plan for a different emirate. The sessions that hold are the ones scheduled around the bus, which usually means shorter weekday blocks and the long timed paper at the weekend.

So this page is organised as a file rather than a sales argument. It sets out the artefact you should expect in each of the first six weeks, how to read a marked IGCSE past paper without a teaching qualification, what a legitimate IB Diploma exploration draft log looks like, where feedback has to stop, what the market charges, and how the Cambridge entry calendar forces the whole schedule backwards. Take the parts that apply to your child and ignore the rest.

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-home-tutor.programmesIntro: Four qualification routes account for almost everything an Umm Al Quwain family needs support with, and each leaves a different paper trail. The differences below matter because they decide what you can legitimately ask a tutor to show you, and what the school keeps hold of until results day.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE is examined in a June series and a November series each year, with syllabus codes that identify the exact paper set a student sits: 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 for Physics, 0620 for Chemistry. Papers are marked out of a stated total and components carry published weightings, which makes this the most measurable qualification a tutor can work on.
programmes.countryNote: Umm Al Quwain students mostly sit Cambridge papers at centres in Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah, which means exam-day logistics involve a drive on a fixed morning. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the wrong zone timetable is the centre's problem, not theirs, so the school's own timetable version is the one to work from.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's International GCSE runs in May/June and November series. Codes look like 4MA1 for Mathematics A and 4PH1 for Physics. Some subjects are structured differently from the Cambridge equivalent, with fewer, longer papers, so revision built on Cambridge past papers can leave a Pearson candidate under-practised on question style.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools on the Sharjah and Ajman run enter candidates with Pearson rather than Cambridge, and a few split boards by subject. The practical consequence for a family in Al Salamah or Al Raas is that the correct past-paper set has to be confirmed from the entry statement before any revision timetable is drawn up.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP subjects are assessed against four criteria, A to D, each marked on an eight-point achievement scale rather than a percentage. A student can answer more questions correctly and see no movement in the published grade, because the criterion descriptors reward different behaviour: communication, inquiry, reflection, application in unfamiliar contexts.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP schools reachable from Umm Al Quwain sit mostly in Sharjah and Ajman, and their reporting cycles differ. For a family tracking evidence, the thing to request is the task-specific clarification sheet for the assessed task, because without it a criterion level is a number with no explanation attached.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma awards up to 45 points: six subjects marked 1 to 7, plus up to three points from the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge combination. Each subject carries an internal assessment marked against lettered criteria by the school and moderated by the IB, so part of the final grade is finished long before the examinations begin.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma candidates in this emirate are usually enrolled in Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah, and their internal deadlines are set by their own coordinator rather than by a published national calendar. Any tutoring plan has to be built around that school's dates, which is why the first session asks for the coordinator's deadline sheet.

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma and MYP subjects Umm Al Quwain families most often ask about, with the component where marks actually go missing. Each description names something checkable, so you can compare it against your child's last marked piece of work rather than against a claim.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Paper 1 is sat without a calculator, and that is where most of the damage happens. Students who can reach an answer on a graphical calculator lose method marks because the written argument is missing. Evidence of progress here is the appearance of intermediate lines of working, not a higher final answer count.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology use dominate. The recurring loss is the untranslated answer: a correct regression coefficient with no sentence explaining what it means in context. Marked scripts should show whether context marks were awarded, and that is a separate column from the arithmetic.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics generate the biggest gaps between understanding and marks. Candidates describe a reaction correctly but omit the curly arrow or the state symbol the markscheme requires. The scientific investigation is assessed against lettered criteria and is a fixed share of the grade, so draft dates matter.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Extended-response questions reward structure over recall. Students who know the content lose marks by answering a different command term from the one printed. A useful artefact is a command-term audit across one marked paper: how many marks were lost to explain-versus-describe confusion.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Data analysis and uncertainty handling cost more marks than the mechanics content does. Graph-based questions carry marks for axis choice, line of best fit and uncertainty bars, each independently awarded. Progress shows up as fewer zeros on the graph items, not as a higher total on the recall items.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation are where the grades separate. A correct explanation with an unlabelled axis scores under half of what the same explanation scores with the axis labelled. HL adds quantitative items that reward disciplined calculation layout rather than extra theory.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and Paper 1 analysis both reward close textual evidence over general comment. Students fall back on summary under time pressure. Evidence of improvement is the density of quotation in a timed response, which is countable in a way that fluency is not.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study questions require the candidate to use the stimulus, not general knowledge. Marks vanish when an answer could have been written without reading the case. A marked script should show which answers were credited for stimulus use, since that is usually the fastest available gain.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode precision and tracing tables are heavily weighted, and candidates who code fluently often write imprecise pseudocode. The internal solution is developed over months, so a dated draft log protects the student as much as it informs the parent.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together these contribute up to three points to the Diploma total. Both are assessed on the student's own argument, which makes the supervision boundary strict: a tutor can question a claim and point at a criterion, and the words on the page must be the candidate's throughout.

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-home-tutor.igcseSubjectsIntro: The IGCSE side of the same household produces a different kind of evidence: whole-paper raw marks against a published total. These are the subjects most often requested, with the syllabus detail worth confirming on the entry statement before revision starts.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge 0580 is tiered, and the tier caps the grade available, so the first question is always which tier the school has entered. Method marks are awarded for working that many students never write down, which makes the fastest early gain procedural rather than conceptual.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 differ in paper structure and in how practical skills are examined. Where a school enters the written alternative to practical, revision has to cover apparatus description and variable control explicitly rather than hoping lab memory carries it.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry
igcseSubjects.description: Mole calculations and ionic equations are the two reliable mark sinks. Both are drill-responsive, which is why they are good early targets: the second marked paper usually shows measurable movement on exactly those question types if the drilling was real.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology
igcseSubjects.description: Long-answer questions are marked against specific points, so a student writing three paragraphs can score two marks. Teaching the student to count the marks available and plan that many points is a mechanical change with a visible effect on the script.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language
igcseSubjects.description: Reading comprehension items reward exact lifting from the text, while writing tasks reward register control. The two need separate practice, and a combined mark hides which half is actually weak until the script is broken down by component.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies and Economics
igcseSubjects.description: Both subjects examine application to a given context and both punish generic answers. Marked scripts should be annotated with where application credit was given, because that annotation is what turns a 4 into a 6 over a term of practice.

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Where in Umm Al Quwain our students are, and what that does to the timetable
umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Distance inside this emirate is short, but almost every internationally schooled student travels out of it for school. That is what compresses the useful tutoring window. The notes below describe the real constraint in each area rather than repeating a postcode.

regions.name: Al Salamah
regions.note: The densest residential area and the one with the most Indian-curriculum and British-curriculum commuters. A bus leaving for Sharjah before seven returns late enough that a 17:00 start is optimistic and 18:30 is realistic on weekdays.

regions.name: Al Raas
regions.note: Older established housing close to the creek. Families here often run two children in two different schools, which means two different pickup times and a tutoring slot that has to be agreed around the later of them.

regions.name: Al Riqqa
regions.note: Spread-out plots with a longer internal drive before the main road. The practical effect is that Thursday evening and the weekend carry the longer sessions, while weekdays carry short, tightly scoped work on one question type.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain Marina and the corniche
regions.note: Newer apartment stock with a mix of expatriate families and shorter school commutes toward Ajman. This is the area where a 17:30 weekday session is genuinely feasible, which changes how a revision block can be spread.

regions.name: Al Humrah
regions.note: Industrial and residential mix on the southern side, closest to the Ajman boundary. Students here are often in Ajman schools, so the commute is the shortest in the emirate and the evening window is the widest.

regions.name: Falaj Al Mualla
regions.note: Inland and distinctly separate, roughly forty minutes from the coastal strip. Travel to any tuition centre is impractical on a school night, which makes live video the only format that fits a weekday at all.

regions.name: Al Haditha and the old town
regions.note: Close to the government offices and the older schools. A number of families here use Ministry schools and add private IGCSE entries separately, which changes both the evidence trail and the exam-day planning.

schoolClusters.city: The southbound run: Sharjah and Ajman
schoolClusters.note: Most IB and IGCSE students living in Umm Al Quwain are enrolled in one of these schools. Their internal assessment deadlines, mock windows and report cycles are set by the school, which is why a tuition plan starts by reading the school's own calendar rather than a generic one.
schools: Our Own English High School, Sharjah

schoolClusters.city: The northern run: Ras Al Khaimah
schoolClusters.note: A smaller group of families drive north instead, usually for IB continuity or for a particular subject combination. Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in that emirate, so an inspection report for one of these schools sits with a different authority from the one supervising schools inside Umm Al Quwain.

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-home-tutor.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every request from this emirate, and the choice is usually dictated by the commute rather than by preference. Each produces the same kind of evidence; what changes is how much of a single session is available for new teaching rather than consolidation.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, 60 minutes
modes.description: The standard arrangement for a student who is broadly on track and needs one component fixed. The hour is split: a short review of the marked work from last week, focused teaching on the weak question type, then a timed attempt that becomes next week's evidence. It fits a weekday evening even after a long southbound commute.
bullets: One marked artefact produced or reviewed every single week
Short enough to run at 18:30 on a school night without wrecking sleep
Best for one subject, one component, one measurable target

modes.title: Twice-weekly short blocks, 45 minutes each
modes.description: Two shorter sessions beat one long one for younger MYP students and for anyone whose commute leaves them flat by evening. Attention holds for forty-five minutes in a way it does not for ninety, and the gap between the two sessions forces independent practice that becomes the second artefact of the week.
bullets: Suits MYP students and Year 10 candidates building habits
Produces two pieces of evidence a week instead of one
Spreads the load across the commute rather than stacking it

modes.title: Weekend long session, 90 to 120 minutes
modes.description: Reserved for full past papers under timed conditions, extended-response practice and internal assessment work that needs continuous thinking. For families in Falaj Al Mualla or Al Riqqa, where weekday evenings are genuinely short, this is often the main session and the weekday slot becomes the follow-up.
bullets: The only realistic format for a complete timed paper
Used for exploration and essay work where the thinking is continuous
Marked script returned with the markscheme before the next weekday slot

sections.heading: What searching for an IB IGCSE home tutor in Umm Al Quwain actually gets you
paragraphs: The direct answer: in-home tuition exists in this emirate, it is usually delivered by a generalist, and in the northern emirates it costs more per hour than online work because the rate absorbs travel. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Tuition here is one-to-one over live video, and the specialist is matched to the component your child is losing marks on rather than to a radius around your address.

That trade is sharper in Umm Al Quwain than anywhere else in the country. In Dubai a family can plausibly find a Diploma Chemistry HL specialist within a twenty-minute drive. Here, the realistic in-home candidate is somebody who teaches several subjects at several levels and happens to live nearby. The subject-specialist pool for Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625 or Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL is not local, and pretending otherwise is how families end up paying for supervision rather than teaching.

There is a second practical point that nobody writing about home tutoring mentions. A visiting tutor leaves with nothing written down. The notebook stays with the student, the marking is verbal, and three weeks later there is no way to answer the question you actually care about. A session run over live video produces a file by default: the script is photographed or typed, the annotation is on the document, and the markscheme reference sits next to the mark. The evidence is a by-product of the format rather than an extra request.

None of that makes in-home tuition wrong. It makes it a different product with a different price and a different evidence profile, and a family should choose between them knowingly. What follows is the comparison a parent in Al Salamah or Al Raas actually needs, including what each option costs and what each one leaves behind.

sections.heading: The evidence file: the artefact you should be able to open in each of the first six weeks
paragraphs: A tuition arrangement that is working leaves a trail you can read without a teaching qualification. The sequence below is what a competent start looks like, and it is deliberately front-loaded: the diagnostic happens before any plan is written, because a plan written from a parent's description of the problem is a guess.

Week one is a marked paper or a marked section of one, chosen to match what the school has already taught. Not a quiz written by the tutor. A real past paper from the correct board, timed, and marked against the published markscheme with the mark written beside each item. What you receive is the script with annotations and a short note identifying the two or three question types that account for most of the lost marks. If week one produces only a conversation, the arrangement has started badly.

By week four there should be a second marked artefact on the same question types, and the comparison is the whole point. Raw marks on different papers are not directly comparable, which is why the comparison has to be type-level: six marks available on graph interpretation, two scored in week one, five scored in week four. That is a measurement. A rise in the overall paper total, on its own, could be an easier paper.

Weeks five and six are where internal assessment work starts leaving dates. Every exploration, investigation or coursework draft is logged with the date the student submitted it and the date feedback was returned. This protects the student. If a school or a moderator ever asks how a piece of work developed, a dated sequence of the student's own drafts with comments attached is the answer, and it is also the clearest possible demonstration of where the help stopped.

sections.heading: Reading a marked IGCSE script without a teaching qualification
paragraphs: Most parents are handed a marked paper and look at the total. The total is the least useful number on it. What you want is the distribution of the loss, and that is visible to anyone willing to spend ten minutes with a pen.

Work through the script and write one of three letters beside every lost mark. K for knowledge: the student did not know the content. M for method: the student knew it but did not write the step that earns the mark. C for command: the student answered a different instruction from the one printed, describing when the paper said explain, or stating when it said justify. Add the letters up. The proportions tell you what kind of help is needed, and they tell you quickly whether a tutor's diagnosis matches the paper.

A script dominated by M losses is the most encouraging result there is, because method marks are procedural. Cambridge Mathematics 0580 awards marks for working that students routinely skip, and a candidate who writes the substitution line before the answer picks up marks on questions they were already getting right. That change is teachable in weeks, and it shows up on the next marked paper unambiguously.

A script dominated by C losses points at a reading problem rather than a subject problem, and it is the most common pattern among second-language candidates across the northern emirates. The fix is a command-term drill, not more content. A script dominated by K losses is the slowest to move and the one where a weekly hour needs supplementing with real independent study, which is a conversation about the student's week, not about the tutor.
bullets: Mark every lost mark K for knowledge, M for method, or C for command term
Count the three totals before reading any comment the tutor has written

sections.heading: Two boards in one household: why the two evidence trails cannot be compared
paragraphs: A household running an IGCSE candidate and a Diploma or MYP student at the same time is the normal case in Umm Al Quwain, because families tend to pick one school run and keep both children on it. The trap is assuming the two children's progress can be read the same way.

IGCSE evidence is cardinal. A paper has a total, a script has a mark, and two marks on comparable papers can be subtracted from one another. Grade boundaries shift between series, so a raw mark does not map permanently onto a grade, but the arithmetic of improvement is straightforward and visible.

MYP and Diploma internal evidence is ordinal and criterion-referenced. An MYP criterion level of 6 out of 8 is not seventy-five per cent of anything; it is a descriptor the work matched. A Diploma internal assessment is marked against lettered criteria with separate mark allocations, and a student can write a markedly better second draft while the criterion level stays put, because the criterion that was capping the mark was never the one being improved. Parents who do not know this conclude, reasonably but wrongly, that nothing is happening.

The practical consequence is that a tutor supporting two children in one house owes you two different kinds of report. For the IGCSE child, marks by question type across dated papers. For the MYP or Diploma child, criterion letters with the descriptor band quoted and the specific gap named. Receiving one format for both is a sign that nobody has looked closely at the younger child's assessment model.
