sections.heading: Where feedback on a draft has to stop
paragraphs: This is the part of the page that matters most, and it is the part competitors in this market handle worst. Some of them openly sell finished internal assessments. A family that buys one is buying an academic malpractice finding against their own child, and under IB rules that is a risk to the whole Diploma, not to one subject grade.

The boundary is about authorship, and it is simple to state. The student thinks, researches, drafts and types. The tutor asks questions, points at the criterion descriptor, identifies what is missing, and explains the underlying subject content again if the gap is a content gap. Every sentence on the page is the student's. A tutor who returns a draft with rewritten paragraphs in it has crossed the line, whatever the accompanying explanation says.

In practice legitimate feedback looks like a question or a pointer, never a replacement. Where is the control variable identified. Which criterion is this paragraph trying to satisfy. The method section describes what happened but not why that method was chosen, and the descriptor asks for justification. That kind of comment forces the student to write the improvement themselves, which is both the rule and the only thing that improves the student.

The dated draft log is what makes this verifiable rather than assertable. A sequence of the student's own files, each with a submission date and a feedback date, demonstrates development over time. If a coordinator ever queries a piece of work, that sequence is the evidence. Ask for it from the first session on any internal assessment, exploration, investigation or essay, and keep it yourself rather than leaving it with the tutor.
bullets: The student is the author of every sentence, with no exceptions
Feedback is a question or a criterion pointer, never replacement text
Drafts are dated on submission and on return, and the family keeps copies
Published syllabus documents and markschemes are linked from the official site, never redistributed
Any offer to supply finished coursework should end the conversation

sections.heading: What the market charges, and what the fee should buy in evidence
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages examined for this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in. The figures below are market bands in dirhams, each attributed to the source that published it, and none of them is an IB Gram price list. For our own cost, the free trial session and the consultation are the honest answer, because the right number depends on the subject, the level and how many sessions a term actually needs.

The pattern worth noticing is the in-home premium. Bestimate's Dubai rate work puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350, with home tutors reaching AED 200 to 500, against qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300. In the northern emirates the gap widens rather than narrows, because the approach drive from Sharjah or Ajman is longer and somebody pays for it. The cheapest tiers, from around AED 45, are university-student tutors, and at IGCSE Extended or Diploma HL that usually buys supervision of homework rather than teaching of a component.

Judge a rate by the artefact it produces, not by the hour it fills. An hour that returns a marked script with the markscheme reference attached is worth more than two hours of homework company, at any price. The useful question to ask before paying anything is what the first session will produce in writing, and whether the family keeps it.

Monthly packages are common in this market, and the figures circulating publicly are around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Before committing to a block, check what happens to unused sessions when a school moves its mock window, because in this emirate the school calendar belongs to another emirate entirely.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the paper: entries, mocks and the dates that are actually fixed
paragraphs: Every revision plan in this emirate is built backwards from a date somebody else controls, and the date that surprises families is not the exam. It is the entry deadline, which sits months earlier and is the point after which the subject, tier and board are locked.

Cambridge publishes its key dates by series, and the March 2027 series is the clearest worked example of the gap. The examination period runs from 3 February to 4 March 2027, final entries are due on 27 November 2026, forecast grades are due on 27 February 2027, results reach centres on Direct on 13 May and certificates follow in late June. Read that order again: entries close more than two months before the first paper. A decision to move a candidate from Core to Extended tier has to happen before that deadline, which means the diagnostic evidence supporting the decision has to exist earlier still.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year, and the published pattern is useful for planning: the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also issues provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the document to work from rather than any restated date, including the ones on this page.

On IB dates this page says nothing specific, deliberately. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. UAE schools sit the May session, and Diploma candidates in Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah work to internal deadlines set by their own coordinator. Get those dates from the coordinator's deadline sheet and treat them as the real calendar, because they are the ones that bind your child.

One logistical point specific to Umm Al Quwain: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, and will not accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an examination after working from the wrong version. A family whose child sits papers at a centre in another emirate should confirm the zone with that centre rather than assuming the timetable a cousin abroad is using applies.

sections.heading: Who supervises the school, and what you can therefore ask to see
paragraphs: Private schools in Umm Al Quwain are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which performs the role that KHDA performs in Dubai, ADEK performs in Abu Dhabi and Ain, and the Sharjah Private Education Authority performs in Sharjah. Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education there. Knowing which body holds the file matters because the published documentation differs, and a family in this emirate is often dealing with two authorities at once: the Ministry for a school inside Umm Al Quwain, and SPEA or another emirate's regulator for the school their child actually attends.

The mandatory UAE subjects run alongside whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for. Federal rules oblige private schools to teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies regardless of curriculum. In Dubai, KHDA's guidance sets this out in detail: separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ; Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs; instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit with any mandatory subject lesson advised to run at least twenty-five minutes. The same guidance states that using different or additional content for these subjects without prior Ministry permission is prohibited, which constrains how any tutoring on them can be described.

For an evidence file, the useful implication is that these subjects sit on the report alongside the IGCSE and Diploma grades and are frequently the ones dragging an average down while nobody looks at them. They are also the subjects where a tutor has the least freedom to improvise, because the content is fixed. Support here means working through the set material and the assessment format, not supplying alternative material.

On equivalency, the Ministry route for British-track students is published and specific: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not counted among the five, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One page currently ranking in this market states that UAE candidates need six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong. For the IB route there is no points figure published that could be verified for this project, so none appears here. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutoring service performs, and the official channel is where it should be confirmed.

sections.heading: What the file looks like when the answer is to stop
paragraphs: A page selling tuition should be willing to describe the circumstances in which a family should stop buying it. There are three, and all of them are visible in the evidence file rather than in anyone's opinion.

The first is six weeks of flat type-level marks on the targets that were set. Not a flat paper total, which can be noise, but no movement on the specific question types the plan named. That is a signal that the diagnosis was wrong or the tutor is the wrong match, and the correct response is to change one of those things rather than to add hours.

The second is a student who has stopped doing anything between sessions. A weekly hour can fix method and command-term problems on its own, because those are procedural. It cannot substitute for independent study on a knowledge gap. When the file shows the only work produced each week is the work produced inside the session, the constraint is time and motivation at home, and more sessions will not touch it.

The third is the good ending, which is the one families forget to plan for. The targets have moved, the method marks are being collected, the internal assessment is drafted and dated, and the student is now capable of marking their own work against a markscheme. At that point the sensible move is to drop to a session a fortnight through the final stretch and stop afterwards. A tutoring arrangement that never ends is not a success story.

On availability, the honest position: specialist coverage is not unlimited, and for a narrow combination at HL in a specific evening slot there are weeks when nobody suitable is free. When that happens the options offered are a different time, a different specialist with adjacent experience, or a wait with a date attached. What is not offered is a generalist presented as a specialist, because that produces exactly the file full of activity and empty of movement this page is about.

process.title: Tell us the component, not just the subject
process.description: The enquiry that gets matched fastest names the board, the level and the thing going wrong: Cambridge 0580 Extended, losing marks on multi-step algebra, or Diploma Chemistry HL with the investigation due in six weeks. Subject and level alone takes longer to match, because the specialist pool is organised by component.

process.title: Send the last marked piece of work
process.description: One marked script, one report page or one draft with comments on it is worth more than a long description. It tells us whether the losses are knowledge, method or command term, and it lets the trial session start from something real instead of spending twenty minutes finding out what a parent already knows.

process.title: Use the free trial to produce evidence
process.description: The trial is a working session on live video, timed to suit the commute. It produces a marked piece of work or a marked section, plus a short note naming the first two target question types. If it produces only a friendly conversation, the trial has been wasted and you should say so.

process.title: Agree the six-week review before the first paid session
process.description: Fix the date, the targets and the evidence you expect to see at it. Two dated marked attempts on the same question types, a type-level comparison, and the draft log if an internal assessment is live. Agreeing this in advance is what makes the review a decision point rather than a chat.

process.title: Review, then change something or stop
process.description: At six weeks there are three honest outcomes: continue because the marks moved, change the tutor or the targets because they did not, or stop because the student now works independently. All three are results. Rolling on without looking at the file is the only outcome with no defence.

whyPoints.title: The specialist is chosen by component, not by postcode
whyPoints.description: Matching happens on the board, the level and the component where marks are being lost. For a family in Falaj Al Mualla or Al Raas that is the difference between a tutor who has marked Cambridge 0625 papers and a tutor who lives twenty minutes away and teaches four subjects.

whyPoints.title: Every session leaves something you can read
whyPoints.description: An annotated script, the markscheme reference, the mark, and a note naming what is being targeted next. The format produces this as a by-product rather than as a favour, which is why a live-video arrangement is easier to audit than a visit that leaves nothing behind.

whyPoints.title: Authorship of internal work is never blurred
whyPoints.description: Dated drafts, criterion-referenced comments, and no replacement text at any point. The student writes every sentence. That is both the IB rule and the only version of coursework support that leaves the student better at the subject rather than better supplied.

whyPoints.title: Prices are quoted as market bands with sources attached
whyPoints.description: Every dirham figure on this page is a published market band with the publisher named, not an invented price list and not a competitor's number passed off as ours. Our own cost comes after a trial session, because it depends on the component and the number of weeks left.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling is built around the southbound commute
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set in Gulf Standard Time around the school run to Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah, with shorter weekday blocks and the long timed-paper session on the weekend. Timetables move for mock weeks and for the shortened Ramadan school day.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits are stated rather than concealed
whyPoints.description: When no specialist is free for a narrow HL combination in a specific slot, you are told, with an alternative time, an adjacent specialist or a date. Several providers in this market conceal non-local delivery entirely; naming the limit is cheaper than discovering it in week three.

faqs.question: Does an IB IGCSE home tutor in Umm Al Quwain teach in our living room or on a screen?
faqs.answer: On a screen. IB Gram delivers tuition to every emirate as one-to-one lessons over live video; home visits are an India-only service and are not available anywhere in the UAE. The phrase is kept because it is what parents search, and the underlying need is real. What changes is the delivery: instead of whoever teaches that subject within driving distance of Al Salamah or Al Raas, the match is made on the board, the level and the component losing marks, and the hour contains no travel. The session also leaves a written record behind, which a visit usually does not.

faqs.question: What should be in the folder after four weeks of IB and IGCSE support?
faqs.answer: Two dated marked pieces of work on the same question types, the markscheme reference used to mark them, a type-level comparison between them, and a short note naming the next target. If an internal assessment is live, add the dated drafts and the criterion-referenced comments on each. That is the whole file. Anything presented instead of it, particularly a monthly summary with adjectives and no marks, is an opinion. A parent with no subject knowledge can still read a folder like that and answer the only question that matters, which is whether the specific thing being worked on has moved.

faqs.question: How do we compare one marked paper with the next when the papers are different?
faqs.answer: Not by the total, which depends on how hard that paper happened to be. Compare at question-type level. If six marks were available on graph interpretation in week one and two were scored, and five of six were scored on the equivalent items in week four, that is a measurement of the thing being taught. Totals are noise at this scale; type-level counts are signal. This is why the week-one diagnostic names two or three target types rather than giving a general verdict, and why the four-week comparison reports those types separately from everything else on the script.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a raw mark and a grade on an IGCSE script?
faqs.answer: The raw mark is what the script earned against the markscheme. The grade is what the board awards after setting boundaries for that series, and boundaries move because papers vary in difficulty. A raw mark therefore does not map permanently onto a grade, and any tutor converting one into the other with confidence is guessing. What a raw mark is good for is comparison: the same question types, marked the same way, a few weeks apart. Boundaries are the board's business on results day; marks by type are the only thing a weekly session can actually change.

faqs.question: Can one tutor keep evidence for an IGCSE child and a Diploma child at once?
faqs.answer: One tutor can, if their subject covers both, but the two files have to look different. The IGCSE child's file is raw marks by question type across dated papers. The Diploma child's file is criterion letters with the descriptor band quoted and the specific gap named, because an internal assessment is marked against lettered criteria rather than out of a paper total. Receiving the same format for both children is a sign the younger one's assessment model has not been looked at. In most households the two children are matched to two different specialists anyway, since the components differ.

faqs.question: How many drafts of an internal assessment should the evidence trail show?
faqs.answer: Enough to show development, each one dated on submission and on return. Three or four is typical over a term: an outline or proposal, a first full draft, a revised draft after criterion-referenced feedback, and a final version the student has checked themselves. The number matters less than the dating. A sequence of the student's own files with feedback attached demonstrates how the work grew, which protects the student if a coordinator ever asks, and makes clear where the help stopped. Keep copies yourself rather than leaving the only set with the tutor.

faqs.question: Which criterion letters should appear in feedback on a Diploma exploration?
faqs.answer: The ones the subject guide actually uses, quoted with the mark allocation, and named individually rather than as a general comment. Feedback that says the work is strong tells a student nothing. Feedback that identifies which criterion the paragraph is attempting to satisfy, and what the descriptor asks for that is currently missing, forces the student to write the improvement themselves. Ask to see the criteria the tutor is working from at the start. If they cannot name them, they are commenting on the writing rather than on the assessment, and the criterion level will not move.

faqs.question: What does a method mark look like, and how do we know it was awarded?
faqs.answer: A method mark pays for the step rather than the answer: the substitution line, the rearrangement, the correct formula written before any numbers go in. On a marked script it usually appears as a tick beside a line of working rather than beside the final answer, with a code from the markscheme. These are the marks students lose most often and recover fastest, because writing the step down is a habit rather than an insight. Ask the tutor to annotate which marks on a script were method marks. The count on the next paper is then directly comparable.

faqs.question: Who should keep the marked scripts, the tutor or the family?
faqs.answer: The family. Scripts, drafts, session notes and the six-week comparison belong with you, in one folder, for a practical reason: if the tutor changes, the evidence should not restart from zero. A new specialist handed a dated set of marked work can begin on week two rather than week one, and you can compare the old pattern with the new one. It also means the record of an internal assessment's development sits with the student, which is exactly where it should be if authorship is ever questioned.

faqs.question: What does the evidence trail cost per hour in the northern emirates?
faqs.answer: The hour costs what the tier costs; the trail should come with it rather than as an extra. Published market bands put budget online tutors from roughly AED 45 to 150, qualified online subject tutors at AED 150 to 300, in-home visits at AED 180 to 500 once travel is absorbed, and IB or IGCSE specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with premium examiner-experienced tutors quoted higher by BartyED at AED 650. Those are the market's figures, not ours. Ask what the first session produces in writing before paying anything, at any tier.

faqs.question: How far before a Cambridge series do entries have to be finalised?
faqs.answer: Months. Cambridge's published key dates for the March 2027 series show final entries due on 27 November 2026 against an examination period of 3 February to 4 March 2027, with forecast grades due 27 February and results to centres on Direct on 13 May. Entries close more than two months before the first paper. Any tier decision, any subject change and any private-candidate arrangement has to happen before that date, which pushes the diagnostic evidence supporting the decision earlier still. Check the live timetable for your child's series, since dates differ by series and by board.

faqs.question: Why does this page give Cambridge dates but no IB exam dates?
faqs.answer: Because the Cambridge and Pearson dates were read from those boards' own published pages and the IB dates could not be. The IB's site blocks automated checking, so no session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, and publishing an unverified date across a large set of pages would simply multiply the error. UAE schools sit the May session. For your child's actual deadlines, the Diploma coordinator's sheet is the authoritative document, because internal assessment dates are set by the school and are usually tighter than anything the board publishes.

faqs.question: Which authority supervises a private school inside Umm Al Quwain?
faqs.answer: The federal Ministry of Education, which supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Elsewhere the regulator is local: KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority in Sharjah, and the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah. This matters for families here because the school a child attends is frequently in another emirate, so two authorities are involved at once. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve fees, curricula and assessment methods, not only inspection outcomes.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory UAE subjects appear in the same evidence file?
faqs.answer: They should, and they are often the subjects nobody is looking at. Federal rules require private schools to teach Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside the licensed international curriculum. KHDA's guidance for Dubai schools sets out separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes prohibited. Support on these subjects means working through the set material and the assessment format, because the guidance prohibits using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission. Put the marks in the same folder as everything else.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with a family here need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through MoHRE and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here. MoHRE's own service page is the route to verify the position.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers the subject and tier we need this term?
faqs.answer: You are told, with options rather than a holding message. Narrow combinations at Higher Level in one fixed evening slot are the usual pressure point, and in some weeks nobody suitable is free. The alternatives are a different time in the week, a specialist with adjacent component experience who can start now, or a wait with a date attached. What should never happen is a generalist being presented as a specialist to fill the slot, because that produces a folder full of activity and empty of movement, which is the failure this whole approach exists to prevent.

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, make it the first request you put to any tutor you speak to: what will the first session produce in writing, and do we keep it? A family in Umm Al Quwain cannot drop into a classroom to see how things are going, and the school whose calendar governs the year is usually in another emirate. The file is the substitute, and it is a better one. Book a free trial session, send the last marked piece of work your child brought home, and judge the arrangement on the artefact that comes back rather than on how the conversation felt.

intro.heading: Distance is the wrong first filter for an IGCSE grade
paragraphs: Parents in Umm Al Quwain type "IB IGCSE tuition near me" and get results for Al Nahda, Muwaileh and Dubai Marina. That is not a fault in the search. It reflects where tutors live. Umm Al Quwain is the least populous emirate, and the pool of people within a short drive who can teach Extended-tier Chemistry 0620 to a Year 11 student is small enough to be measured in single figures. A family that insists on proximity is choosing from that handful. A family that drops the proximity filter is choosing from everyone who teaches the syllabus.

That matters because IGCSE grades are decided by specifics. A Core candidate and an Extended candidate in the same maths class sit different papers and can be awarded different grades. A Cambridge candidate and a Pearson Edexcel candidate studying what looks like the same physics course are examined on different question styles and reported on different grade scales. A tutor who teaches "GCSE maths" in general will spend the first month discovering which of those your child is in. A tutor matched by syllabus code starts on the content in the first hour.

The second thing this emirate decides is time, not distance. Most internationally schooled students here commute out: to Sharjah, to Ajman, sometimes to Ras Al Khaimah. A bus that leaves Al Salamah before seven and returns after four compresses the usable evening into roughly two hours. In-home tuition takes a slice of that for someone else's travel. Online tuition does not, which is why every lesson IB Gram arranges for a UAE family runs over live video rather than at an address. Home visits are a service we provide only in India.

This page is built around what IGCSE actually assesses and where students lose marks on it, because that is the question behind the search. A parent looking for tuition near me is not really asking about geography. They are asking whether anyone can tell them why a child who understands the subject keeps scoring a 5, and what an hour a week would change. The sections below answer that paper by paper, with the syllabus codes named, so you can check every claim against the board's own published syllabus.

Nothing here promises a grade. Tiering alone makes that impossible to promise honestly: a Core candidate cannot be awarded an A* however well they perform, and no tutor can change that after the entry deadline has passed. What a good match does produce is a diagnosis you can read, marked work you can keep, and a short list of topics worth the two hours your evening has left. It also produces an honest number of sessions, including the answer that the gap needs none, which is a thing a provider paid by the hour has no commercial reason to say and should say anyway.

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: Three programmes sit behind almost every enquiry from this emirate: the IGCSE years themselves, the Middle Years Programme that feeds them in IB schools, and the Diploma that follows. The notes below are specific to families based in Umm Al Quwain, whose children are usually enrolled at schools in a neighbouring emirate.

programmes.name: International General Certificate of Secondary Education
programmes.description: A two-year, subject-by-subject qualification taken one subject at a time, so a student can be strong in one and weak in another without either affecting the other. Most students enter eight to ten subjects. Each has its own syllabus code, its own set of papers and, on many subjects, a tier choice that sets the highest grade available. Assessment is almost entirely by terminal written paper, with coursework retained on only a minority of syllabuses.
programmes.countryNote: Umm Al Quwain families sit these exams at a centre run by the school, which for most students is in Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah rather than in this emirate. That means the exam timetable your child follows is the one issued to that centre, not a national one. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that the correct version of the timetable for that zone must be used.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB's middle-school programme, assessed against four criteria per subject with achievement levels from 1 to 8, converted to a subject grade from 1 to 7. There are no papers in the IGCSE sense until the final year, where schools may offer on-screen eAssessment. The habits it rewards, which are investigation, reflection and extended written response, are not the habits a timed IGCSE paper rewards.
programmes.countryNote: A number of students in this emirate move from an MYP school in Ajman to an IGCSE stream elsewhere, or sit both in the same household. The gap is real and specific: MYP work is marked against descriptors, IGCSE work is marked against a mark scheme with command terms. A student who writes a thoughtful MYP paragraph can still lose every mark on an IGCSE question that said "state" and wanted three words.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma, taken as six subjects plus the core of Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Grades run from 1 to 7 per subject with up to three further points from the core. Internal Assessment carries a meaningful share of most subject grades, which is why Diploma support looks different from IGCSE support: some of the marks are earned months before the exam.
programmes.countryNote: Post-16 options inside Umm Al Quwain are limited, so Diploma students from here usually travel further than they did at IGCSE or board weekly. For a family planning ahead, the IGCSE tier decision made in Year 10 is already a Diploma decision: Extended-tier mathematics is the realistic route into Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and a Core entry closes doors that are hard to reopen later.

umm-al-quwain/ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: The subjects below are the ones Umm Al Quwain families ask about most, with the Cambridge syllabus code given where it is the common entry. Pearson Edexcel and Oxford AQA equivalents are taught as well; the code only tells you which paper structure applies.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580)
subjects.description: Extended adds algebraic manipulation, functions, non-right-angled trigonometry, vectors and transformations on top of the Core content. Marks are lost most often in multi-step algebra where no working is shown, and on questions that ask for an exact answer where a rounded decimal is given.

subjects.name: International Mathematics (0607)
subjects.description: A separate syllabus from 0580, with a graphics calculator assumed and an investigation-style paper. Students sometimes arrive believing they are on 0580. Check the code on the statement of entry: the papers, the calculator rules and the revision material are all different.

subjects.name: Physics (0625)
subjects.description: The recurring losses are units and unit conversion, rearranging a formula before substituting, and the explanation questions on electromagnetic induction and radioactivity, where a correct idea written vaguely scores nothing against a mark scheme that wants named quantities.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620)
subjects.description: Moles and reacting-mass calculations account for a large share of Extended-tier losses, along with electrolysis half-equations and organic reaction conditions. The qualitative analysis section of the alternative-to-practical paper is learnable in two sessions and is routinely left to chance.

subjects.name: Biology (0610)
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Students lose marks by describing a process when the question asked them to explain it, and on data questions that require a calculated percentage change rather than a comment on the trend.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into a double award, so the syllabus is narrower than three separate subjects but the paper moves between disciplines without warning. Revision built from single-science past papers wastes time on content this syllabus does not examine.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510)
subjects.description: Reading comprehension, directed writing to a stated audience, listening and an endorsed speaking test. The directed writing task is where most marks move: register and format are assessed, so a fluent student who writes an essay when a report was asked for is capped before the content is read.

subjects.name: First Language English (0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and composition against reading passages. The analysis question rewards close attention to the writer's choices, which is a trainable technique. Students who read widely often score below their ability because they summarise instead of analysing.

subjects.name: Economics (0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries marks on its own: axes labelled, curves named, the shift shown in the right direction. Evaluation questions need a judgement supported by the analysis already written, not a restatement of both sides.

subjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
subjects.description: A case-study paper where application to the named business is assessed separately from knowledge. Generic answers about any firm score the knowledge marks and none of the application marks, which is the single most common reason a hard-working student lands on a 5.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Paper 1 theory on data representation, networks and security; Paper 2 on algorithms and programming. Pseudocode conventions are examined, so a student who codes competently in Python can still lose marks writing their answer in Python syntax.

subjects.name: Geography (0460)
subjects.description: Case-study recall plus skills: map interpretation, cross-sections, graph reading. The longer questions want named examples with located detail, and a student with no revised case studies cannot answer them whatever they know about the process.

sections.heading: What a search for IB IGCSE tuition near me is really asking
paragraphs: The literal answer first. Searching for IB IGCSE tuition near me in Umm Al Quwain will show you providers in Sharjah, Ajman and Dubai, plus platforms with no local presence at all. There is no meaningful inventory of in-home IGCSE specialists inside this emirate, and the few that exist will not cover the full range of subjects a Year 11 student takes. Any provider implying otherwise is describing a market that does not exist here.

The useful answer is that "near me" is a proxy for three other things parents actually want: a tutor who knows the local school calendar, a tutor who can be relied on at a fixed time, and a tutor who is accountable to someone if it goes wrong. None of those requires proximity. All three are contractual and organisational, and all three can be delivered to Falaj Al Mualla as easily as to Al Salamah, because the lesson travels over a video link rather than down Emirates Road.

What proximity does buy, honestly stated, is a physical presence in the room, which helps a small number of students: those who will not start work unless someone is sitting beside them, and those too young to manage a screen session. For a Year 10 or Year 11 student, the trade is usually the wrong way round. A twenty-minute radius around Umm Al Quwain contains very few Extended-tier chemistry teachers. A video link contains all of them, and the hour that would have gone on travel goes on the paper instead.

So the honest framing of this page: we target the phrase because it is the phrase parents type, and then we answer the question underneath it. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE. Lessons for every UAE family are taught one to one over live video, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India.

sections.heading: Core, Extended and the grade ceiling your child's tier has already set
paragraphs: On many Cambridge IGCSE subjects a student is entered at one of two tiers, and the tier decides the highest grade that can be awarded. A Core candidate sits a different pair of papers from an Extended candidate and can be graded from C down to G. An Extended candidate sits the harder papers and can be graded from A* down to E. This is the single most consequential fact on a Year 10 statement of entry, and a large number of parents have never been told it.

The practical consequence is that tutoring cannot lift a Core candidate to a B. If your child is predicted a strong C on Core papers and is capable of more, the conversation to have is with the school about the entry, not with a tutor about extra hours. Entries are made by the centre and there is a deadline after which a change is not possible, which is why this needs raising in the autumn of Year 11 rather than in the spring.

The reverse error is just as common. A student entered at Extended tier who is struggling with the supplement content may be heading for an E or a U where a Core entry would have produced a secure C. Neither outcome is a failure of effort. Both are a mismatch between the entry and the student, and both are visible months ahead in the mock scripts if anyone reads them against the right mark scheme.

Check the tier before buying anything. It appears on the statement of entry and the school office can confirm it in a sentence. The table below shows the pattern for the subjects Umm Al Quwain families ask about most; the current syllabus on cambridgeinternational.org is the authority for any specific year, since paper structures are revised.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE marks go missing, paper by paper
paragraphs: Most students who score below their ability are not short of knowledge. They are losing marks in a pattern, and the pattern repeats across every paper they sit. Reading three marked scripts in one sitting shows it immediately: the same five or six behaviours account for most of the lost marks, and none of them is "did not know the topic".

The first is the command term. "State" wants a fact with no reasoning, "describe" wants what happens, "explain" wants why, and "evaluate" wants a judgement. A student who writes a paragraph of explanation for a one-mark state question loses nothing but time, and then runs out of it on the four-mark question at the end. A student who writes a description where an explanation was asked for loses the marks outright, however correct the content.

The second is method. On calculation papers the mark scheme awards method marks that survive an arithmetic slip, but only if the method is visible. A student who works in their head and writes one line gets everything or nothing. The third is units and significant figures, which are examined deliberately in the sciences and in 0580. The fourth is the data question: a trend is described where a calculation was required, or a percentage change is attempted without the baseline.

None of this is fixed by covering the syllabus again. It is fixed by sitting papers to time, marking them against the published mark scheme, and tracking which of these recurs. That is what the table records, and what a session in the final term should be spending its hour on.

sections.heading: Paper 6: how practical skills are examined without a laboratory
paragraphs: Cambridge science syllabuses examine practical skills either by a timed practical test or by an alternative-to-practical written paper, which is commonly Paper 6. Most schools in this region enter candidates for the written alternative. That has a consequence parents rarely hear: the practical marks are not earned in the laboratory at all. They are earned on a desk, in writing, from a described experiment the student has never performed.

What the paper actually tests is a short, learnable list. Reading an instrument to the correct precision, including a thermometer, a measuring cylinder with a meniscus and a burette. Drawing a results table with headings and units in the header rather than beside each value. Plotting a graph with sensible scales, correctly labelled axes and a line of best fit that is not joined dot to dot. Identifying the dependent, independent and controlled variables in someone else's method. Naming a source of error that is not "human error", and suggesting an improvement that addresses it.

In chemistry, the alternative-to-practical paper also carries qualitative analysis: the colour of a precipitate, the flame test result, the gas test. These are recall items with a fixed answer set, and they are routinely left unlearned because they feel like laboratory trivia. Two sessions covers them properly, and the marks are as real as any on the theory paper.

This is the clearest example of why an online session loses nothing for an IGCSE science candidate. The skill being assessed is a paper skill. A tutor sharing a screen can mark a student's plotted graph line by line against the conventions, which is exactly what the examiner will do. The school's own laboratory work still matters for understanding; it is simply not where these particular marks come from.

sections.heading: Extended mathematics 0580: the topics that decide the grade
paragraphs: Extended mathematics is where the largest number of IGCSE tutoring hours in this region are spent, and the content that separates a 5 from a 7 is narrower than most families expect. Number, basic algebra and straightforward geometry are usually secure by the mocks. What is not secure is the Extended supplement, and it concentrates in a handful of areas.

Algebraic manipulation is the first: simultaneous equations where one is non-linear, rearranging a formula to make a nested variable the subject, and algebraic fractions where the student must factorise before cancelling. The second is functions: composite and inverse functions in the f(g(x)) notation, and reading a transformed graph. The third is trigonometry beyond right angles, where the sine and cosine rules apply and the student must first decide which. The fourth is vectors and transformations, often the last topic taught and the least practised.

Then there are the question types that cut across topics. Bounds and accuracy, where an answer must be given to a stated degree of precision or an upper and lower bound calculated. Probability trees with conditional branches and without replacement. Set notation and Venn diagrams with three sets. Each of these appears reliably on Paper 4 and each is a self-contained technique that can be taught in a session and tested the following week.

The practical plan for a Year 11 student from this emirate is to stop revising what is already secure. Sit a whole Paper 4 to time, mark it against the published scheme, and list every question that lost marks by topic. Four topics usually account for most of the gap. Four weekly sessions on those four topics, with a re-sit at the end, is a plan that can be checked, which is more than a general programme of maths tutoring will ever give you.

sections.heading: A* to G or 9 to 1: reading the report against the right scale
paragraphs: Two children in neighbouring villas in Al Salamah can bring home IGCSE reports in different alphabets. Cambridge International reports IGCSE results on an A* to G scale. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on a 9 to 1 numerical scale. Oxford AQA International GCSE also reports numerically. None of these is a harder or easier qualification by virtue of its scale, and a number cannot be read off against a letter informally without producing nonsense.

This matters for three practical reasons. First, when you compare your child against a cousin or a neighbour, you may be comparing two scales. Second, when you buy revision material, the board matters more than the subject name: a Cambridge 0620 chemistry past paper is not useful preparation for a Pearson chemistry paper, because the question style and the paper structure differ. Third, when a family moves school mid-course, the board can change, and a student can lose a term discovering that their practised paper format no longer applies.

Tiering also differs by board. Cambridge uses Core and Extended on many subjects. Pearson Edexcel uses Higher and Foundation on some, and a single tier on others. Entry series differ too: Cambridge runs June and November series with a restricted March series for certain syllabuses and centres, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The one thing that applies to every board is that the entry deadline sits months before the paper.

Before any tutoring starts, write down three things for each subject: the board, the syllabus or specification code, and the tier. Those three facts determine which past papers are worth sitting and which are a waste of an evening you did not have to spare.

sections.heading: Nine subjects, one week: deciding which two to support
paragraphs: A Year 11 student entered for nine subjects cannot be tutored in nine subjects, and should not be. The evening in this emirate is short, the student is tired after a cross-emirate commute, and spreading two hours across nine subjects produces nothing measurable in any of them. The decision that actually matters is which one or two subjects the hour goes to.

The wrong way to decide is by the lowest grade on the report. A 4 in a subject the student dislikes and will drop after this year is worth less than a 5 in the subject their Diploma choices depend on. Mathematics is the clearest case: an Extended maths grade is the gate to Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level, and a weak maths grade narrows post-16 options in a way that a weak geography grade does not.

The second filter is the shape of the gap. A student who is one technique away from a better grade, for example a physicist who understands the content and loses every calculation mark to invisible method, will move quickly. A student who has missed a term of content needs more hours than a term can provide, and the honest answer may be to protect two other subjects instead. This is what a diagnostic session is for, and it is a question that needs marked scripts to answer, not a conversation about how the student feels.

The third filter is the calendar. Subjects with coursework or an endorsed speaking component have earlier internal deadlines, so support has to arrive before those dates rather than in the revision period. The table in the sessions section of this page sets out the order. For most families here, the stable answer is one weekly hour on maths, one on the weakest science, and nothing else until the mocks are marked.

sections.heading: The Umm Al Quwain evening, and the order to do the work in
paragraphs: A student who leaves Al Salamah at 6.40am and gets home at 4.15pm has, realistically, two usable hours before fatigue makes new content pointless. How those two hours are ordered changes what they produce. Hard, unfamiliar content first while attention holds. Practice of something already half-learned second. Anything mechanical, such as copying out a results table or learning qualitative analysis colours, last.

A tutoring session should take the first slot, not the last. Booked at 7.30pm after homework, it becomes a lesson taught to a tired student who will retain little of it, and the parent has paid full price for the worst hour of the day. Booked at 5pm, with homework afterwards, it is the hour with the best chance of changing something. For families whose children return later, the better answer is often a single longer weekend session rather than a weekday hour that cannot really be used.

Ramadan reorders this completely. School days shorten, which frees the afternoon, and the evening reorganises itself around iftar. A session that moves to the late morning on a shortened school day, or to a post-iftar slot, keeps continuity through a month that otherwise interrupts it. That needs arranging a fortnight ahead, because every family in the Gulf is trying to book the same post-iftar hours.

The last piece of ordering is the term. Content teaching belongs in the autumn and winter. From the point the mocks come back, the hour should be whole papers sat to time and marked, because at that stage technique and timing move a grade further than new content does. A tutor who is still teaching chapters in April has not read the calendar.

faqs.question: Is my child entered for Core or Extended IGCSE, and can that still be changed?
faqs.answer: It is printed on the statement of entry and the school office can confirm it in one email. The tier matters because it sets the highest grade available: Core candidates on Cambridge subjects can be awarded C to G, Extended candidates A* to E. Entries are made by the centre, not by you, and there is a final entry deadline months before the papers after which a change is not possible. If you think the tier is wrong, raise it in the autumn of Year 11, in writing, with the mock scripts attached. By the spring the decision has usually hardened.

faqs.question: What is the highest grade a Core-tier candidate in Umm Al Quwain can actually be awarded?
faqs.answer: On Cambridge IGCSE subjects that are tiered, a Core entry caps the outcome at grade C. A student can answer every question perfectly and still receive a C, because the papers sat do not contain the Extended content on which higher grades are awarded. This is a fact about the entry, not about the student or the teaching, and no amount of tutoring changes it. It is also why we ask for the tier before quoting a plan: buying twenty hours to chase a B on a Core entry is spending money on something that cannot happen.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child's maths course is 0580 or 0607?
faqs.answer: Check the syllabus code on the statement of entry or ask the maths department directly. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 and Cambridge IGCSE International Mathematics 0607 are different syllabuses with different papers. 0607 assumes a graphics calculator and includes an investigation-style component; 0580 does not. Past papers are not interchangeable between them, so a student revising from the wrong code is practising questions they will never see. Families moving between schools in Sharjah and Ajman sometimes change code without being told, which is worth checking at the start of Year 11.

faqs.question: How are science practical skills examined if my child's school enters the written alternative?
faqs.answer: On Cambridge science syllabuses the practical skills are usually assessed through an alternative-to-practical written paper, commonly Paper 6. The marks come from a desk rather than a laboratory: reading instruments to the right precision, building a results table with units in the headings, plotting a graph with sensible scales and a line of best fit, identifying variables in someone else's method, and naming a real source of error with an improvement that addresses it. In chemistry it also carries qualitative analysis, which is fixed recall. All of it can be taught and marked over a shared screen.

faqs.question: Why does my neighbour's child get grades 9 to 1 while our report shows A* to G?
faqs.answer: Because they are sitting a different board. Cambridge International reports IGCSE results on an A* to G scale. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE and Oxford AQA International GCSE report on a 9 to 1 numerical scale. Neither scale indicates a harder qualification, and converting informally between them produces misleading comparisons. The practical consequence is about revision rather than status: past papers, mark schemes and question styles belong to one board, so material bought for the wrong board wastes study time. Note the board and the specification code for every subject before buying anything.

faqs.question: My child takes nine IGCSE subjects. Which two should we support first?
faqs.answer: Rank by consequence rather than by the lowest grade. Mathematics usually comes first, because an Extended maths grade is the realistic gate into Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level and narrows post-16 choices if it is weak. Then the science your child's intended Diploma route needs. A subject they will drop after this year, even at grade 4, is rarely worth the hour. The second filter is the shape of the gap: a technique problem moves in weeks, a missing term of content needs longer than a term usually has. Marked scripts tell you which it is.

faqs.question: Does searching for IGCSE tuition near me find anyone actually inside this emirate?
faqs.answer: Largely no. Umm Al Quwain is the least populous emirate and the pool of in-home specialists here is very small, especially at Extended tier in the sciences and mathematics. Search results are dominated by providers in Sharjah, Ajman and Dubai, plus platforms with no local presence. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India. Lessons for families here are taught one to one over live video, which is also what removes the twenty-minute radius from the choice of tutor.

faqs.question: What should one hour of IGCSE tuition actually produce?
faqs.answer: Something you can read afterwards. In a content session, a worked set of questions on the target topic plus practice set for the week. In the exam term, a whole paper sat to time, marked against the published mark scheme, with the lost marks categorised by cause rather than just totalled. Over four weeks that builds a file showing which errors are disappearing and which are not. If after a month the only evidence is a tutor saying sessions are going well, you have no basis for deciding whether to continue, and you should ask for marked work.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover both Extended mathematics and a science at the same time?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Mathematics and physics overlap heavily in technique, so a specialist in both is common and a combined plan can work well. Chemistry and biology are different enough from mathematics that the same person is less often strong in both. The test is not a claim on a profile but a trial lesson in the weaker of the two subjects. If a tutor is comfortable teaching 0580 Extended algebra and 0625 supplement calculation in the same hour, that will be obvious in forty-five minutes.

faqs.question: What do IGCSE tuition rates look like in dirhams in the northern emirates?
faqs.answer: Published market rates vary widely by tier of tutor rather than by emirate. Budget online tutoring, often by university students, is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online sit roughly in the AED 150 to 300 band, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home visits, where they exist, carry travel and run higher. Those are other providers' published figures, not ours. Ask any provider for the rate, the session length and what is included before paying.

faqs.question: Why is in-home tuition more expensive here than the same hour in Sharjah?
faqs.answer: Because you are buying travel as well as teaching. A tutor driving from Sharjah or Ajman to Al Salamah loses an hour on the road for a one-hour lesson, and that time is priced into the quote whether or not it appears as a line item. Market figures for in-home one-to-one visits run from roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour depending on level and provider. The further from the tutor pool you live, the worse the arithmetic becomes, which is why households in Falaj Al Mualla see the widest gap between in-home and online quotes.

faqs.question: Is there any point starting IGCSE support one term before the papers?
faqs.answer: Later than most families assume, provided the plan changes to match the time left. With a term to go, new content teaching is the wrong purchase. What still moves marks is technique: sitting whole papers to time, marking them against the published scheme, and removing two or three recurring errors such as invisible method, dropped units or misread command terms. Those gains are real and they are available in weeks. What is not available in weeks is a term of missed content across four subjects, and a provider who implies otherwise is selling hours rather than advice.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE Ministry of Education actually require for equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track, the published requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor states that six IGCSE subjects are required, which does not match the published rule. Equivalency is a Ministry process that families apply for directly; it is not something a tutoring provider performs or guarantees on your behalf.

faqs.question: Does my child need a permitted tutor, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. You are entitled to ask any tutor about their permit, and a provider that treats the question as unreasonable has told you something useful.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with coursework or an Internal Assessment without breaking the rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the underlying skills, explain the assessment criteria, discuss a draft the student has written, and give feedback that the student then acts on themselves. A tutor may not write, complete, redraft or substantially edit the work, supply a topic worked up into an outline that only needs typing, or produce any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or Personal Project. The second list is academic malpractice and the consequence falls on the student. Any provider offering to produce assessed work is a risk to your child's qualification.

intro.heading: Without a percentage, what counts as proof the hour is working?
paragraphs: Middle Years Programme reports do not behave like the ones most parents grew up with. There is no 68 per cent, no class rank and often no exam. Each subject is assessed against four criteria, lettered A to D, and each criterion is awarded an achievement level from 1 to 8 by best fit against a published descriptor. Those four levels are then converted, using the school's grade boundaries, into a single subject grade from 1 to 7. A parent reading that report cannot tell from the numbers alone whether anything improved.

This is the real problem an MYP tutor is hired to solve in a household here, and it is why this page is built around evidence rather than around subject content. If you cannot see a percentage move, you need something else you can read: the marked task with the criterion levels shown, the task-specific clarification the teacher used, the redraft, and the next task marked the same way. Four weeks of that is readable by a parent who has never taught the subject. Four weeks of a tutor saying sessions are going well is not.

The second thing worth saying plainly is that MYP marking is not arithmetic. A level 5 on criterion B is a band, not a score out of eight, and the descriptors are written as holistic statements. A teacher judges which descriptor the work best fits. That means a student can write more, work harder and produce a longer piece without moving a single criterion, because the thing that moves a level is usually a specific missing move: an evaluation that was never attempted, a variable that was never controlled, a source that was never questioned.

Families in Umm Al Quwain are also solving a logistics problem at the same time. Most internationally schooled students here commute to Sharjah, Ajman or Ras Al Khaimah, and an MYP 2 or MYP 3 student is often home later and more tired than their own parents expect. An hour that starts at 7.30pm after homework is an hour spent on a child with nothing left. Some of the practical sections below are about where in the evening a session should sit, and when a shorter one twice a week is the better purchase.

Everything described here is delivered online, one to one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service we offer only in India. For an MYP student the online format has a specific advantage beyond the tutor pool: criterion-marked work is shared, annotated and redrafted on screen, so the marked evidence accumulates in one place instead of in the bottom of a school bag.

A level is a descriptor band, not a score out of eight
Task-specific clarifications tell you what that unit's descriptors meant
The Personal Project in MYP 5 is assessed on its own criteria
Lessons are delivered online, one to one, in Gulf Standard Time

umm-al-quwain/ib-myp-tutor.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes sit around an MYP student: the Primary Years Programme behind them, the Middle Years Programme itself, and the Diploma ahead. The notes below are about how each one behaves for a family based in this emirate, where the school is usually in a neighbouring one.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria on an eight-point scale. Learning is organised into units built on a statement of inquiry, key and related concepts and a global context. Approaches to learning skills are taught deliberately and reported on. In the final year every student undertakes a Personal Project, and some schools enter candidates for on-screen eAssessment leading to the MYP certificate.
programmes.countryNote: MYP provision reachable from Umm Al Quwain sits mostly in Ajman and Sharjah, which means the commute shapes the week for a child aged 11 to 16 who is not yet managing their own time. It also means two households in Al Salamah can be on different term dates and different assessment calendars, so a session plan has to follow the school rather than a generic UAE calendar.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry organised around six themes, finishing with the exhibition. Assessment is formative and descriptive rather than graded, so a student arriving in MYP 1 may never have sat anything resembling a timed task. The habits the PYP builds, which are questioning, research and reflection, are the ones MYP criteria B and D reward most directly.
programmes.countryNote: Students moving from a PYP school into MYP 1 locally usually change school as well as programme, often crossing an emirate boundary in the process. The first MYP report is where families here most often ask for help, because the criterion-level format is unfamiliar and a grade 4 on a 1 to 7 scale reads worse than it is.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Assessment combines terminal examinations with Internal Assessment marked against criteria lettered A onwards. The MYP is the better preparation for the Internal Assessment half of that; it is weaker preparation for the timed-paper half, which is where most MYP 5 students feel the step up.
programmes.countryNote: Post-16 IB provision is thin in the northern emirates, so Diploma students from Umm Al Quwain generally travel further than they did in MYP or board weekly. Families planning that move usually want the MYP 4 and 5 years used to build timed-writing stamina, because the Diploma adds examinations that the MYP has not required.

umm-al-quwain/ib-myp-tutor.subjectsIntro: MYP subjects are grouped rather than listed as separate qualifications, and each group has its own four criteria. The notes below say what each group's criteria actually reward and where levels are most often lost, which is the detail a school report leaves out.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. Levels are lost most often in B, where the hypothesis has no scientific reasoning behind it and variables are listed without being controlled, and in C, where data is presented but not evaluated.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. B is the criterion most students have never been taught to attack: it wants a general rule, tested and justified, not a table of values. C costs marks when working is correct but unexplained.

subjects.name: Language and literature
subjects.description: A analysing, B organizing, C producing text, D using language. The recurring loss is in A, where a student retells the text rather than analysing how the writer achieves an effect, and in D, where register and control are assessed separately from ideas.

subjects.name: Language acquisition
subjects.description: A listening, B reading, C speaking, D writing, with phase bands rather than year groups. Students placed in the wrong phase are the commonest cause of a puzzling grade: a capable speaker in a high phase can score below a weaker student placed in a lower one.

subjects.name: Individuals and societies
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating, D thinking critically. D is where the grade is usually decided, and it needs sources weighed against each other, not described. Referencing is part of C and is lost through carelessness rather than ignorance.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: A inquiring and analysing, B developing ideas, C creating the solution, D evaluating. The design folder is where levels live: a strong product with a thin folder scores poorly, because three of the four criteria are about the process rather than the object.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: A investigating, B developing, C creating or performing, D evaluating. As in design, the process journal carries most of the assessment. Students who make good work and document nothing are the ones whose reports surprise their parents.

subjects.name: Physical and health education
subjects.description: A knowing and understanding, B planning for performance, C applying and performing, D reflecting and improving performance. Only one of the four is about physical performance, so a sporty student with no written reflection can sit on a grade 4 indefinitely.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Assessed on its own criteria covering disciplinary grounding, synthesis and reflection. Students treat these units as a double dose of two subjects, which is exactly what the criteria do not reward: the marks are for integrating the two disciplines into one explanation.

subjects.name: Personal Project
subjects.description: A planning, B applying skills, C reflecting, assessed through the process journal, the product and the report. It is the one piece of MYP work with a formal academic-honesty dimension, and the boundary between supervision and interference matters here more than anywhere else in the programme.

umm-al-quwain/ib-myp-tutor.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in Umm Al Quwain decides the commute, and for an eleven to sixteen year old the commute decides how much of the evening is usable. These notes are about MYP-age students specifically.

regions.name: Al Salamah
regions.note: The largest residential district and the main source of MYP enquiries here. Buses to Sharjah leave early and return after four, so a younger MYP student is often better served by two shorter sessions than one long one.

regions.name: Al Riqqah
regions.note: Closer to the Ajman boundary, with many families choosing Ajman schools. The shorter return leg makes a 4.30pm start realistic, which for an MYP 1 or 2 student is the difference between a session that works and one that does not.

regions.name: Al Raas
regions.note: Older housing by the creek, with a high proportion of households running the mandatory national subjects alongside an international programme. For MYP students the competition for the evening hour is Arabic and Islamic Education homework.

regions.name: UAQ Marina and the corniche
regions.note: Newer development with a mobile expatriate population, so mid-year arrivals are common. A student joining MYP 3 in January has missed the units the current criteria were taught through, which a school report will not explain.

regions.name: Al Humrah
regions.note: Near the industrial area and the Sharjah boundary. Short distance, slow at the wrong hour. Weekend sessions suit families here, and for Personal Project work a longer weekend block is more useful than a weekday hour anyway.

regions.name: Falaj Al Mualla
regions.note: The inland town, roughly fifty kilometres from the coast. There is no realistic local market in MYP subject specialists at that distance, which is the plain reason online delivery widens the choice rather than narrowing it.

schoolClusters.city: Ajman and Sharjah: where most MYP students from here study
schoolClusters.note: The nearest IB continuum provision sits in Ajman and Sharjah. Journey times of thirty to sixty minutes each way are normal, and the schools run their own assessment calendars, so unit deadlines differ between two children living on the same street.

schoolClusters.city: Ras Al Khaimah and inside Umm Al Quwain
schoolClusters.note: Families nearer Falaj Al Mualla sometimes look north instead. Private schools inside Umm Al Quwain are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority, and the international offer inside the emirate is narrow.
schools: Ras Al Khaimah schools under the Department of Knowledge
Private schools in Umm Al Quwain under Ministry of Education supervision

umm-al-quwain/ib-myp-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: Named schools describe where students in this emirate study and are given as context only; no affiliation, endorsement or partnership is implied.
umm-al-quwain/ib-myp-tutor.modesIntro: Three formats cover most MYP requests from this emirate, and all three are taught online, one to one. For a younger student the choice is mostly about attention span and the time the bus gets home.

modes.title: Two shorter sessions a week
modes.description: Forty to forty-five minutes, twice, usually the right shape for MYP 1 to MYP 3. A younger student who has been on a bus since quarter to seven cannot concentrate for a full hour at five o'clock, and two contacts a week also means the gap between teaching and practice never grows past three days.
bullets: Shorter contact, more often
One criterion targeted per session
Work set is small enough to be finished properly

modes.title: Weekly hour on one subject group
modes.description: The standard shape for MYP 4 and 5, where tasks are longer and the Personal Project is running alongside. The hour follows the school's current unit, works on the specific criterion that unit is assessing, and uses the task-specific clarification the teacher issued rather than a generic version of the descriptors.
bullets: Built around the live unit, not a syllabus
Drafts annotated against the criteria
Redraft reviewed the following week

modes.title: Project and draft review block
modes.description: A short run of sessions timed to a task deadline or to Personal Project milestones. The tutor reads what the student has written, marks it against the criteria, and talks through what is missing. The student makes every change themselves; nothing is rewritten for them, which is the line IB academic honesty draws and we hold it visibly.
bullets: Timed to the school's internal deadlines
Feedback on the student's own draft only
Process journal entries reviewed, never written

sections.heading: What an MYP tutor is hired to do when there is no past paper
paragraphs: The direct answer: an MYP tutor's job is to make the criteria legible and then teach the specific moves a criterion rewards. There is no bank of past papers to grind through, because most MYP assessment is task-based and set by the school. What exists instead is a published set of criteria per subject group, a task-specific clarification per unit, and whatever your child's teacher wrote on the last piece of work.

That changes the shape of a session. A tutor working on IGCSE physics can sit a Paper 4 and mark it. A tutor working on MYP sciences has to start from the marked task and the criterion that cost the most: usually B, inquiring and designing, where the student wrote a hypothesis with no scientific reasoning and listed variables without saying how they would be controlled. The teaching is then narrow and specific. Write three hypotheses with reasoning. Identify the independent, dependent and controlled variables in each. Redraft the method so another student could follow it.

The second part of the job is translation for the parent. You are entitled to know which criterion is holding the grade, what the next band up actually requires, and what evidence will show it has moved. In practice that means a written note after the first few sessions saying something like: criterion D in individuals and societies is sitting at 4 because sources are described rather than weighed, and here is the redraft where it was done properly.

The third part is restraint. A great deal of MYP work is coursework-shaped, and the temptation to improve it directly is constant. A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own writing. A tutor does not write, redraft or substantially edit it. That boundary is not a formality in the final year, where the Personal Project carries an academic-honesty requirement that the student signs.

sections.heading: Criteria A to D: the four questions every MYP task is really asking
paragraphs: Each MYP subject group has four criteria, and they are not interchangeable between subjects. A student who has worked out what criterion B rewards in mathematics has learned nothing about criterion B in sciences, because one is about investigating patterns and the other is about designing an investigation. Parents are rarely given this map, and without it a report is four unexplained numbers.

Learning the map takes a quarter of an hour and changes how you read everything that comes home. It tells you, for instance, that three of the four design criteria are about the folder rather than the product, which explains why a beautifully made object scored a 4. It tells you that only one of the four physical and health education criteria is about performing, which explains the sporty child on a grade 4. It tells you that in language acquisition the four criteria are the four skills, so a confident speaker can be carried by criterion C while B and D sit low.

The map also tells you where a tutor can help quickly and where they cannot. Criteria that reward a written move, such as evaluating, justifying or weighing sources, respond fast to teaching because the student usually knows the content and has never been shown the move. Criteria that reward sustained independent work, such as the design folder or the arts process journal, need habit change over a term rather than a technique taught in an hour.

The table below sets out the four criteria for each subject group. The published subject guides on the IB's own site are the authority, and your child's school issues a task-specific clarification for each unit which is more precise again. Ask for it; most schools provide it on request and some print it on the task sheet.
